yRN9bGltlW.one_liner: Fine-grained annotations unifying four sarcasm benchmarks, plus a single-tower Qwen3-VL-Embedding model with field-specific latent tokens.
yRN9bGltlW.problem: Binary multimodal sarcasm detection does not show why a sample is sarcastic, and annotation policy shifts across datasets limit cross-dataset generalization.
yRN9bGltlW.method: SarcAtlas adds annotations for strict and broad sarcasm, type, target, shared and modality-specific information, cross-modal relations, rationales and interpretation dependencies to MMSD, MMSD2.0 and the English and Chinese SarcNet splits. A single-tower Qwen3-VL-Embedding model assigns five latent-token groups to annotated fields plus a decision token, trained with multi-task prediction, text-field reconstruction, teacher-similarity distillation and label supervision.
yRN9bGltlW.key_idea: Assign latent-token groups to annotated semantic fields in one embedding tower and train them with reconstruction and similarity distillation, so detection needs no generative inference.
yRN9bGltlW.evidence: Reviewers cite 41,812 annotation records built with staged annotation, review, repair and expert audit, an analysis of differences among the benchmarks, and model experiments including a backbone comparison.
yRN9bGltlW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the new annotation layer, with its strict and broad sarcasm distinction and pragmatic fields, a useful resource that fits the model's motivation and is clearly written.
yRN9bGltlW.main_concern: About 97.6% of annotations are generated and reviewed by LLMs with only 2.4% expert audited and no agreement statistics, so scores measure agreement with LLM annotators and gains may come from the backbone.

Vooph1BfBt.one_liner: MINA-GABT predicts a gap-formation state (cue, process, gap) and then verbalizes it as the question viewers will ask.
Vooph1BfBt.problem: A proactive video agent must decide what information to prepare before a viewer asks, but many questions are plausible at a moment and the ones viewers actually ask are hard to predict.
Vooph1BfBt.method: The authors define Moment-level Information Need Anticipation (MINA), build MINA-Data from 12,510 timestamped viewer questions on 872 videos, and propose MINA-GABT, which predicts a gap-formation state (observed cue, the process evoking an information gap, and the gap) guided by a taxonomy induced from training-set viewer behavior.
Vooph1BfBt.key_idea: Predict the viewer's gap-formation state, guided by a taxonomy induced from training-set viewer behavior, before generating the question text.
Vooph1BfBt.evidence: Evaluation on MINA-Data of whether an answer to a predicted question would satisfy the observed need, with human validation, a held-out content category, and analyses of remaining uncertainty.
Vooph1BfBt.claimed_gains: MINA-GABT reaches 21.20% Hit@5 and 27.12% Hit@10, compared with 15.53% Hit@5 at best for Direct Forecasting.
Vooph1BfBt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that anticipating real viewer information needs is a compelling direction, grounded in naturally occurring questions, with a well-written paper, human validation, and detailed analyses.
Vooph1BfBt.main_concern: The practical value of the task is not shown, since evaluation assumes question timestamps are known and uses a single real question as the target although viewers' needs differ.

kEzHZvnAee.one_liner: An open dataset of 100 ms per-GPU power traces for LLM fine-tuning and inference workloads.
kEzHZvnAee.problem: Existing LLM energy benchmarks report aggregates such as joules per token and rarely release time-series measurements, leaving power dynamics poorly characterized.
kEzHZvnAee.method: Collects time-resolved per-GPU power traces at a nominal 100 ms polling interval on varying NVIDIA platforms with workload and system metadata, using controlled fine-tuning and inference sweeps. Defines power-grid-facing metrics and an AI compute power and energy scaling law.
kEzHZvnAee.key_idea: Release time-resolved per-GPU traces paired with workload metadata and controlled configuration sweeps, instead of aggregate energy numbers.
kEzHZvnAee.evidence: Fine-tuning sweeps over model families, batch size, sequence length, precision, parallelism, and checkpointing, and inference sweeps over concurrency, GPU frequency, quantization, prompt and output lengths, and arrival patterns.
kEzHZvnAee.claimed_gains: Dataset contribution only; the only figure stated is the nominal 100 ms polling interval.
kEzHZvnAee.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the dataset a useful, broad measurement resource that captures temporal power behavior hidden by aggregate energy figures.
kEzHZvnAee.main_concern: The 100 ms polling does not guarantee 100 ms resolution because GPU sensors average readings over roughly one second, and the data-center-level relevance of per-GPU traces is not established.

ljPSxZ0wVZ.one_liner: Adds kernelized moment balancing, selecting informative balancing functions from an RKHS, as a training objective for forecasting.
ljPSxZ0wVZ.problem: Existing forecasting objectives enforce moment matching for only one or two predefined balancing functions, so they do not reach full distribution balance under Imbens' criterion.
ljPSxZ0wVZ.method: KMB-DF adaptively selects the most informative balancing functions from a reproducing kernel Hilbert space and uses a tractable, piecewise differentiable formulation estimated from empirical samples for gradient-based training.
ljPSxZ0wVZ.key_idea: Enforce that forecast and ground-truth moments match for adaptively chosen RKHS balancing functions, using top-K informative anchors and a soft-margin penalty.
ljPSxZ0wVZ.evidence: Multiple models and datasets with ablations; reviewers cite ten alternative objectives on seven datasets, several history lengths, and multiple seeds.
ljPSxZ0wVZ.claimed_gains: Reports consistent forecasting-accuracy improvements across models and datasets; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
ljPSxZ0wVZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the RKHS-based remedy principled and trainable, with broad empirical gains over alternative objectives across datasets and backbones.
ljPSxZ0wVZ.main_concern: The stated soft-margin loss is inconsistent with Algorithm 1, the top-K step is not differentiable, ablations of anchor selection and an MMD baseline are missing, and the statistical guarantee is weakly justified.

LdJongzCI0.one_liner: SRE-Bench: private, expert-built binary reverse-engineering benchmark to evaluate frontier agents without training-data contamination.
LdJongzCI0.problem: Agentic reverse-engineering evaluation lacks benchmarks that are both absent from LLM training data and representative of real-world binary scale and anti-analysis protections.
LdJongzCI0.method: Reverse-engineering experts built 19 private programs averaging 16.9K lines of code from scratch (over 5,000 expert hours), then added 44 in-house anti-analysis mechanisms to yield 262 binary instances and 1,572 deterministically graded tasks.
LdJongzCI0.key_idea: Construct clean-room, never-published programs with layered anti-analysis protections and deterministic grading, so models cannot rely on memorized code and tasks match real binary scale.
LdJongzCI0.evidence: 13 agentic settings across 11 models were evaluated (eight public-facing, five internal unconstrained with cyber safeguards disabled and no budget cap), plus a contamination and scale ablation over three compression programs.
LdJongzCI0.claimed_gains: not stated; the truncated abstract reports only that realistic reverse engineering remains challenging for frontier agents.
LdJongzCI0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the substantial engineering effort, private programs, deterministic grading, reference solutions and adversarial reward-hacking audits as a stronger basis than small challenge-style reverse-engineering tasks.
LdJongzCI0.main_concern: The contamination and scale ablation (Table 5) compares three different compression programs, so it cannot isolate the effect of training-data exposure from program complexity.

NZf75JAUME.one_liner: IRPO updates a shared meta-policy so an intrinsic-reward-adapted subpolicy optimizes extrinsic reward, driving exploration without changing the objective.
NZf75JAUME.problem: Combining intrinsic with extrinsic rewards changes the performance objective and induces suboptimality, while hierarchical use of intrinsic rewards is sample inefficient and also suboptimal.
NZf75JAUME.method: IRPO derives subpolicies from a shared meta-policy using intrinsic rewards in an inner loop, then updates the meta-policy with meta-gradients so that one subpolicy optimizes the extrinsic reward only.
NZf75JAUME.key_idea: Meta-gradient through inner-loop updates driven by intrinsic rewards, with the outer loop optimizing only extrinsic reward, so intrinsic rewards guide exploration without altering the objective.
NZf75JAUME.evidence: Sparse-reward experiments with ablation studies and a proof of convergence to an epsilon-approximate first-order stationary point; reviews cite 7 baselines, 9 environments and 10 seeds.
NZf75JAUME.claimed_gains: Outperforms relevant baselines in sparse-reward environments with similar wall-clock time to standard policy gradient methods; no numeric gains are stated.
NZf75JAUME.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the inner-loop intrinsic and outer-loop extrinsic separation clear and interesting, the evaluation thorough (many baselines, seeds and ablations), and the convergence guarantee supportive.
NZf75JAUME.main_concern: Environments and baselines are limited (EIPO and harder exploration benchmarks are missing), and the method depends on pretrained ALLO intrinsic rewards that assume uniformly sampled initial states.

UtOpoFqHdi.one_liner: FAULT converts verified self-diagnoses into step-level credit anchored by terminal outcomes for agentic RL on long-horizon tasks.
UtOpoFqHdi.problem: Terminal-outcome rewards give no learning signal in same-outcome rollout groups and only trajectory-wide feedback, while natural-language diagnoses are unreliable and do not quantify how much each error should matter.
UtOpoFqHdi.method: FAULT checks diagnostic evidence, learns relative error costs from task outcomes, and turns diagnosed errors into step-level penalties; the policy and self-diagnoser co-evolve while error costs are updated online from recent outcomes.
UtOpoFqHdi.key_idea: Split credit into error localization (evidence-verified self-diagnosis) and error valuation (error costs regressed from terminal outcomes), then redistribute terminal reward to diagnosed steps.
UtOpoFqHdi.evidence: Experiments on ALFWorld against GRPO and GiGPO with credit-localization analyses; reviews also mention SearchQA and ablations on online pricing and a fixed diagnoser.
UtOpoFqHdi.claimed_gains: On ALFWorld, FAULT reaches 95% signal coverage versus 41% for GRPO and 72% for GiGPO.
UtOpoFqHdi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like separating where an error occurs from how costly it is, note that diagnostic penalties give differentiated signals in zero-reward failure groups, and find the method detailed and reproducible.
UtOpoFqHdi.main_concern: Diagnosis quality is weakly guaranteed: verification only checks that cited evidence exists in the trajectory, and the frozen error taxonomy is imperfect (off-table rate 0.31, decisive-step localization 0.48).

XwbL97Ct2Z.one_liner: SCoRE constrains an EEG classifier so spatial reflection of the signal transforms class evidence correspondingly, using learnable reflection equivariance.
XwbL97Ct2Z.problem: Cross-subject EEG decoding suffers from large inter-individual variability, and scaling up pretrained models adds complexity and inference cost while leaving the shared structure implicit in weights.
XwbL97Ct2Z.method: SCoRE trains a shared network on each input and its spatial reflection, building an equivariant classifier through joint training and parameterization that separately captures class evidence that reverses under reflection. The reflection is parameterized by conjugating an initial electrode-pairing matrix with a learnable orthogonal matrix built via the Cayley transform.
XwbL97Ct2Z.key_idea: Constrain the classifier so a spatial reflection of the EEG signal induces a corresponding transformation of class evidence, with the reflection learned as a Cayley-parameterized orthogonal transform.
XwbL97Ct2Z.evidence: Experiments on 9 evaluation datasets (including three released by the authors) against 11 baselines with statistical analysis, ablations, and beta-lateralization analyses, without pretraining.
XwbL97Ct2Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method well motivated, simple, and efficient, with strong performance from a compact model, thorough ablations, and explainability analyses that match known physiology.
XwbL97Ct2Z.main_concern: Physiological justification for reflection equivariance is thin outside left-right motor imagery, since it is extended to sleep staging, depression detection, mental arithmetic, SSVEP, and aesthetic judgment without showing it holds there.

x8xC02yO8n.one_liner: Teacher repairs all-failure GRPO groups, then hands control back once the student's independent success is verified.
x8xC02yO8n.problem: In group-relative RL, when every rollout in a group fails with the same reward, advantages collapse toward zero and the group gives no learning signal, while letting a teacher finish the task turns supervision into off-policy imitation.
x8xC02yO8n.method: A frozen teacher attempts recovery from a state the student reached, and its continuation is retained only if the environment verifies success. Control returns to the student at the earliest point where independent student success is confirmed, so successful experience is again student-generated.
x8xC02yO8n.key_idea: The teacher acts only long enough to cross what the student cannot yet handle, with the handoff point chosen by verifying that the student can finish independently.
x8xC02yO8n.evidence: Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop with a 1.5B student, mechanism ablations (Terminal Teacher, random handoff) on ALFWorld, and a reimplemented OVCSD baseline (per reviews).
x8xC02yO8n.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a review cites a 7.81-percentage-point gap over a Terminal Teacher ablation in Table 3.
x8xC02yO8n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is a clean, simple fix for the known all-failure GRPO problem, with explicit verification criteria and a coherent teacher-recovery, handoff-confirmation, and student-continuation design.
x8xC02yO8n.main_concern: It assumes a capable teacher without guidance on vetting one, mechanism ablations cover only ALFWorld with a 1.5B student, the Terminal Teacher control confounds supervision scope with handoff timing, and training overhead is not fully characterized.

3gcgGEIExx.one_liner: CLIP model inversion for data-free quantization using WordNet-sampled prompts, similarity-based soft targets, and appearance decorrelation with view consistency.
3gcgGEIExx.problem: Data-free quantization of CLIP needs semantically diverse text prompts as inversion targets, but a recent method builds them manually, covering a narrow semantic range and degrading the quantized model's generalization.
3gcgGEIExx.method: Vista samples visual prompts from the WordNet lexical hierarchy, replaces one-hot supervision with identity-preserving soft targets from pairwise prompt similarities, and decorrelates the appearance components the target prompts do not explain while enforcing view consistency to preserve semantic alignment.
3gcgGEIExx.key_idea: Broadens inversion targets via WordNet sampling and soft similarity targets, and expands visual coverage by decorrelating unexplained appearance components under view consistency.
3gcgGEIExx.evidence: Experiments across multiple CLIP architectures, bit-width configurations, and downstream zero-shot classification datasets (per reviews); the abstract's results are cut off.
3gcgGEIExx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies limitations of earlier CLIP inversion well, with WordNet-based prompt coverage and soft targets as interesting ideas and extensive evaluation showing large improvements.
3gcgGEIExx.main_concern: Reported numbers are inconsistent across sections (e.g., 56.26% in Table 2 versus 53.91% in Table 12 for ViT-B/32 W8/A8), the Table 3 baseline is unclear, and contributions over D4C are seen as limited with only CLIP zero-shot classification tested.

wPkvMGRCkW.one_liner: Self-editing loop where a unified multimodal model assesses, edits, and distills its own safety corrections into safer image generation.
wPkvMGRCkW.problem: Unified multimodal models often fail to prevent safety violations during image generation even though they can recognize those violations in their own outputs.
wPkvMGRCkW.method: SGSE has the same UMM identify how a safety violation manifests in a generated image, write an editing instruction describing a benign target scene, edit toward it, and reassess, repeating if a violation remains. Accepted correction trajectories supervise both assessment and editing, and the same corrective loop is kept at inference time.
wPkvMGRCkW.key_idea: Distill the model's own accepted assess-edit-reassess trajectories back into the model so safety understanding drives corrective editing without external safety assessments or reference images.
wPkvMGRCkW.evidence: Evaluated across diverse harmful concepts on I2P, on BAGEL and other unified multimodal models across several safety benchmarks, with a benign-content safety-utility evaluation.
wPkvMGRCkW.claimed_gains: Average attack success rate on I2P falls from 31.31% for the base model to 7.84% with at most one edit.
wPkvMGRCkW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is coherent, using one model to assess, formulate a correction, and edit without an external safety teacher or reference images, and that safety gains are broad across models and benchmarks.
wPkvMGRCkW.main_concern: Closely related iterative safety-editing work (SafeEditor, Self-Refine, UniEdit-I) is not compared under matched conditions, so SGSE's distinct contribution is not isolated, and the reliability of self-generated safety assessments is not validated.

dxNgY9vhAt.one_liner: RSM-LinUCB plans over memory states Bellman-style while learning reward parameters like linear bandits, making memory cost additive in regret.
dxNgY9vhAt.problem: In linear bandits with memory, where past actions induce endogenous nonstationarity through a known memory map, prior regret bounds couple memory length multiplicatively with the horizon.
dxNgY9vhAt.method: RSM-LinUCB learns the reward parameter with optimistic linear-bandit estimation and plans with Bellman recursion over the known memory state, switching policies rarely via a determinant-triggered rule. The algorithm is also extended to generalized linear rewards.
dxNgY9vhAt.key_idea: Treat recent action history as a known deterministic state, plan with Bellman recursion, and split regret into memory-induced error and cumulative reward-estimation error.
dxNgY9vhAt.evidence: High-probability regret upper bound, a matching minimax lower bound, a generalized-linear extension, and numerical experiments on synthetic instances and semi-synthetic KV-cache and semantic-cache tasks.
dxNgY9vhAt.claimed_gains: Regret bound of O-tilde(dRS(M+1) + sigma*d*sqrt(T)) with memory contributing only an additive cost, a matching minimax lower bound, and better performance than baselines in experiments (no numeric margins stated).
dxNgY9vhAt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the additive dependence on memory length in the regret bound is a meaningful theoretical improvement, supported by a clear Bellman-based regret decomposition and a matching lower bound.
dxNgY9vhAt.main_concern: Exact Bellman planning over the memory state space (up to n^M states) is not computationally tractable in general, and no general efficient implementation is provided.

jYU9SyjKm1.one_liner: EPIG_surv picks censored patients and follow-up depth by predictive information gain per expected cost to de-censor survival data
jYU9SyjKm1.problem: A budgeted learner can pay to extend follow-up of right-censored patients, but follow-up does not always uncensor, and standard acquisition rules ignore what the follow-up window will actually reveal.
jYU9SyjKm1.method: Casts de-censoring as budgeted active learning where the learner pays to partially label censored instances, for example by extending follow-up by one year. EPIG_surv guides patient and depth selection by predictive information gain per unit of expected cost, with an entropy-capped batch objective and marginal greedy selection.
jYU9SyjKm1.key_idea: Score each censored patient and follow-up depth by expected predictive information gain per unit cost, accounting for what the extra follow-up can reveal.
jYU9SyjKm1.evidence: Theory for marginal greedy selection on the entropy-capped surrogate under equal costs, plus experiments on three real-world datasets with 40 paired seeds and fresh-seed confirmation (per reviewers).
jYU9SyjKm1.claimed_gains: Marginal greedy selection under equal costs achieves the same (1 - 1/e) approximation factor as BatchBALD for the entropy-capped batch objective; the TLDR says the algorithm matches or beats every competing acquisition rule.
jYU9SyjKm1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practically relevant and the follow-up-aware acquisition idea sensible, with carefully run experiments (paired seeds, fresh-seed confirmation, negative results reported).
jYU9SyjKm1.main_concern: The theory says little about the method actually used (the cap rarely matters), and the gains are not isolated from the setup since most baselines ignore the follow-up window.

BsaeLhrJf9.one_liner: RocketWM recovers commands from launch footage via a physics twin and renders counterfactual videos to train action-conditioned aerospace world models
BsaeLhrJf9.problem: Public launch broadcasts show only what happened, not the commands, so video world models trained on them learn appearance and trajectory statistics but generation stays unresponsive to actions.
BsaeLhrJf9.method: Extracts flight dynamics from on-screen telemetry, initializes an aerospace physics engine with them, and renders the trajectories in a game engine whose camera is matched to the broadcast. The commands whose effect a model must learn come from the twin's rendered counterfactuals.
BsaeLhrJf9.key_idea: Invert the vehicle's equations of motion from telemetry to recover commands, then re-fly the physics twin to render counterfactual videos that supply action-conditioned training data.
BsaeLhrJf9.evidence: Launch-vehicle broadcast footage (5,061 real clips per a reviewer) evaluated with a CommandBench built around engine-ignition command following on upper-stage landing burn and booster landing tasks.
BsaeLhrJf9.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text in the batch ends before the results)
BsaeLhrJf9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a relatively novel problem and a domain-agnostic recipe that turns observation-only video into supervised action-conditioned data, with careful handling of telemetry delays, quantization, and uncertainty.
BsaeLhrJf9.main_concern: The physics twin both labels and grades the data, and the ignition-timing metric does not verify the vehicle's dynamical response, which narrows the claims; results also differ across flight tasks.

6CWo59fgfd.one_liner: FlashRocket fuses MiniRocket feature extraction into one tiled GPU pass with a ridge head, training hundreds of classifiers in seconds
6CWo59fgfd.problem: Training and testing a classification head per task takes from 15 minutes to an estimated 7.5 hours in the authors' experiments, too slow for quick adaptation, and tasks differ so much in size that small ones underuse the GPU while large ones stall the rest.
6CWo59fgfd.method: Trains and tests classifiers on MiniRocket features at archive scale as one GPU workload. It extracts features in a single fused on-chip pass, tiles long series so the longest few do not become the bottleneck, and fits a cheaper ridge classification head.
6CWo59fgfd.key_idea: Fuse feature extraction into one on-chip GPU pass, tile long series to balance heterogeneous tasks, and replace the head with cheap ridge regression, running all datasets as one workload.
6CWo59fgfd.evidence: 188 datasets across four archives (UCR, UEA, Bake Off Redux, Multiverse-core) with 279,247 training and 249,041 test series on one L40S GPU with 16 CPUs, compared with MiniRocket in tsai and MantisV2.
6CWo59fgfd.claimed_gains: Trains and tests all 188 classifiers in 3.07 seconds on one L40S GPU with 16 CPUs, 242x faster than MiniRocket in tsai at matching accuracy (83.07% against 83.10%).
6CWo59fgfd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit large training and inference speedups at preserved average accuracy, effective handling of heterogeneous workloads through tiling, and broad evaluation over 188 datasets.
6CWo59fgfd.main_concern: The sources of the speedup are not isolated (feature extraction versus ridge head), and timings cover one GPU model with few repeats and uncontrolled MiniRocket runtime variation.

QwTpaSgGaR.one_liner: cMG-DICE computes Nash equilibria of convex Markov games from logged data by combining shadow rewards with stationary distribution correction estimation
QwTpaSgGaR.problem: Computing equilibria of convex Markov games requires tracking the current state-action occupancy at every update, through fresh environment interactions or an exact transition model, which is computationally expensive.
QwTpaSgGaR.method: cMG-DICE combines the shadow reward formulation with stationary distribution correction estimation (DICE) so each agent's best response reduces to a single minimization over logged transitions. Reviewers describe it as a regularized optimization problem with opponent-aware occupancy correction.
QwTpaSgGaR.key_idea: Treat the gradient of each agent's concave utility as a shadow reward and compute regularized best responses from logged transitions through DICE occupancy correction.
QwTpaSgGaR.evidence: Tabular games and the Clean Up environment from a single dataset under diverse utilities and initial joint policies, plus a bound relating regularized-game exploitability to target-game exploitability.
QwTpaSgGaR.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports approximating equilibria under diverse utilities and initial joint policies from a single dataset, without figures)
QwTpaSgGaR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the principled formulation for offline multi-agent learning with nonlinear utilities, the analysis of regularization bias, and low-exploitability strategies in the original game.
QwTpaSgGaR.main_concern: Convergence guarantees cover only a limited utility family (near-potential games), and the exploitability bound does not show that cMG-DICE reaches a policy with small regularized exploitability.

RqDPMISi6P.one_liner: Fine-tunes a VLA on expert data mixed with filtered self-generated rollouts from the zero-shot model to retain prior skills.
RqDPMISi6P.problem: Fine-tuning a VLA such as pi0.5 on in-domain expert data from a new robot improves the expert task but loses the original instruction following and behavioral priors.
RqDPMISi6P.method: Generates online interaction rollouts from the zero-shot VLA on the target robot and uses them as additional fine-tuning data alongside expert demonstrations, so pretrained tasks are distilled without expert demos for them.
RqDPMISi6P.key_idea: Co-train on the zero-shot VLA's own rollouts, a form of generative replay, so fine-tuning stays anchored to the pretrained behavior distribution.
RqDPMISi6P.evidence: A real ALOHA robot test set and a new RoboTwin simulation benchmark, with ablations and generalization tests.
RqDPMISi6P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clear with many ablations, and see co-training on the model's own rollouts as a practical way to preserve pretrained capabilities and improve over expert-only fine-tuning.
RqDPMISi6P.main_concern: The method needs manual selection of task prompts and filtering of rollouts, with unclear human effort and base-policy capability required, and limited methodological novelty over replay and distillation.

IPyHCIaQMw.one_liner: Verifier-guided backtracking over a generator's denoising and renoising transitions whose stationary distribution equals the reward-tilted target despite verifier error.
IPyHCIaQMw.problem: Imperfect intermediate verifiers distort sampling in verifier-guided inference-time scaling for continuous generative models, and repeated refinement alone does not recover the desired reward-tilted distribution.
IPyHCIaQMw.method: CS-VGB uses a pretrained generator's denoising and renoising transitions for value-guided, bidirectional exploration across checkpoints; with correctly paired transitions the stationary distribution at the clean checkpoint equals the reward-tilted target.
IPyHCIaQMw.key_idea: Bidirectional denoise-renoise moves with correctly paired transitions form a Markov chain whose clean-checkpoint stationary distribution is the reward-tilted target regardless of verifier accuracy.
IPyHCIaQMw.evidence: Theory on exponential convergence and expected updates growing linearly in the number of checkpoints, analytically tractable settings, and prompt-guided ImageNet and CelebA facial-attribute generation (abstract truncated).
IPyHCIaQMw.claimed_gains: Expected updates to reach a clean sample grow only linearly with the number of checkpoints, and it recovers the target where compared verifier-based methods fail; no numeric gains are visible in the abstract.
IPyHCIaQMw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a fresh theoretical framework with distribution-preservation and convergence results that hold despite verifier error, and strong results over competing approaches at comparable NFE.
IPyHCIaQMw.main_concern: There is a theory-practice gap: the practical search omits correction factors and uses heuristics outside the guarantees, related-work comparisons are missing, and NFE comparisons may not reflect wall-clock cost.

qWVMAhns15.one_liner: Extracts a linear confidence direction from verbalized confidence and steers backtracking and answer proposals in reasoning models.
qWVMAhns15.problem: Reasoning models make many answer proposals and backtrack even after reaching the correct answer, and it is unclear whether an internal uncertainty signal drives that behavior.
qWVMAhns15.method: They extract a linear latent-confidence direction by querying verbalized confidence after answer proposals, then test whether steering along it changes the next-token probability of backtracking, mid-trace response length and the number of answer proposals.
qWVMAhns15.key_idea: Fit a linear direction separating high from low verbalized confidence at answer proposals, then add it to activations to steer backtracking.
qWVMAhns15.evidence: Three 32B models and five benchmarks, with steering at proposal markers, continuation experiments, position and prompt controls, and a comparison against a direction extracted directly from backtracking examples.
qWVMAhns15.claimed_gains: About 87% of rollouts contain one unique answer yet make about 8 answer proposals on average; steering changes response length by about -1.3k to +2.5k tokens and answer proposals by -4.18 to +4.75.
qWVMAhns15.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question important, the steering interventions and controls careful, and the evidence across three models and five benchmarks supportive of confidence influencing backtracking.
qWVMAhns15.main_concern: The evidence is interventional rather than observational: stated confidence barely correlates with backtracking probability, and the direction may encode confounds such as problem difficulty or trace position.

NM7KnMSNsn.one_liner: Partial-weight LoRA alternative training shard-aligned weight suffixes to remove adapter communication in tensor-parallel multi-adapter serving.
NM7KnMSNsn.problem: Serving many LoRA adapters incurs overhead from two sequential GPU-unfriendly matrix multiplications and extra inter-GPU communication under tensor parallelism.
NM7KnMSNsn.method: TESSA trains only shard-aligned suffixes of pretrained weight matrices and stores their deltas as adapters, reducing each adapter computation to one product and eliminating adapter-specific communication; reviewers add that it is paired with a workload-aware dispatcher in vLLM.
NM7KnMSNsn.key_idea: Restrict each adapter to a shard-aligned suffix slice of the weight matrix, so the update is one matrix product that stays local to each tensor-parallel shard.
NM7KnMSNsn.evidence: Per the reviews, throughput and latency are compared with S-LoRA and BD-LoRA across TP1 to TP8 on dense and MoE models with fixed-length sweeps and production-trace replay, plus adaptation-quality comparisons.
NM7KnMSNsn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree multi-adapter serving overhead is a real systems problem, the co-design of adapter structure and tensor-parallel execution is well motivated, and the evaluation is broad.
NM7KnMSNsn.main_concern: Limited novelty: TESSA is a special case of existing partial-weight methods such as PaCA and S²FT, and it is not compared with them on serving.

iI0qxi1dvN.one_liner: Structured LLM pruning that deletes coordinates in the WUS-optimal basis, implemented with blockwise polar factors.
iI0qxi1dvN.problem: Structured pruning removes dimensions in a fixed basis, and it is unclear how to choose a transformation that makes coordinate deletion preserve the original computation.
iI0qxi1dvN.method: Derives the optimal invertible transform (WUS) for a local linear reconstruction objective, whose deletion error decomposes into coordinate-wise terms set by a singular-value spectrum, then builds a practical pruner from blockwise polar factors of WUS with coordinate importance recomputed in the resulting orthogonal bases.
iI0qxi1dvN.key_idea: Rotate each layer into the WUS basis, which minimizes deletion error under positive-definite second moments, then truncate coordinates by their singular-value contribution.
iI0qxi1dvN.evidence: Llama and Qwen models from 8B to 72B parameters, evaluated on six knowledge and commonsense benchmarks and on PTB and C4 perplexity.
iI0qxi1dvN.claimed_gains: Higher average accuracy than baselines across six knowledge and commonsense benchmarks and lower perplexity on PTB and C4, with no specific numbers stated in the abstract.
iI0qxi1dvN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the clear problem formulation, a precise local analysis with an optimality proof, and strong gains at meaningful model scales.
iI0qxi1dvN.main_concern: The contribution beyond activation-aware SVD is not isolated by component ablations, and baselines are limited and compared at a single pruning ratio.

WHPydZqOYT.one_liner: 4B reasoning model trained on 15,251 RummaGEO-derived samples to predict kinase, transcription-factor and process cascades between biological conditions.
WHPydZqOYT.problem: Transcriptomic foundation models work on individual cells, and general LLMs miss the regulatory pathways and molecular cascades behind study-level transcriptomic signatures.
WHPydZqOYT.method: Formulates a task where an LLM, given a disease context and two conditions, predicts the intermediate mechanistic cascades; builds a benchmark and training set from curated RummaGEO contrasts with cascades derived from differential-expression enrichment, and trains TRACE, a 4B model based on Qwen3.5, with rubric-based LLM-judge evaluation.
WHPydZqOYT.key_idea: Supervise a reasoning LLM with multi-scale kinase, transcription-factor and process cascades derived from each study's own differential-expression enrichment.
WHPydZqOYT.evidence: Held-out evaluation on unseen series and diseases using rubric-based judging of reasoning traces, final mechanistic summaries and recovery of top enriched regulatory entities, plus case studies (abstract is cut off).
WHPydZqOYT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see an important, checkable task with a large dataset that supports both training and evaluation, and training that is effective on held-out studies and diseases.
WHPydZqOYT.main_concern: Evaluation depends on a rubric LLM judge (also the teacher for training traces) and on enrichment lists that do not guarantee correctness, and there are no prior-only baselines to separate study-specific gain.

MzAFJEMFfg.one_liner: Hierarchical anisometric positional encoding for neural vehicle routing, combining distance-indexed circular in-route and depot-anchored angular cross-route components.
MzAFJEMFfg.problem: Transformer-based neural VRP solvers use NLP-style positional encodings that ignore routing structure: anisometric node distances, cyclic direction-aware topology and depot-anchored multi-route structure.
MzAFJEMFfg.method: Formalizes three structural properties a routing-aware positional encoding should respect, compares encodings from NLP, graph-transformer and routing-specific families, and proposes an encoding that pairs a distance-indexed, circularly consistent in-route component with a depot-anchored angular cross-route component.
MzAFJEMFfg.key_idea: Ground positions in route geometry: encode cumulative distance circularly within a route and depot-relative angle across routes, instead of node index.
MzAFJEMFfg.evidence: Controlled retraining of 13 encodings under a fixed DACT backbone, deployment into the NDS backbone, several VRP variants and distribution shifts, paired per-instance tests, and CVRPLIB X instances.
MzAFJEMFfg.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says geometry-grounded encodings consistently outperform index-based alternatives across problem variants, architectures and distribution shifts, without numbers.
MzAFJEMFfg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the systematic, controlled evaluation of positional encodings, the taxonomy of structural properties with probing, and transfer of the encoding to a stronger backbone.
MzAFJEMFfg.main_concern: Gains over the strong NDS baseline are small, and the evaluation omits inference runtimes and optimality-gap benchmarks such as XML100.

shkTJ66cvj.one_liner: Event-native foundation model pretrained only on a synthetic structural simulator for zero-shot next-mark and time forecasting.
shkTJ66cvj.problem: Event streams lack a shared grid, a fixed output space and large interoperable corpora, so train-once zero-shot foundation models for marked temporal point processes are underdeveloped.
shkTJ66cvj.method: EventFM normalizes time within each history, builds one candidate query per observed mark, and jointly predicts the next mark and its conditional occurrence time. It is pretrained on-the-fly on EventSS, a simulator of trigger-response relations, overlapping workflows, delayed and cancellable consequences, recurrence and non-additive interactions.
shkTJ66cvj.key_idea: Pretrain a mark-agnostic forecaster on an on-the-fly synthetic prior of event relations so one frozen model forecasts unseen sequences from their own history.
shkTJ66cvj.evidence: Strict sequence-level zero-shot evaluation on five real-world benchmarks and structured settings, with architecture, simulator and sensitivity ablations.
shkTJ66cvj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree synthetic-only pretraining with frozen-model evaluation gives meaningful transfer evidence, and the paper is clearly presented with useful architecture and simulator ablations.
shkTJ66cvj.main_concern: Transfer relies on hand-chosen simulator assumptions (graph families, rules, delay distributions) and there is no simpler model trained on the same synthetic data, so real-data failure modes and the source of gains stay unclear.

RUKq63oIpw.one_liner: Trains GNNs for approximate k-coloring with an absolute-value InfoNCE loss whose optima are line-collapsed, edge-orthogonal color prototypes.
RUKq63oIpw.problem: Unsupervised GNN coloring methods optimize each instance directly and do not amortize optimization across test graphs.
RUKq63oIpw.method: A contrastive framework aligns same-color node embeddings up to sign and pushes adjacent nodes toward orthogonal directions. It proves optima collapse each color class onto a line with orthogonal lines for adjacent vertices, proves global convergence of projected subgradient descent in a Gram parameterization, and derives Lovasz-theta colorability certificates.
RUKq63oIpw.key_idea: Use an absolute-value InfoNCE loss so same-color embeddings align up to sign while adjacent nodes become orthogonal, giving a decodable coloring geometry.
RUKq63oIpw.evidence: Theoretical characterization of optima and convergence under conditions, plus experiments on size and out-of-distribution generalization (details are cut off in the abstract).
RUKq63oIpw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the precise geometric analysis of what the contrastive loss enforces and the links between excess loss, representation geometry and decoding certificates.
RUKq63oIpw.main_concern: Experiments do not establish practical quality and cost advantages (a low-conflict success criterion, no repaired palette size or runtime), do not measure the predicted geometry, and have unclear separation of model selection from final evaluation.

TwhnvDkXKN.one_liner: Muon variant that updates a randomly sampled subset of layers per step, with convergence guarantees under layer-wise smoothness.
TwhnvDkXKN.problem: Optimizers such as Muon update all layers at every step, which the authors argue is suboptimal in theory and in practice.
TwhnvDkXKN.method: Drop-Muon is a non-Euclidean randomized progressive training method that updates only a subset of layers per step on a randomized schedule, combining progressive training with layer-specific non-Euclidean updates. It proves convergence under layer-wise smoothness and layer-wise (L0, L1)-smoothness for deterministic and stochastic gradients.
TwhnvDkXKN.key_idea: Sample which layers receive a non-Euclidean (LMO-based) Muon update at each step, with layer smoothness constants determining when partial updates are compute-optimal.
TwhnvDkXKN.evidence: Convergence theory and a cost analysis, plus experiments on NanoGPT and small controlled CNN studies compared with full-network Muon.
TwhnvDkXKN.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms full-network Muon, reaching the same accuracy up to 1.4x faster in wall-clock time.
TwhnvDkXKN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the technically meaningful extension of randomized progressive training to non-Euclidean stochastic generalized-smooth settings and a simple method whose profiling shows lower backward, communication and optimizer costs.
TwhnvDkXKN.main_concern: The experiments mix metrics and lack downstream tasks and repetition, and the theory relies on a layer-independence assumption and a cost model that the heuristic sampling used in practice only partly follows.

atUcqgANfG.one_liner: Amortized neural sampler for power distributions of a fixed PGM, trained with reverse KL and a beta curriculum, for MPE.
atUcqgANfG.problem: Repeated MPE inference on a fixed probabilistic graphical model with changing evidence is costly, and existing neural MPE predictors give one-shot predictions without sampling.
atUcqgANfG.method: Learns a factor-reading neural sampler of P_beta(q|e) proportional to P(q|e)^beta, amortized over evidence and trained with reverse KL and a curriculum that raises beta, with no labeled MPE solutions or normalizing constants. At inference it draws samples, returns the best-scoring assignment, and can refine per query with the same objective.
atUcqgANfG.key_idea: Sampling from a power-tempered posterior whose beta is raised during training concentrates the proposal on MPE modes, so best-of-samples replaces one-shot prediction.
atUcqgANfG.evidence: Nine PGMs for comparison with neural MPE baselines and six benchmark PGMs against branch-and-bound solvers under matched wall-clock budgets.
atUcqgANfG.claimed_gains: A single sample per query achieves higher mean solution quality than the evaluated neural MPE baselines across nine PGMs, and with query-specific refinement it outperforms the evaluated branch-and-bound solvers on six benchmark PGMs under matched wall-clock budgets.
atUcqgANfG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the amortized repeated-query setting is well motivated and the solution-quality gains over neural MPE baselines are large and broad.
atUcqgANfG.main_concern: Novelty is unclear against prior annealed reverse-KL and autoregressive samplers for Boltzmann distributions, and the distributional evaluation and presentation need clarification.

RvCkW44eOm.one_liner: Post-hoc correction model that takes a vector of multiple LLM-sampled responses to debias synthetic respondents against human labels.
RvCkW44eOm.problem: LLM-simulated respondents misalign with human responses through model-side bias and latent-context omission, and single-response or mean summaries discard distributional variation.
RvCkW44eOm.method: Keeps the LLMs frozen and learns an external correction from human-labeled data whose input is the vector of responses across samples (fixed model sources for individual prediction, sampled personas for population-mean prediction). Under squared loss the vector weakly reduces Bayes-optimal risk relative to either scalar summary.
RvCkW44eOm.key_idea: Feed the correction model the full vector of multiple LLM responses rather than a single response or their mean, preserving variation and source identity.
RvCkW44eOm.evidence: Three benchmarks spanning diverse domains, with checks on respondent-ranking preservation and revenue prediction, plus a Bayes-risk argument under squared loss.
RvCkW44eOm.claimed_gains: Reduces MAE relative to uncorrected LLM predictions by up to 47% at the population level and 54% at the individual level, and attains the best mean in every main comparison.
RvCkW44eOm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find preserving the variation across multiple synthetic responses interesting, with matched comparisons showing the vector input beats single-response and mean inputs and a lightweight method that leaves the LLMs frozen.
RvCkW44eOm.main_concern: The method is inflexible (fixed number K of input responses) and seen as standard supervised calibration with limited novelty, and some evaluations (such as averaging unordered answer codes) weaken the evidence.

vF3ezwki18.one_liner: Learns jump-diffusion dynamics from trajectories, then discovers neural Lie symmetry generators satisfying continuous and finite-jump invariance conditions.
vF3ezwki18.problem: Symmetry discovery for diffusion SDEs does not cover jumps, because invariance of the continuous dynamics alone does not guarantee invariance under the discrete jump mechanism.
vF3ezwki18.method: Building on Nass's point-symmetry theory, it first fits the jump-diffusion dynamics and then trains neural symmetry generators that enforce continuous and finite-jump invariance conditions. It applies them to out-of-distribution generalization, Generator Matching-based generative editing, and volatility estimation.
vF3ezwki18.key_idea: Add a finite-jump compatibility constraint to learned Lie-symmetry generators so transformations preserve both the continuous drift and diffusion and the jump map.
vF3ezwki18.evidence: Studies of symmetry recovery from data and three applications: out-of-distribution generalization, structure discovery in jump-based generative models via Generator Matching, and symmetry-aware volatility estimation for financial time series.
vF3ezwki18.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find jump-diffusion symmetry discovery an interesting, under-researched topic with a mathematically coherent method and a notable price-rescale experiment.
vF3ezwki18.main_concern: It is not shown that the learned editing directions are genuine symmetries of the generative process (no quantitative test, identifiability unaddressed), and novelty over prior diffusion symmetry work is modest.

0eBadBSvg5.one_liner: Cross-hospital rare-disease diagnosis by sending distilled latent KV blocks or hidden-state sequences instead of clinical text to a host agent.
0eBadBSvg5.problem: No single hospital sees enough cases of a rare disease, privacy rules block sharing clinical text, and raw latent states such as hidden states or KV caches can still reveal prompt-derived content.
0eBadBSvg5.method: Hospital agents keep records local and send compact latent representations to a host agent: LatentDx-H transmits distilled KV blocks in the same-backbone setting, and LatentDx-X transmits compact hidden-state sequences projected into host input embeddings across model families.
0eBadBSvg5.key_idea: Transmit trained, compressed latent KV blocks (or projected hidden-state sequences) rather than text or raw KV caches, so evidence transfers with less reconstructable clinical content.
0eBadBSvg5.evidence: CrossRare-Bench, a self-built rare-disease benchmark with hospital-level partitions, tested in same-backbone and cross-family settings across multiple LLM backbones, non-IID partitions and privacy attacks.
0eBadBSvg5.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports strong cross-hospital diagnostic performance and reduced reconstructable clinical content relative to raw-latent baselines.
0eBadBSvg5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is worth studying and that the method, tested across backbones, partitions and privacy attacks, keeps most of the accuracy of sharing records while leaking less than raw latents.
0eBadBSvg5.main_concern: The main comparison is uneven (a supervised method against mostly training-free baselines, with supervised controls in the appendix) and the privacy claims exceed the attacks tested.

NzRJ3C97oF.one_liner: Controlled study separating PRM discrimination from decision thresholds, via frozen-score audits and class-weight interventions on PRM800K training.
NzRJ3C97oF.problem: When a process reward model misjudges steps, it is unclear whether its scores lack information about errors or its decision boundary is simply misplaced.
NzRJ3C97oF.method: Audits frozen scores of released PRMs on ProcessBench, PRMBench and MedPRMBench, and trains on 6,144 PRM800K chains with interventions that change either the clean-chain mixture or, on byte-identical inputs, only the class weights in the loss.
NzRJ3C97oF.key_idea: Holding inputs fixed and varying only the loss class weights shifts the logit origin (operating point) without changing the ranking, isolating threshold misplacement from missing information.
NzRJ3C97oF.evidence: Seven released PRMs on three benchmarks, 12 paired Qwen3.5-4B training runs, and transfer of a source-selected operating point to related benchmarks.
NzRJ3C97oF.claimed_gains: ReasonFlux-PRM and Qwen-Math reach nearly equal best shared-threshold ProcessBench Macro-F1 (73.36 vs. 73.50) yet differ by 28.35 points at the zero-margin boundary, and loss-only interventions shift the operating point as predicted (slope 0.987, R^2=0.953) and shrink the best-to-fixed gap in all 12 paired runs.
NzRJ3C97oF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating discrimination from thresholding is a useful perspective and that the controlled class-weight intervention is the strongest component.
NzRJ3C97oF.main_concern: The 'fails to decide' conclusion for released PRMs rests on a zero-margin reference not shown to be their intended rule, and the controlled finding comes mainly from one model family and overlaps prior work on threshold sensitivity and logit adjustment.

Nvx30Ezu0c.one_liner: Proves sliding-window transformers without positional encoding are Turing complete by simulating a window-histogram HIST model.
Nvx30Ezu0c.problem: Prior Turing-completeness results for chain-of-thought transformers rely on positional encodings, which are widely assumed necessary to break permutation symmetry.
Nvx30Ezu0c.method: Introduces the HIST autoregressive model, whose update depends on a constant-size state and the token-count histogram of the current window, and proves it Turing complete by showing the window's evolution reveals the token that just left it (simulating Post machines). It then constructs a constant-alphabet sliding-window transformer without positional encoding that simulates HIST.
Nvx30Ezu0c.key_idea: The sliding window itself mildly breaks permutation symmetry, because window evolution exposes the token that just left, which suffices for universal computation.
Nvx30Ezu0c.evidence: Purely theoretical proofs; reviewers note there are no experiments.
Nvx30Ezu0c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical question is clear and interesting, the HIST abstraction is useful, and the proofs appear valid and careful about scope.
Nvx30Ezu0c.main_concern: The result assumes an adaptive-size sliding window unlike the fixed windows used in practice, and there are no experiments connecting it to real transformers.

MZpRMPrQTS.one_liner: Reconstructs local training tasks from web-dev teacher trajectories, anchored on retained file states and successful builds, to supervise coding agents.
MZpRMPrQTS.problem: Complete teacher trajectories for end-to-end web development leave local objectives and action boundaries unlabeled, and repeated file revisions leave multiple candidate endpoints.
MZpRMPrQTS.method: ArtifactReplay groups file histories contributing to shared functionality retained in the delivered project, and BuildReplay extracts edit phases ending in successful builds. For each unit it recovers the repository prestate, synthesizes a local query from recorded target evidence, and uses endpoint-supported teacher actions as supervision, mixed with complete trajectories.
MZpRMPrQTS.key_idea: Use retained file states and successful builds as observable endpoints to cut teacher trajectories into replayable local tasks with recovered repository prestates.
MZpRMPrQTS.evidence: Web and Game sets of ArtifactsBench and Cookie-Bench with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base and Qwen3.6-27B, plus step-matched and intermediate-replay controls.
MZpRMPrQTS.claimed_gains: Improves Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base to an average score of 47.29, surpassing its official post-trained counterpart by 17.2%, and raises Qwen3.6-27B from 40.73 to 62.22.
MZpRMPrQTS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that anchoring data construction on observable terminal states is a practical, carefully specified design, and the gains over base and post-trained models are substantial.
MZpRMPrQTS.main_concern: The gain is not cleanly separated from extra training exposure (Finale processes more tokens than the full-trajectory baseline, and Table 1 has no full-trajectory SFT baseline), and the synthesized local query may leak the solution.

oT6ePufDzy.one_liner: Tests 22 LLMs on predicting individuals' strategies, success and metacognition in 3,725 experience-sampled self-control conflicts.
oT6ePufDzy.problem: LLM evaluations score outcomes such as keyed answers, group-level rates and questionnaire scores, leaving open whether a model reproduces how a specific person handles a specific episode.
oT6ePufDzy.method: Prompts 22 LLMs in English and German with increasingly detailed person descriptions and scores each predicted step (strategy selection, success appraisal, metacognition) against the participants' own reports and reference predictors such as frequency baselines.
oT6ePufDzy.key_idea: Score each step of a person's self-control process against that person's own episode-level reports, separating between-person from within-person accuracy.
oT6ePufDzy.evidence: 3,725 experience-sampled conflicts from 468 participants, 22 LLMs, four levels of person information, frequency-matched baselines and a small human comparison.
oT6ePufDzy.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports that models recover reported strategies less well than a rule listing the most frequent strategies, and that person information changes tracking of a person's episodes only slightly.
oT6ePufDzy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the real experience-sampling data and the separation of between-person and within-person accuracy, which shows persona information improves predictions of typical success but little for individual episodes.
oT6ePufDzy.main_concern: Reading prediction failures against self-reports as failures to model psychological processes goes beyond the evidence, and baselines fitted on the target population make the comparison uneven.

c0werLyrPo.one_liner: Modified Multiplicative Weights Updates on a simplex-constrained NMF provably converge to second-order stationary points.
c0werLyrPo.problem: No guarantees exist that NMF algorithms avoid suboptimal saddle points, and standard saddle-escape theory fails because NMF's domain is non-compact and its loss is non-Lipschitz.
c0werLyrPo.method: Adds one simplex constraint to the NMF problem and shows this preserves second-order stationary points (SOSPs) and their quality, then shows a natural modification of MWU converges asymptotically to exact SOSPs with probability 1 from random simplex initialization, with non-asymptotic rates to approximate SOSPs.
c0werLyrPo.key_idea: Constraining NMF factors to a simplex makes the landscape tractable while preserving SOSPs, so a modified MWU avoids saddles almost surely.
c0werLyrPo.evidence: Theoretical proofs of asymptotic and non-asymptotic convergence, illustrated with a 1D example according to reviewers.
c0werLyrPo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well written and pedagogical, and that it addresses a relevant open problem with a useful analysis.
c0werLyrPo.main_concern: One reviewer finds a mismatch between the SOSP notion proved and the one covered by the cited SNAP and MWU guarantees, and another questions the unexplained normalization choice.

GWckMHvvgo.one_liner: Training-free MoE activation calibration that floors Absmax quantization steps using expert range variation under added unrelated prefixes.
GWckMHvvgo.problem: Each MoE expert is calibrated only on tokens routed to it, so Absmax calibration can set overly fine steps with no range headroom, and clipping errors accumulate over long generations.
GWckMHvvgo.method: Measures how each expert's routed activation range changes when unrelated prefixes are added to the calibration texts and uses that variation as a one-sided floor on the Absmax step. Steps stay fixed, so inference costs the same as static Absmax.
GWckMHvvgo.key_idea: Set each expert's static quantization step no smaller than a floor derived from its context-induced activation-range variation.
GWckMHvvgo.evidence: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B under FP16, AWQ, GPTQ and SmoothQuant weight configurations, with HumanEval, MBPP+ and LiveCodeBench plus a calibration-data-matched control.
GWckMHvvgo.claimed_gains: Improves the average downstream score over Absmax in every weight configuration and, with INT8 expert activations, raises HumanEval pass@1 from 24.4% to 68.9%, staying on par with the unquantized model on HumanEval, MBPP+ and LiveCodeBench.
GWckMHvvgo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a simple, training-free method with fixed inference-time scales that improves average downstream performance on two MoE architectures across several weight configurations.
GWckMHvvgo.main_concern: Gains are concentrated in a few tasks (mainly HumanEval) and are not cleanly separated from broader calibration coverage, since Absmax is not run on the same prefixed inputs, and real low-precision efficiency is not measured.

YMW2yV59lg.one_liner: Looped block-diffusion drafter reuses one backbone twice, regenerating the suffix conditioned on a selected prefix to improve speculative decoding.
YMW2yV59lg.problem: Block-diffusion drafters predict each position's marginal without seeing earlier drafted tokens, causing a repetition trap of redundant neighboring tokens and shorter accepted drafts.
YMW2yV59lg.method: D-Loop's first pass proposes a block, and a second pass of the same backbone conditions on a selected prefix to regenerate the suffix in parallel. A prefix-suffix objective trains the shared drafter for both anchor-only prefix prediction and prefix-conditioned suffix prediction.
YMW2yV59lg.key_idea: Add intra-block causal conditioning by looping the diffusion drafter's own backbone over a selected prefix, with no added parameters.
YMW2yV59lg.evidence: Eight math, code and chat benchmarks on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B targets against DFlash and DSpark, with greedy and sampling decoding.
YMW2yV59lg.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says D-Loop can beat DFlash and DSpark on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with obvious gains.
YMW2yV59lg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the simple, parameter-free reuse of the drafter and the repetition-trap motivation, with acceptance length improving across two model scales and task domains.
YMW2yV59lg.main_concern: Gain attribution and deployment cost are unclear: the second pass more than doubles drafting time, so speedup over DSpark is small, only batch size 1 is evaluated, and component contributions are not disentangled.

zE097Mp2VZ.one_liner: Shared-threshold rounding and chain-traversal exploration give regret bounds for online submodular minimization with Hamming switching costs.
zE097Mp2VZ.problem: Online submodular minimization lacks regret characterizations when the learner pays a cost for changing its chosen set between rounds.
zE097Mp2VZ.method: Algorithms use shared-threshold rounding to control movement, and bandit feedback uses a chain-traversal exploration scheme. High-probability bounds come from a pathwise bound on realized regret that isolates a monitorable cumulative movement and triggers a switching-budget restarting wrapper.
zE097Mp2VZ.key_idea: Round a shared threshold on the Lovasz extension so successive sets stay close in Hamming distance, and restart when a monitorable cumulative-movement quantity exceeds a budget.
zE097Mp2VZ.evidence: Theoretical upper bounds with matching lower bounds (full-information minimax; bandit matching up to logarithmic factors when lambda is at least M); no experiments are mentioned.
zE097Mp2VZ.claimed_gains: Full-information minimax expected regret is Theta(M min{T, sqrt((1+lambda/M) n T)}), and bandit regret is O(M min{T, n (1+lambda/M)^(1/3) T^(2/3)}), matching the lower bound up to logarithmic factors when lambda >= M.
zE097Mp2VZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a clear characterization of regret in dimension, horizon, loss scale and switching weight, with matching or near-matching bounds and a useful bandit exploration design.
zE097Mp2VZ.main_concern: The bandit characterization is incomplete in the small-switching-cost regime, and parts of the analysis adapt existing subgradient and restart arguments.

DX9dhk8rzq.one_liner: Splits a transformer into task-tuned prefill and frozen shared decode modules so multiple LLMs share decode workers.
DX9dhk8rzq.problem: Multi-LLM serving cannot batch decoding across models, so memory-bound decode workers are underutilized, especially under skewed workloads.
DX9dhk8rzq.method: Decomposes a decoder-only Transformer into a prefill module and a decode module, fine-tunes only the task-specific prefill module so a frozen decode module is shared across task variants of one backbone, and uses a model-agnostic decode routing policy to balance requests across shared workers.
DX9dhk8rzq.key_idea: Fine-tune only the prefill module so its KV caches stay compatible with one frozen decoder, enabling cross-model decode batching.
DX9dhk8rzq.evidence: Diverse tasks and model families, plus single-node and eight-model multi-node serving compared with conventional disaggregation, popularity-aware allocation and GPU sharing (MPS).
DX9dhk8rzq.claimed_gains: Improves throughput per decode GPU by up to 2.0x over conventional disaggregation with TPOT degradation within 10%, and in eight-model serving matches baseline throughput with 25% fewer GPUs at moderate load and raises throughput by 15.5% on the same hardware at higher load.
DX9dhk8rzq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of task-specific prefill models producing KV caches compatible with a shared frozen decoder interesting, with evaluation across tasks, load distributions and single- and multi-node setups.
DX9dhk8rzq.main_concern: Applicability is narrow (all models must be same-origin variants sharing weights and KV layout and be retrained with SUN), and closest alternatives such as MuxServe and DeltaZip, and the MPS baseline, are not adequately evaluated.

S4PQ7ZaCpZ.one_liner: GPU-resident latent flow-matching model that generates sparse-plus-low-rank approximations of sparse matrix operators like inverse and inverse square root.
S4PQ7ZaCpZ.problem: Classical methods for applying operators f(A) of sparse matrices map poorly to GPUs, and existing learned approaches are mostly limited to inverses and need CPU-side refinement.
S4PQ7ZaCpZ.method: Encodes the sparse matrix A into a dimension-agnostic conditioning representation, samples latent operator variables by flow matching at a cost independent of matrix size, and decodes a sparse local component over candidate edges from A's sparsity pattern plus a low-rank global component.
S4PQ7ZaCpZ.key_idea: Generate operator approximations as sparse-plus-low-rank factors from a size-independent latent flow-matching sampler conditioned on a dimension-agnostic encoding of A.
S4PQ7ZaCpZ.evidence: Experiments training on smaller matrices and applying to larger ones, compared with exact CPU and GPU solvers and learning-based baselines (abstract is cut off).
S4PQ7ZaCpZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the goal of GPU-only, size-generalizable operator learning and the sparse-plus-low-rank representation, with train-small, apply-large experiments.
S4PQ7ZaCpZ.main_concern: Novelty over prior graph-conditioned generative preconditioner work and the fairness of timing comparisons against exact solvers are questioned, and clarity of the method is lacking.

oPUbH8HOri.one_liner: Conformal calibration with reflected Fenchel-Young scores yields decision-aware uncertainty sets for contextual robust optimization.
oPUbH8HOri.problem: Residual-based conformal sets are conservative because they react to prediction errors that do not affect the optimal decision, while calibrating the nominal regret directly makes robust optimization return the nominal decision unchanged.
oPUbH8HOri.method: Uses reflected Fenchel-Young conformal scores for convex optimization with linear objective uncertainty; the score decomposes into nominal regret, hindsight-optimizer suboptimality and a reflected stability gap. Split conformal calibration gives finite-sample marginal guarantees, and a master-pricing algorithm gives optimality certificates.
oPUbH8HOri.key_idea: Replace exact-regret calibration with a reflected Fenchel-Young gap score whose three-term decomposition lets robust optimization move away from the nominal decision.
oPUbH8HOri.evidence: Theory (a self-centering result, finite-sample coverage, conditions for improved worst-case regret) and experiments on portfolio and real-data solar-grid allocation problems against residual-based robust baselines.
oPUbH8HOri.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says reflected FY refinement improves decision quality over residual-based robust baselines in portfolio and solar-grid allocation problems.
oPUbH8HOri.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper combines convex analysis with conformal prediction well, with a useful self-centering characterization and a decomposition that explains when decision refinement is possible.
oPUbH8HOri.main_concern: The design of the reflected FY score and the motivation for changing the nominal decision are insufficiently justified, the sources of conservatism are not examined, and the notation is heavy.

apxKBAp9IS.one_liner: Cache-aware Conformer RNN-T streams InterMo notation tokens from live piano and violin audio into incrementally rendered sheet music.
apxKBAp9IS.problem: Prior online music transcription stops at MIDI events or beat positions, so no system converts live audio directly into human-readable notation.
apxKBAp9IS.method: A cache-aware Conformer-RNN-T emits playback-ordered Intervals-and-Moments (InterMo) tokens as solo piano, solo violin and violin-piano duet performances unfold, with an incremental sheet-music renderer and a conductor buffer that adds a short startup delay.
apxKBAp9IS.key_idea: Emit a playback-ordered metrical notation token sequence with a streaming RNN-T, and buffer a short startup delay with a conductor buffer to improve quality.
apxKBAp9IS.evidence: Streaming benchmarks across latency configurations from 0.16 to 2.24 seconds against offline audio-to-MIDI-to-score cascades on several real-performance datasets, with conductor-buffer and lookahead ablations.
apxKBAp9IS.claimed_gains: Performs competitively with offline audio-to-MIDI-to-score cascades across latency configurations between 0.16 and 2.24 seconds, and a startup delay of only 5 seconds improves streaming quality, especially in piano music.
apxKBAp9IS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it introduces the first streaming audio-to-score setting with an appropriate RNN-T architecture, a simple effective conductor buffer, and informative ablations.
apxKBAp9IS.main_concern: The evaluation is limited: absolute OMR-NED errors are high, only theoretical latency is reported, and qualitative score examples and a streaming baseline are missing.

XhaJ9V3HhQ.one_liner: Speech token watermark whose embedding and detection functions use a graph-Laplacian basis of codec retokenization substitutions.
XhaJ9V3HhQ.problem: Neural codec resynthesis (retokenization) changes many generated speech tokens, 70% of them in one Mimi round trip, which destroys existing waveform and token-level watermarks.
XhaJ9V3HhQ.method: Redwing builds a basis from the graph Laplacian of token substitutions under retokenization so that tokens that replace each other get similar values, then solves for embedding and detection functions that preserve the signal through retokenization at bounded cost.
XhaJ9V3HhQ.key_idea: Bias generation in a smooth basis over tokens that substitute for each other under retokenization, so the watermark survives codec round trips.
XhaJ9V3HhQ.evidence: Moshi with repeated Mimi resynthesis, three other neural codecs and two TTS models, against KGW, WMAR and signal-based baselines, with thresholds calibrated empirically on held-out unwatermarked speech.
XhaJ9V3HhQ.claimed_gains: After eight passes of Mimi resynthesis on Moshi, Redwing keeps 80.7% TPR at 1% FPR against at most 12.8% for other token-level baselines, and reaches 85.0-93.0% TPR after three other neural codecs.
XhaJ9V3HhQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling retokenization as an estimable channel is well motivated and that the method stays detectable under repeated resynthesis where baselines fail, with ablations showing the Laplacian basis helps.
XhaJ9V3HhQ.main_concern: Robustness to codec resynthesis does not extend to simple desynchronization attacks such as time shifts and cropping, and the closest baseline (HiPT) is excluded although it could be calibrated empirically.

CLNPWplLvB.one_liner: Jointly learns a predictor and a KL-regularized distribution over environment constructions for invariant-risk and group-robust training.
CLNPWplLvB.problem: The environments chosen for robust training, and how much each contributes, strongly affect how much the predictor relies on spurious correlations.
CLNPWplLvB.method: UAED learns a distribution over a family of environment constructions (transformations, or example groupings built from a reference predictor's difficulty), regularized by a KL penalty toward a reference. Cooperative updates tilt toward environments the predictor handles well, while reversing the sign of the update gives a robust counterpart that upper-bounds a KL-ball worst case.
CLNPWplLvB.key_idea: Treat environment weighting as a Gibbs policy learned with the predictor under a KL penalty, where the sign of its update (cooperative or adversarial) determines shortcut or robust behavior.
CLNPWplLvB.evidence: Theoretical characterization of the learned policies plus Colored MNIST and Waterbirds experiments (IRM and GroupDRO protocols) with restricted, uniform and frozen-policy controls.
CLNPWplLvB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the clear unified formulation linking environment weighting, Gibbs policies and distributionally robust optimization, and controls that separate coverage from adaptive weighting.
CLNPWplLvB.main_concern: Learning the environment weights shows no consistent advantage over a fixed broad (frozen) distribution or simple baselines such as IRM, and the theoretical results are seen as expected.

nGWN8PZtok.one_liner: Ledger for self-evolving agents that freezes artifacts and measures held-out value, build cost and carry cost, gating on positive value.
nGWN8PZtok.problem: Self-evolving agents are evaluated by accuracy gained while the task stream runs, which leaves unclear what the deployer owns once evolution stops.
nGWN8PZtok.method: Tags every LLM call by phase, content-addresses the artifact before measuring it, and fills four accounts (frozen held-out value, build cost, per-task carry cost, backbone lifetime). A recognition gate fixed in advance refuses to compute depreciation for an artifact whose value is not shown to be positive.
nGWN8PZtok.key_idea: Freeze and hash each evolved artifact, evaluate it on disjoint held-out tasks with evolution disabled, and book it as an asset only if its value is shown positive.
nGWN8PZtok.evidence: Instantiated inside the AgentStream suite with its methods, tasks and prompts unchanged, on GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4 (for example Tau2-telecom), with multiple builds and confidence intervals.
nGWN8PZtok.claimed_gains: No artifact as shipped was recognised as an asset: GPT-5.5's ACE playbook is harmful in three builds (-0.22, -0.30 and -0.18; pooled -0.23, 95% CI [-0.34, -0.12]), and GPT-5.4's frozen value at medium reasoning effort is +0.02 (95% CI [-0.05, +0.10]).
nGWN8PZtok.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is useful and under-studied and that the frozen, content-addressed, held-out protocol with explicit call attribution is auditable and the strongest contribution.
nGWN8PZtok.main_concern: Each backbone uses a single build and most rounds a single replicate on few tasks, so failing the strict recognition gate may reflect low power and does not show typical harm or absence of benefit.

GJIVGXpuke.one_liner: Recovers a shared reward basis from separately estimated context rewards by minimum-volume unmixing in Fisher geometry, adapting only mixture weights.
GJIVGXpuke.problem: Generalizing preference-based RL to a new task or user normally needs substantial extra feedback, and prior methods fit a shared reward basis directly from preference data.
GJIVGXpuke.method: Estimates context-specific rewards independently, then recovers a reusable basis by regularized minimum-volume unmixing in a preference-induced Fisher geometry. A new context adapts by updating only low-dimensional mixture weights.
GJIVGXpuke.key_idea: Separate reward learning from basis recovery and extract the basis by minimum-volume unmixing under a Fisher metric rather than by joint fitting.
GJIVGXpuke.evidence: Cross-task robotic manipulation (conventional policies and vision-language-action models), cross-user personalization in LLMs and assistive human-robot interaction, real-robot experiments and an assistive-feeding user study, against baselines including LoRe.
GJIVGXpuke.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says it consistently outperforms baselines in preference alignment and downstream task performance, especially when target feedback is scarce.
GJIVGXpuke.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the clean separation of reward learning from basis recovery, the explicit Fisher and minimum-volume criterion with worked analysis, and the real-robot experiments.
GJIVGXpuke.main_concern: Most experiments do not test adaptation to a genuinely new preference (source and target preferences coincide), and the shared-criteria assumption and noise-free preference labels are not validated.

lzmbp5BFV8.one_liner: Trainable harness distilling trajectories into an experience graph and an RL-trained retrieval copilot that improves frozen LLM executors.
lzmbp5BFV8.problem: Agents' accumulated experience rarely flows back into the harness, and combining task-adaptive retrieval with experience reuse across frozen executors is hard.
lzmbp5BFV8.method: Distills trajectories into reusable skills and failure lessons in a self-evolving experience graph, and trains a lightweight retrieval copilot that decides per task how broadly to explore the graph and how strongly to favor historically useful over merely similar experiences. The copilot is optimized with RL from a utility reward combining the with/without-experience score difference and an absolute-performance term, and the same reward updates the graph.
lzmbp5BFV8.key_idea: Learn per-task retrieval breadth and utility-versus-similarity weighting over an experience graph, using a reward based on the with/without-experience score difference.
lzmbp5BFV8.evidence: ExpSuite with 10 static benchmarks and 2 agentic environments, twelve baselines, transfer across executors and four ablations.
lzmbp5BFV8.claimed_gains: Improves over the strongest baseline by 12.1% and 4.5% on static tasks and by 21.4% and 12.7% on agentic tasks with the smaller and larger executors, respectively.
lzmbp5BFV8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is broad, covering 10 static benchmarks, two agentic environments and several executors, with consistent gains and useful cross-executor transfer experiments.
lzmbp5BFV8.main_concern: Technical novelty is limited (graph memory, personalized PageRank and PPO combined), reported baseline numbers look low, and there is no statistical uncertainty reporting or fixed-retrieval ablation.

JCL7A13W09.one_liner: Entity lens, a relation-agnostic Jacobian-lens variant, predicts which relations a language model decodes linearly.
JCL7A13W09.problem: The faithfulness of linear relational embeddings (LREs) varies enormously across relations, and the factors behind that variation are unclear.
JCL7A13W09.method: Trains an entity lens for an entity type (for example countries or persons) to predict the model's output under the neutral prompt '{} is known for', then measures how highly it ranks the model's answer for a relation using no relation-specific information.
JCL7A13W09.key_idea: Rank a relation's answers with a lens trained only on what the model says about an entity type, treating linear decodability as a property of the subject representation.
JCL7A13W09.evidence: 28 relations of the LRE dataset on OLMo-3-7B, with six more models in the appendix according to reviewers.
JCL7A13W09.claimed_gains: The relation-agnostic score correlates with LRE faithfulness at rho = 0.7355 (p < .01) across 28 relations of the LRE dataset on OLMo-3-7B.
JCL7A13W09.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question relevant and the prediction of LRE faithfulness from subject representations without relation information a neat, impressive finding backed by many studies.
JCL7A13W09.main_concern: The headline analysis relies on a single model (OLMo-3-7B), and alternative explanations such as pretraining frequency of facts are not ruled out.

zQ7rqJUTBz.one_liner: Post-hoc temperature scaling of the draft distribution raises speculative-decoding acceptance length by matching the underconfident draft to the target.
