zQ7rqJUTBz.problem: Speculative-decoding speedup depends on the gap between target and draft distributions, and open-source draft models are generally underconfident relative to the target.
zQ7rqJUTBz.method: Applies post-hoc calibration, including standard temperature scaling and token-wise calibration, to the draft distribution while the target distribution is preserved by the rejection-sampling verification.
zQ7rqJUTBz.key_idea: Sharpen the draft distribution with a scalar temperature so it matches the target's confidence, increasing token acceptance probability at no additional cost.
zQ7rqJUTBz.evidence: Online decoding experiments across nine target-draft pairs and eight workloads according to reviewers, plus analysis of more general token-wise calibrators.
zQ7rqJUTBz.claimed_gains: Standard temperature scaling improves the acceptance length by approximately 10% at no additional cost across different settings.
zQ7rqJUTBz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the intervention is simple, inexpensive and preserves the target distribution, with gains across nine target-draft pairs and a broad range of good temperatures.
zQ7rqJUTBz.main_concern: Only accepted length is measured, not end-to-end latency or throughput, so the serving-speed claim is unverified, and the method is standard temperature scaling with small gains for some draft checkpoints.

SH7yYNr3NF.one_liner: Defines a task's ceiling as best shallow-circuit accuracy and proves transformers without chain of thought cannot exceed it.
SH7yYNr3NF.problem: It is debated whether the content of chains of thought does real computational work or is largely decorative.
SH7yYNr3NF.method: Treats one transformer pass as a constant-depth circuit, defines the ceiling of a task as the best accuracy of a shallow circuit (serial if below one), and proves necessity (content-independent replacements fall to the ceiling), depth (no shallow computation can write the chain) and locality (the answer is one shallow pass from the finished chain).
SH7yYNr3NF.key_idea: Bound accuracy without chain content by the best accuracy of a constant-depth circuit on the task, so serial tasks require the chain's content.
SH7yYNr3NF.evidence: Proofs that hold for any trained transformer, plus experiments on finite-group word problems with known ceilings using small transformers trained from scratch (with or without RL) and on math benchmarks.
SH7yYNr3NF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the ceiling framework gives a precise, training-independent criterion for when chain of thought is necessary and links circuit complexity to measured accuracy.
SH7yYNr3NF.main_concern: Empirical accuracy drops after chain erasure are confounded by train-test mismatch and do not show the ceiling is the cause, and the theoretical advance over prior chain-of-thought expressivity results is seen as limited.

L997IPslIB.one_liner: Stateful graph-feedback framework comparing repeated refitting with continued deployment of an initial classifier under prediction-induced graph change.
L997IPslIB.problem: Graph-based predictions can alter the features and outcomes used in later training, so a better fit on an updated graph state may not give a better deployment policy.
L997IPslIB.method: Formulates a stateful graph-feedback process with a common-state comparison that isolates the contribution of refitting and a policy comparison that also captures deployment-generated graph states. It is instantiated for synthetic node classification (well-posedness, invariant distribution, finite-horizon transfer condition) and a user-product graph with explanation recourse.
L997IPslIB.key_idea: Evaluate classifiers on a common graph state to separate the gain from refitting from the graph states induced by deployment.
L997IPslIB.evidence: Synthetic node-classification experiments across independently generated datasets, an end-to-end GCN versus skip-GCN study, and a user-product graph simulation with explanation recourse.
L997IPslIB.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports that the update policy can reverse the performance ordering of GNN architectures.
L997IPslIB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem relevant to deployed graph models, the common-state comparison easy to interpret and the theory sound under its assumptions, with a GCN and skip-GCN ranking reversal across update policies.
L997IPslIB.main_concern: The transfer theorem and bounds are not evaluated in the experiments, which use few architectures, small graphs and a fixed strength of prediction-induced feature change.

tIzUK2ql43.one_liner: Non-asymptotic coverage and interval-length guarantees for split conformalized quantile regression on time series via functional dependence measures.
tIzUK2ql43.problem: Conformal theory for time series rests on mixing conditions that are hard to verify and fail for many standard processes, and the accuracy of interval length is understudied.
tIzUK2ql43.method: Fits a model on one block and calibrates the conformal interval on the adjacent block for conformalized quantile and median regression, replacing mixing assumptions with the functional dependence measure. For Gaussian linear processes with long memory it derives a sharper length-error rate with a matching lower bound.
tIzUK2ql43.key_idea: Control the dependence between the fitted center and the adjacent calibration block through the functional dependence measure to bound coverage and interval length together.
tIzUK2ql43.evidence: Theorems 1-4 with examples where the dependence assumption holds (Bernoulli autoregressions, Gaussian long-memory processes), simulations, and one electricity-load application according to reviewers.
tIzUK2ql43.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper guarantees coverage and interval length simultaneously and non-asymptotically for non-mixing and long-memory processes, widening the class covered by split-conformal theory.
tIzUK2ql43.main_concern: The theory combines known tools under strong assumptions (stationarity, uniform consistency of the learner, a Gaussian constant-covariate long-memory case), and real-data validation is limited with no comparison to ACI or EnbPI.

RzsEZubFoV.one_liner: Neural ODE with a Stuart-Landau limit-cycle prior and cyclic feedback across omics layers for stable multi-omics dynamics.
RzsEZubFoV.problem: Standard neural ODEs suffer timescale collapse and numerical stiffness when modeling hierarchical, multi-timescale oscillatory biological systems.
RzsEZubFoV.method: Embeds a Stuart-Landau limit-cycle prior in the latent vector field so the network models deviations from an underlying rhythm (orbit-centered residuals), with explicit feedback between omics layers. A cyclic small-gain analysis guarantees bounded trajectories and exponential orbital attraction.
RzsEZubFoV.key_idea: Constrain the latent vector field to an oscillator prior and bound the loop gains through cyclic small-gain analysis so trajectories stay bounded and attracted to an orbit.
RzsEZubFoV.evidence: Compared with continuous-time models including scNODE and Heavy Ball NODE on a four-layer mouse liver atlas, a two-layer Neurospora crassa time course in constant darkness, and a two-layer yeast dataset.
RzsEZubFoV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the architecture addresses the loss of bounded, sustained oscillations in unconstrained continuous-time models, with an orbit-centered residual and a small-gain argument that supports stability.
RzsEZubFoV.main_concern: Ablations change several components at once, so gains cannot be attributed to the Stuart-Landau prior or cyclic topology, and the evaluation covers few sparse time courses with limited seeds.

hZnvnKD5Wp.one_liner: Benchmark of visual math proofs for VLMs, graded by LLM judge with expert rubrics, plus proof-preserving and proof-breaking variants.
hZnvnKD5Wp.problem: Existing visual math benchmarks test shallow calculation rather than deeper reasoning such as explaining a visual proof.
hZnvnKD5Wp.method: Builds 50 core visual proofs that models must translate into natural-language explanations, graded at scale by an LLM judge using expert-crafted per-item rubrics, plus 102 proof-preserving and 88 proof-breaking diagram variants to test whether models distinguish valid from flawed constructions.
hZnvnKD5Wp.key_idea: Require explaining the construction shown in a proof diagram, and test faithfulness by modifying diagrams so the proof is either preserved or broken.
hZnvnKD5Wp.evidence: Evaluation of open-source and frontier VLMs on the benchmark and its variants, with human annotator agreement on the rubric grading.
hZnvnKD5Wp.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports dramatic failures of open-source and frontier VLMs in explaining visual proofs, without numbers.
hZnvnKD5Wp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark targets an important, underexplored distinction between mathematical correctness and fidelity to visual evidence, with well-designed valid and invalid variants.
hZnvnKD5Wp.main_concern: LLM-judge validity is not shown on held-out responses (agreement is reported among human annotators who saw each other's scores), and performance drops under modified figures are not shown to isolate memorization.

OnZwqqRq3M.one_liner: Adversarial-training regularizer aligning clean and adversarial intermediate features using representation-similarity metrics such as CKA and Soft-kNN.
OnZwqqRq3M.problem: Methods like TRADES and ALP align only softmax or logit outputs at the end of the network, and robust training often causes severe accuracy-robustness trade-offs.
OnZwqqRq3M.method: RepAlign adds a term maximizing representation similarity (CKA, HSIC, CKNNA or Soft-kNN) between features of clean and adversarially perturbed inputs at chosen layers on top of standard PGD adversarial training.
OnZwqqRq3M.key_idea: Maximize batch-level representation similarity between clean and adversarial intermediate features instead of matching outputs pointwise.
OnZwqqRq3M.evidence: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Imagenette against PGD-AT and TRADES, with AutoAttack-style robustness evaluation, lambda sweeps and layer ablations.
OnZwqqRq3M.claimed_gains: Soft-kNN on CIFAR-10 reaches 86.90% clean accuracy (+4.05% over TRADES) with 49.36% robust accuracy under AutoAttack (+3.08% over PGD-AT), and on CIFAR-100 reaches 60.42% clean and 25.97% robust accuracy (+4.63% and +0.65% over TRADES).
OnZwqqRq3M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a simple, practical regularizer that plugs into adversarial training at a cost similar to PGD-AT and gives a clear clean-accuracy gain.
OnZwqqRq3M.main_concern: The reported 'AutoAttack' accuracy is the minimum of separately run attacks rather than the standard per-sample worst case, likely overstating robustness, and the gains are mostly in clean accuracy against weaker baseline configurations.

XzlNiYoA7t.one_liner: Training-free masked-diffusion image-editing accelerator that uses look-ahead decoded images to localize edits, cache regional features and adapt sampling length.
XzlNiYoA7t.problem: Masked diffusion editing models recompute full-sequence bidirectional attention at every step under a fixed schedule, wasting compute on small edits and already-stable predictions.
XzlNiYoA7t.method: Decodes intermediate token predictions into look-ahead images; their difference from the reference image progressively localizes the edit region and drives a two-stage regional caching strategy that reuses features outside it, while changes between successive look-ahead images set the sampling budget.
XzlNiYoA7t.key_idea: The spatial support of an edit stabilizes before its appearance is refined, so look-ahead images can localize edits for caching and signal when to stop sampling.
XzlNiYoA7t.evidence: ImgEdit and PIE-Bench experiments compared with acceleration baselines, plus ablations of caching, support expansion and residual correction.
XzlNiYoA7t.claimed_gains: Achieves an 8.02x speedup while maintaining instruction-following capability on ImgEdit and PIE-Bench (the rest of the abstract is cut off).
XzlNiYoA7t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is practical, needs no training or extra masks, and gives strong efficiency with comparable quality on two benchmarks.
XzlNiYoA7t.main_concern: The comparison and ablations do not isolate the sources of gain: baselines use 24 steps against 12-18 for LightDraft, and residual correction alone accounts for much of the preservation improvement.

MMkYLPv7YO.one_liner: Fine-tunes models to evade model-diffing audit statistics while keeping a planted false belief, then proposes a logit-offset depth detector.
MMkYLPv7YO.problem: Model-diffing audits infer what fine-tuning changed, but a fine-tuner who knows the audit can subtract its signal, so exposed audit statistics may not be forensic evidence.
MMkYLPv7YO.method: Plants false beliefs in models and trains each to evade one or several audit statistics (mean activation difference, output classifiers, frozen probes, text-only auditors), testing all auditors on sealed documents. For persistent top-K logit tails, a bound on logit-offset depth yields a detector with a threshold sealed in advance.
MMkYLPv7YO.key_idea: Optimize fine-tuning to cancel a specific audit statistic while keeping the belief, then detect the surviving tell-tale through the depth of the logit offset.
MMkYLPv7YO.evidence: Sealed test documents, matched strength-0 controls, cross-auditor evaluation, and benign Qwen3-1.7B fine-tunes to measure false accusations.
MMkYLPv7YO.claimed_gains: With its threshold sealed in advance, depth detects every held-out attack on the top-K output classifier and accuses 0 of 288 Qwen3-1.7B benign fine-tunes, while most targeted auditors were evaded with the belief kept.
MMkYLPv7YO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the careful protocol with sealed test sets, matched controls and cross-auditor comparisons, and the reporting of false accusations on benign fine-tunes.
MMkYLPv7YO.main_concern: The planted beliefs are narrow and low-stakes and the presentation is dense, so generality to realistic hidden behaviors is not established, and a threshold-aware attack evades the proposed depth detector.

oAMmUnkAAA.one_liner: Anti-distillation defense that injects easy-to-fit shortcuts into teacher reasoning so students fit responses without acquiring the capability.
oAMmUnkAAA.problem: LLM responses can be distilled without authorization, and existing defenses make responses hard to fit rather than preventing transfer of the generalizable capability.
oAMmUnkAAA.method: DistilShield uses an Unlearnable Converter to implant implicit shortcuts into teacher reasoning, steers learning dynamics away from capability transfer during optimization, and consolidates the induced behavior under the student's own rollout distribution.
oAMmUnkAAA.key_idea: Decouple fitting from knowledge transfer by making teacher reasoning easy to imitate through shortcut perturbations (unlearnable examples) that carry no transferable capability.
oAMmUnkAAA.evidence: Experiments across several student models (including Qwen, Gemma and Llama-3.2-1B), math and code tasks, robustness tests (adversarial training, repetitive querying, paraphrasing) and component-removal ablations.
oAMmUnkAAA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating data fitting from skill learning is an original, useful view of anti-distillation, supported by extensive experiments and ablations.
oAMmUnkAAA.main_concern: Gains vary across student models and robustness is tested against a limited set of countermeasures, leaving robustness to adaptive attackers, added training cost and novelty over prior unlearnable-distillation work unclear.

NWE5oGOrVo.one_liner: Training-free length adaptation for masked diffusion LLMs that expands or contracts the canvas using implicit EOS density during denoising.
NWE5oGOrVo.problem: Masked diffusion LLMs such as LLaDA use a fixed generation length, so a short canvas constrains content while a long one wastes computation.
NWE5oGOrVo.method: Reads the implicit density of end-of-sequence tokens over remaining mask positions during denoising: low density triggers expansion and high density triggers contraction, within the original denoising loop and without retraining or a separate length-adjustment stage.
NWE5oGOrVo.key_idea: Use the evolving density of EOS predictions among masked positions as an online signal of whether the current length is too short or too long.
NWE5oGOrVo.evidence: Mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks on LLaDA-family 8B models, compared with fixed lengths and DAEDAL according to reviewers.
NWE5oGOrVo.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says it yields a more favorable Pareto frontier in the quality-efficiency trade-off on math and code tasks.
NWE5oGOrVo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree implicit EOS density is a simple, practical, training-free signal that works better than EOS confidence and, unlike DAEDAL, can also shrink the canvas.
NWE5oGOrVo.main_concern: The method is incremental over DAEDAL with small gains, is evaluated only on LLaDA-family models, and its 'bidirectional' and Pareto-dominance claims are overstated.

FgNg0T6sTW.one_liner: Splits a Transformer into state and prediction towers, then has every prediction layer read the final state (Sequential).
FgNg0T6sTW.problem: Each hidden state of a decoder-only Transformer both stores context and predicts the next token, and it is unclear which state prediction should read.
FgNg0T6sTW.method: Gives the two jobs separate towers with separate weights, analyzes attention patterns, ablations, probes and layer lesions, finds that prediction depends most on later state layers and distant positions, and designs Sequential, where every prediction layer reads the final state.
FgNg0T6sTW.key_idea: Let every prediction layer read the final-layer state output rather than same-depth states, since prediction loses previous-token information in its later layers while state keeps it.
FgNg0T6sTW.evidence: Mechanistic analyses (ablation, patching, probes) and matched-parameter and matched-FLOP language-model comparisons at four sizes up to 327M non-embedding parameters, with out-of-domain and 32K-token tests at 92M.
FgNg0T6sTW.claimed_gains: At equal non-embedding parameters and FLOPs, Sequential beats the Transformer at all four sizes up to 327M, with validation loss lower by 0.042-0.079 nats/token and higher zero-shot accuracy.
FgNg0T6sTW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled comparison at matched parameters and FLOPs, with mechanistic ablations and probes, gives useful evidence of state-prediction specialization.
FgNg0T6sTW.main_concern: Quality is judged mainly by validation loss on one corpus without downstream tasks, and the design overlaps with earlier final-state-reading architectures such as YOCO that are not baselines.

SauNY7P5yQ.one_liner: Lightweight trainable plugin adapts a frozen binary-treatment causal foundation model to continuous treatments via quantile anchors and local ensembling.
SauNY7P5yQ.problem: Existing in-context causal effect foundation models handle only binary treatments and cannot be applied directly to continuous treatment effect estimation.
SauNY7P5yQ.method: Uses treatment quantiles as thresholds to binarize the continuous treatment into anchor values, learns a covariate-treatment interaction representation for each anchor with a task-specific encoder fed into the frozen binary model (only the encoder is fine-tuned), and combines the anchor models locally around each treatment value.
SauNY7P5yQ.key_idea: Feed treatment-dependent learned representations and quantile-binarized labels into a frozen binary causal foundation model at several anchors, then ensemble the anchors near the queried dose.
SauNY7P5yQ.evidence: A Lipschitz-based error bound (Theorem 1) and experiments with ablations, according to reviewers (the abstract is cut off before results).
SauNY7P5yQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing existing binary causal foundation models for continuous treatments without repeating pretraining is practically relevant and the design is interesting.
SauNY7P5yQ.main_concern: The constructed inputs contain treatment information and so are not conventional binary causal tasks, and the transfer of causal guarantees, positivity and counterfactual accuracy from factual training loss are not established.

0ow2QpmAsR.one_liner: Proves matched bounds on prediction error for SGD with stochastic rounding in a random-features linear model with power-law spectra.
0ow2QpmAsR.problem: It is unclear how stochastic rounding in low-precision training affects prediction risk as model size, training time and precision change.
0ow2QpmAsR.method: Analyzes a two-layer linear network with a fixed random first layer trained by mini-batch SGD on Gaussian power-law data, with forward and backward features rounded independently. It proves matched upper and lower bounds for the last iterate and for parameter averaging under general learning-rate and precision schedules, and derives compute-optimal scaling.
0ow2QpmAsR.key_idea: Stochastic rounding leaves the mean on the exact-GD path and adds distinct noise terms, so forward and backward rounding enter the scaling law differently.
0ow2QpmAsR.evidence: Theorems in a solvable model, with transfer to actual SGD resting on a conjecture, plus transformer experiments that reviewers say were added during rebuttal.
0ow2QpmAsR.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says rounding only forward features preserves the compute scaling of exact arithmetic while rounding backward features changes it.
0ow2QpmAsR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a clear theoretical model of low-precision training that yields useful insights on where and when higher precision matters.
0ow2QpmAsR.main_concern: The transfer of the main scaling laws to real SGD with joint rounding relies on an unproven conjecture, and the real-network experiments do not directly validate the precision-allocation prescriptions.

FsMaAZOsLq.one_liner: Localizes a safety-critical layer block, aligns safety only there, then freezes it during downstream fine-tuning of LLMs.
FsMaAZOsLq.problem: Benign fine-tuning overwrites safety-critical parameters and weakens refusal behavior and jailbreak resistance, and existing defenses do not prevent this direct overwrite.
FsMaAZOsLq.method: AlignLock follows a localize-align-lock paradigm: layer-wise sensitivity analysis finds a safety-critical layer block, safety alignment updates are restricted to that block, and the same block is locked during downstream fine-tuning. An interference-based analysis argues that locking removes direct overwrite from task gradients.
FsMaAZOsLq.key_idea: Confine safety alignment to a layer block found by layer-wise sensitivity analysis, then freeze exactly that block so task gradients cannot overwrite it.
FsMaAZOsLq.evidence: Experiments across multiple open-weight LLM families and benign downstream domains, plus an interference-based analysis; reviews mention code, math and finance tasks, Qwen, Llama, Gemma and OLMoE models, and baselines such as SafeLoRA and RESTA.
FsMaAZOsLq.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports only consistent safety gains over vanilla fine-tuning with competitive task performance, with no numbers).
FsMaAZOsLq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the align-then-lock design is clear, the evaluation covers several model families and utility benchmarks, and the ablations and layer-sensitivity analysis support the design.
FsMaAZOsLq.main_concern: Margins over the best baselines are small and lack standard deviations or same-size block controls, and over-refusal and localization stability across harmful datasets are not examined.

7nq8cLrifw.one_liner: Differentially private continual-release mechanism that keeps exactly n synthetic users while answering pattern-frequency queries over longitudinal data.
7nq8cLrifw.problem: Prior continual-release synthetic data (Bun et al., PODS 2024) inflates the synthetic dataset exponentially in the window length k and has higher error for short patterns.
7nq8cLrifw.method: They introduce a differentially private mechanism that updates a synthetic dataset at each time step while maintaining the same number of individuals as the original. Reviews describe a recursive construction with deficit-based analysis, user-level zCDP guarantees, and an extension to categorical data.
7nq8cLrifw.key_idea: Continually update a synthetic dataset with a recursive private construction that preserves the user count n and supports all pattern lengths up to k at once.
7nq8cLrifw.evidence: Theoretical accuracy bounds and user-level zCDP guarantees; reviews also mention experiments comparing against Bun et al. with reasonable runtime overhead.
7nq8cLrifw.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports no numbers; it claims lower worst-case asymptotic error for normalized pattern frequencies and lower error for shorter patterns).
7nq8cLrifw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preserving exactly n synthetic users and handling categorical data are meaningful contributions, and that the mechanism is clean and the theory strong.
7nq8cLrifw.main_concern: The Theorem 3 error bound can far exceed the maximum possible count error n (about 84,793 versus 200 in one example), and the experimental metrics are argued to be unfair to the prior method.

8GAC3uIjci.one_liner: Dataset of 800 scale-resolved CFD simulations of parameterized pickup trucks, with benchmarks of neural surrogates and out-of-distribution sets.
8GAC3uIjci.problem: Existing automotive aerodynamics datasets such as DrivAerML and SHIFT-SUV lack the open cargo-bed flow of pickup trucks, and scale-resolved CFD is too costly for broad design exploration.
8GAC3uIjci.method: SHIFT-Truck provides 800 SA-DDES simulations of a reference pickup morphed across 17 shape parameters, each on a mesh of about 100 million cells at a Reynolds number of 1.4 x 10^7, released with time-averaged fields and benchmarks of recent neural surrogates and published out-of-distribution sets.
8GAC3uIjci.key_idea: Parametric morphing of one reference pickup geometry across 17 shape parameters, with matched bed-state and spoiler variants, supplies scale-resolved ground truth for training aerodynamic surrogates.
8GAC3uIjci.evidence: 800 SA-DDES simulations described as experimentally validated, with mesh and numerical validation discussion, a baseline drag of 0.446 versus 0.393 experimental per a reviewer, and neural-surrogate benchmarks with out-of-distribution sets.
8GAC3uIjci.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dataset fills an underserved aerodynamic setting (open-bed recirculation) with high-fidelity surface and volume targets and controlled geometry and part variations, and is well motivated.
8GAC3uIjci.main_concern: The contribution is incremental and narrow: all cases morph one GTU template, limiting geometric diversity, the final CFD setup is not fully verified (drag 0.446 versus 0.393 experimental), and out-of-distribution tests use a single training truck.

xMJpG5fy25.one_liner: Calibrated edit distillation shifts teacher logits by log population odds ratios so rankers respond to requests by the right amount.
xMJpG5fy25.problem: Text-profile recommenders are trained and evaluated only on the direction of a user's correction, not on how much the recommendation list should change, so fine-tuned rankers ignore requests or over-react.
xMJpG5fy25.method: CED trains the ranker with a teacher that, given each request's kind and attribute, shifts the logits of the concerned items by the log of the population odds ratio, which under a softmax choice model moves a neutral user's odds to those of reference users who already hold the preference. The model learns to produce this shift from the request.
xMJpG5fy25.key_idea: Teacher logits are shifted by the log population odds ratio of the requested attribute, which under a softmax choice model matches a neutral user's odds to reference users'.
xMJpG5fy25.evidence: Measurements on thousands of add, withdraw, and negate requests for unseen users on MovieLens-1M and held-out tag-level attributes, with multiple baselines, unseen request phrasings, and users with changing preferences.
xMJpG5fy25.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating the direction of a request from its magnitude, and withdrawal from negation, is a useful insight, and CED is a simple, principled way to add calibration without an inference-time parser.
xMJpG5fy25.main_concern: The calibration target is a population-level average that may not match what an individual user wants, aggregation can hide over- and under-adjustment, and the method is shown only on a cross-encoder with explicit metadata that scales poorly.

71zSREXRh7.one_liner: Benchmark of 114 full-stack web feature-delivery tasks from 24 public repositories, scored by executable behavioral checks.
71zSREXRh7.problem: Existing benchmarks cover isolated repository-level issues or greenfield web apps, so it is unclear how reliably agents deliver long-horizon features across frontend, backend, and database in existing codebases.
71zSREXRh7.method: WebDevHorizon has 114 tasks from 52 releases across 24 public repositories, each a feature shipped by maintainers with requirements reconstructed from development history. The requirements are mapped to executable checks of component behavior, API contracts, persistent state, and browser workflows.
71zSREXRh7.key_idea: Reconstruct each shipped feature's behavioral requirements from project history and verify them with executable component, API, state, and browser-workflow checks.
71zSREXRh7.evidence: Evaluation of several models and agent harnesses (including Codex and Claude Code) on the 114 tasks, with an analysis of failure types.
71zSREXRh7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is carefully built and validated, fills a real gap by requiring changes across frontend, backend, and database, and is clearly written.
71zSREXRh7.main_concern: The analysis of results is thin (why official harnesses score lower, why incomplete implementation dominates failures), and the hidden LLM-drafted checks are not validated as measuring true feature delivery.

qytGDfyVNK.one_liner: IGIS distills shorter-horizon intermediate-goal representations into distant-goal representations to sharpen primitive-action scoring in flat goal-conditioned offline RL.
qytGDfyVNK.problem: In long-horizon goal-conditioned RL, action-dependent differences become weak relative to estimation noise for distant goals, making primitive actions hard to discriminate.
qytGDfyVNK.method: IGIS builds a goal-conditioned action scorer from state-action and state-goal representations and strengthens the distant-goal representation by distilling shorter-horizon information from intermediate-goal representations along offline trajectories. No subgoal generation or hierarchical execution is needed at test time.
qytGDfyVNK.key_idea: Use intermediate-goal representations along offline trajectories as training-time distillation targets for the distant-goal representation, keeping a flat action scorer at test time.
qytGDfyVNK.evidence: Long-horizon locomotion and manipulation benchmarks (humanoidmaze-giant and puzzle-4x6 with four seeds, per reviews), with ablations against TRL and TRL+BVN.
qytGDfyVNK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see meaningful gains on hard benchmarks (e.g., TRL 75 to 96 on humanoidmaze-giant) and an ablation indicating the gains are not explained by the bilinear critic alone.
qytGDfyVNK.main_concern: The closest related methods (SAW, Dual Advantage Fields, Multistep Quasimetric Estimation) are untested or missing as baselines, and the contribution of the relevance weight rho is not isolated.

RV8zRC9ELb.one_liner: DUET separately tracks visual novelty and action dispersion in a frozen VLA to trigger EXECUTE, CAUTION or HELP responses.
RV8zRC9ELb.problem: Existing monitors merge uncertainty from unfamiliar visual content and from multiple valid action continuations into one score, hiding the source of a warning.
RV8zRC9ELb.method: A visual evidence branch measures novelty relative to successful demonstrations, and an action evidence branch measures local conditional dispersion at a fixed observation and noisy flow state. Separate references calibrate the two branches into EXECUTE, CAUTION and HELP, and the visual branch also provides spatial evidence.
RV8zRC9ELb.key_idea: Keep two evidence channels apart: demonstration-referenced visual novelty and flow-matching action dispersion (a Gaussian covariance-divergence identity), each calibrated against its own reference.
RV8zRC9ELb.evidence: Tests on a frozen SmolVLA policy (multiple checkpoints and training seeds, per reviews) and on a physical robot with familiar versus unfamiliar objects.
RV8zRC9ELb.claimed_gains: The visual branch detects unfamiliar observations with 0.940 frame AUROC, the action branch detects local action ambiguity with AUROC 0.963 +/- 0.052, and on a physical robot HELP triggers in 45/50 unfamiliar-object trials and 1/50 familiar-object trials.
RV8zRC9ELb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating visual novelty from action ambiguity is a clear, formally grounded design that deploys on frozen VLAs without fine-tuning.
RV8zRC9ELb.main_concern: Validation uses a single VLA (SmolVLA), and robot experiments cover only the visual HELP branch, not the action-driven CAUTION branch or full three-way routing.

cgGAzHaB9R.one_liner: Gradient penalty on DreamerV3's posterior latent distribution, derived from a finite-difference penalty, shares transition information between neighboring states.
cgGAzHaB9R.problem: Where transitions are sparse, a learned world model's transition function can change rapidly between neighboring states, and long imagined rollouts compound the resulting errors.
cgGAzHaB9R.method: GPLD is derived as the small-neighborhood limit of a finite-difference penalty on transition laws in a finite MDP, giving the squared Frobenius norm of the dynamics Jacobian. It is applied to DreamerV3's posterior latent distribution and estimated with Hutchinson-style stochastic probes.
cgGAzHaB9R.key_idea: Penalize the squared Frobenius norm of the dynamics Jacobian of DreamerV3's posterior latent map, estimated with Hutchinson probes, so neighboring states share transition information.
cgGAzHaB9R.evidence: 18 proprioceptive DeepMind Control tasks with one fixed configuration against DreamerV3, plus a tabular experiment, comparisons to alternative regularizers, ablations, and multi-step prediction error analysis.
cgGAzHaB9R.claimed_gains: GPLD raises final return over DreamerV3 on 15 of 18 proprioceptive DeepMind Control tasks (sign test p = 0.0075), mean final return by 9.8% on the 12 unsaturated tasks (18.1% in normalized return), and by 20.7% on the six humanoid and dog tasks.
cgGAzHaB9R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is clearly motivated by a principled link between smoothness regularization and transition estimation and improves on DreamerV3 on proprioceptive control tasks.
cgGAzHaB9R.main_concern: The improvement diminishes on pixel-based tasks, and there is a gap between the theory (smoothness of transition distributions) and the method (regularizing the observation-conditioned posterior).

LZoeyR10RO.one_liner: On-policy distillation that builds response-level targets minimizing KL to student predictions while preserving a set teacher-gradient contribution, for tool-integrated reasoning.
LZoeyR10RO.problem: Multi-turn tool-integrated reasoning in small language models needs supervision that accounts for how student responses and tool feedback shape later contexts, which token-wise or step-wise targets do not.
LZoeyR10RO.method: Targets are chosen to minimize the KL from targets to student predictions, averaged over positions in a response, under a response-level constraint on retained teacher contribution. They are obtained by shifting student log probabilities along teacher-student difference directions with a single scale per response, found by one-dimensional bisection.
LZoeyR10RO.key_idea: Solve a per-response minimum-KL problem under a teacher-gradient constraint, giving an exponential-form target with a single shared scalar per response.
LZoeyR10RO.evidence: Small models (0.6B and 1.7B per reviewers) on AIME, GPQA, and LiveCodeBench against SOD, EOPD, and vanilla baselines, with ablations, paired confidence intervals, and a contamination audit.
LZoeyR10RO.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; reviewers cite mean Avg@8 gains over SOD of +2.67 at 0.6B and +0.89 at 1.7B.
LZoeyR10RO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the target construction has an explicit closed-form theoretical foundation with careful statements of scope, and the appendix is transparent about uncertainty and contamination.
LZoeyR10RO.main_concern: Gains over SOD are uneven and statistically weak (the 1.7B interval [-1.77, 3.34] includes zero and AIME scores are lower), and the contribution of joint response-level construction is not isolated.

ORnDqWLo1e.one_liner: Pipelined autoregressive Transformer: tokens decode in parallel, each delayed slightly behind the previous, for faster decoding and smaller KV cache.
ORnDqWLo1e.problem: Standard Transformers must fully generate each token before starting the next, and diffusion models that break this serial bottleneck are non-autoregressive latent-variable models.
ORnDqWLo1e.method: PipeT decodes tokens in parallel while attending bidirectionally as in diffusion, but delays token i+1 relative to token i so it depends autoregressively on token i and all previous tokens. Training stays simple, but pretraining and prompt prefilling are slower than in a standard Transformer.
ORnDqWLo1e.key_idea: Stagger parallel token streams so each token starts one step after its predecessor, keeping autoregressive dependence while overlapping computation across tokens.
ORnDqWLo1e.evidence: Models of 4M-200M parameters trained on the SlimPajama-6B subset with Chinchilla-style token budgets, plus a circuit-complexity expressivity analysis and state-tracking experiments according to reviews.
ORnDqWLo1e.claimed_gains: At 100M parameters, a 3-layer PipeT matches the test loss of a 4-layer standard Transformer while decoding 1.8x faster with a 3.1x smaller KV cache; the rest of the comparison is cut off in the abstract.
ORnDqWLo1e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the architecture is a creative, clearly presented way to overlap token computation while staying autoregressive, with quality-efficiency tradeoffs measured under matched budgets.
ORnDqWLo1e.main_concern: Few comparisons (no speculative decoding, recurrent, or hybrid baselines), small-scale evaluation (4M-200M models, batch size 8 in FP32), and training and prefill costs that are not well characterized.

lxyOAOhTcK.one_liner: Generates hard UNSAT instances by masked variational hypergraph autoencoding, reconstructing masked clauses via arity and membership prediction.
lxyOAOhTcK.problem: Realistic, challenging SAT instances are scarce in application-specific domains, and existing generators use handcrafted priors or predefined graph transformations that do not model how clauses are formed.
lxyOAOhTcK.method: Represents each CNF formula as a literal-clause hypergraph and casts generation as masked hyperedge reconstruction with a hypergraph neural network encoder, latent variables, and a decoder that predicts the arity and membership of each masked clause.
lxyOAOhTcK.key_idea: Model clause formation directly by masked hyperedge reconstruction in a variational hypergraph autoencoder over literal vertices and clause hyperedges.
lxyOAOhTcK.evidence: Experiments on real-world SAT benchmarks against generative baselines, a test of generalization to larger unseen instances without retraining, and data augmentation for solver-runtime prediction; reviews cite five SAT solvers across three benchmarks.
lxyOAOhTcK.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract claims harder instances than generative baselines, generalization to larger unseen instances without retraining, and useful augmentation for runtime prediction.
lxyOAOhTcK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the hypergraph-based generation a fresh take with good downstream tests, and one notes strong results across three benchmarks and five SAT solvers.
lxyOAOhTcK.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the learned generator from scrambling, hardness refinement, and the preserved UNSAT core, and it is not shown that the generated hard instances matter to solver developers.

0Fl2BtJlBz.one_liner: Traces how gradients cluster intermediate-variable representations in Transformers learning combinators, linking this to compositional generalization.
0Fl2BtJlBz.problem: Little is known about what drives networks to decompose problems into reusable subroutines and where such decomposition should be expected.
0Fl2BtJlBz.method: Studies which combinators (higher-order functions that combine simpler functions) Transformer language models learn across model sizes and data configurations, relates generalization on novel combinations to realization of intermediate causal variables, and traces gradients of training examples that share an intermediate value but differ downstream.
0Fl2BtJlBz.key_idea: Gradients from examples that share an intermediate value but differ downstream cluster that variable's representations, producing causal variables and compositional generalization.
0Fl2BtJlBz.evidence: Experiments with Transformer language models on synthetic combinator tasks across sizes and data configurations, mechanistic analysis with DAS per reviews, and a theoretical basis (Theorem 1).
0Fl2BtJlBz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated, the synthetic combinator tasks are a good lens on implicit reasoning, and the mechanistic analysis of how intermediate variables are learned is well executed.
0Fl2BtJlBz.main_concern: Clarity and presentation: key setup details such as task format and DAS implementation are buried in the appendix, the narrative is a sequence of results, and Theorem 1 lacks a formal proof.

lin9oXsbXJ.one_liner: Divides the dollar value or time saved by AI outputs on professional tasks by measured end-to-end energy.
lin9oXsbXJ.problem: Existing evaluations assess the economic value of AI output separately from the end-to-end energy needed to produce it, leaving the tradeoff unclear.
lin9oXsbXJ.method: Defines net dollar value (output value minus execution cost) and time saving (expert time minus AI time), then divides each by measured energy to give Net Value per Joule (NVJ) and Time Saving per Joule (TSJ). Studies 220 GDPval tasks across 44 occupations, serving five open-weight models locally on four accelerator types.
lin9oXsbXJ.key_idea: Net dollar value and time saved per task are divided by directly measured end-to-end energy, yielding NVJ (USD/MJ) and TSJ (hours/MJ).
lin9oXsbXJ.evidence: 220 public GDPval tasks across 44 occupations, five open-weight models served locally, four accelerator types, with an AI judge and a 32-comparison human validation per reviews.
lin9oXsbXJ.claimed_gains: Engineering work such as CAD design delivers about 27% more net dollar value per task than software development; the rest of the findings are cut off in the abstract.
lin9oXsbXJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that linking economic value to measured energy is timely and useful for the sustainability discussion, and that the framework extends across models, tasks and hardware.
lin9oXsbXJ.main_concern: Methodological validity: a fixed batch size of 20 across models is not a comparable setting, judge-based task values are weakly validated (71.9% agreement on 32 comparisons), and the energy allocation rule changes rankings.

Mgk5lTKXSn.one_liner: Training-free context extension combining position remapping (Pack) and score-based key-block skipping (Pick) in one FlashAttention pass.
Mgk5lTKXSn.problem: Training-free context extension to millions of tokens faces out-of-distribution context embeddings at unseen lengths and the quadratic cost of attention.
Mgk5lTKXSn.method: PickPack combines two composable operators in a single FlashAttention pass: Pack maps every query-key pair to a relative position inside the trained window, and Pick uses attention scores to dynamically decide which key blocks to skip.
Mgk5lTKXSn.key_idea: Remap relative positions into the trained window and skip key blocks below a running-max score threshold, both inside one FlashAttention kernel.
Mgk5lTKXSn.evidence: Per reviewers: eight model sizes from one family, base and post-trained checkpoints, five released long-context recipes, and three benchmarks, with lengths up to 4M tokens.
Mgk5lTKXSn.claimed_gains: At 50% sparsity it improves accuracy over dense attention under a condition that is cut off in the abstract; no other numbers stated.
Mgk5lTKXSn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dual challenge is practically important and the composable position-remapping plus block-skipping design is simple and hardware-aware, with broad evaluation across model sizes and context lengths.
Mgk5lTKXSn.main_concern: Novelty is mainly the composition, since Pack reuses Jet-Long-style remapping and Pick reuses BLASST-style skipping, and the accuracy gains come mostly from Pack while efficiency gains are modest.

zdwpxRFJkA.one_liner: Q-Former consolidates DNA, gene, protein, and text embeddings into multimodal tokens for a frozen LLM, transferring zero-shot to genomic tasks.
zdwpxRFJkA.problem: Multimodal AI systems for biology are limited to the specific tasks they are fine-tuned on, whether they textify biological evidence or project embeddings into fine-tuned language models.
zdwpxRFJkA.method: BioBLIP uses a master Q-Former to integrate DNA, gene, protein, and text modalities into multimodal tokens for a frozen LLM, pretrained on human single nucleotide variant annotation with 66M trained parameters and applied to unseen genomic tasks without fine-tuning.
zdwpxRFJkA.key_idea: A master Q-Former turns modality-specific biological embeddings into tokens a frozen LLM can read, trained only on variant annotation and reused zero-shot for other tasks.
zdwpxRFJkA.evidence: Pretraining on variant annotation, then variant prioritization and target gene prediction against matched-text LLMs and genomic foundation models such as Evo2 and GPN; reviewers cite 119 held-out loci and OpenTargets annotation training.
zdwpxRFJkA.claimed_gains: 85.2% overall annotation accuracy; 70.2% Top-1 variant prioritization versus 64.9% for LLMs given matched evidence in text and 59.3% for 40B-parameter genomic foundation models; 60.50% versus 43.70% in target gene prediction against matched-text LLMs.
zdwpxRFJkA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the experiments are broad and the frozen-LLM interface gives meaningful downstream gains, especially on target genes that are not the closest gene.
zdwpxRFJkA.main_concern: BioBLIP and the text baselines receive different information and training (gene-function descriptions, OpenTargets annotation training), and the ablations do not isolate whether multimodal tokens rather than extra knowledge or generated annotations drive the gains.

jlIdynNSpN.one_liner: Predicts future outcomes into a shared latent goal space and uses a learned bilinear containment score as the critic.
jlIdynNSpN.problem: In goal-conditioned RL, the critic and policy must relearn from value targets what structured goal representations mean, so agents trained on single goals do not generalize to set-valued abstract goals.
jlIdynNSpN.method: LFG learns a shared goal space without critic gradients and trains an action-conditioned predictor to map state-action pairs into it, each prediction representing a latent goal region. A learned bilinear containment relation scores whether a desired goal belongs to that region, and these scores serve as the critic; the predictor trains on observed future goals with targets discounted by time until arrival.
jlIdynNSpN.key_idea: Use the learned containment relation between a predicted latent goal region and a desired goal as the critic, so the critic inherits the goal space's structure.
jlIdynNSpN.evidence: Experiments on OGBench with single goals and on abstract goals (unions of disjoint goals and goal sets defined by a reward), comparing logistic and linear readouts of the relation against HGA-based and other baselines.
jlIdynNSpN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing the learned goal-space relation as the critic is a coherent idea that clearly distinguishes the method from separately learned critics.
jlIdynNSpN.main_concern: The abstract-goal evaluation is narrow (mostly two-goal unions), the set-containment reading of union success needs justification, and a baseline composing singleton critics (for example the max of two Q-values) is missing.

Mp0eLyV28N.one_liner: Offline spectral-trajectory curvature profiles place diffusion-cache refresh steps at equal cumulative-mass quantiles.
Mp0eLyV28N.problem: Fixed or generic-distance cache schedules can skip brief denoising windows when global structure forms, causing persistent image corruption.
Mp0eLyV28N.method: PACE calibrates a phase-sensitive dispersion profile from in-band spectral-coefficient curvature once per backbone. It places computation anchors at equal cumulative-mass quantiles and uses a static lookup with reuse- or prediction-based caches.
Mp0eLyV28N.key_idea: Calibrate spectral-coefficient curvature along denoising trajectories and schedule cache refreshes at equal quantiles of the accumulated dispersion profile.
Mp0eLyV28N.evidence: Phase-swap and perturbation analyses accompany matched-function-evaluation tests on FLUX.1-dev, SiT-XL/2, Wan2.1-1.3B, and HunyuanVideo-13B, plus a partition-optimality analysis.
Mp0eLyV28N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the spectral analysis of structural corruption and the coherent, practical cache-scheduling design.
Mp0eLyV28N.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate whether phase information specifically drives scheduling gains rather than amplitude or general spectral-curvature effects.

Age62DyKKR.one_liner: Composable tool workflows let agents create, cache, and reuse executable skills under controlled task difficulty.
Age62DyKKR.problem: Instance-level tool-use benchmarks do not reveal whether agents acquire reusable higher-level procedures for recurring workflows.
Age62DyKKR.method: SkillCraft constructs compositional tasks with quantitative and structural difficulty controls. Its protocol lets agents compose atomic tools into executable skills, cache them, and reuse them within and across tasks while measuring execution and efficiency.
Age62DyKKR.key_idea: Expose skill creation and persistent reuse as explicit actions in repeated tool workflows so compositional behavior becomes measurable.
Age62DyKKR.evidence: Experiments compare multiple agents across skill hierarchies and transfer settings, measuring task success, skill execution, reuse, tokens, cost, and turns.
Age62DyKKR.claimed_gains: Stronger models reduce token usage by up to 80% through the composition affordance.
Age62DyKKR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value making skill creation and reuse directly observable under controlled task difficulty.
Age62DyKKR.main_concern: Skill Mode also changes code execution, batching, storage, and prompting, so the evaluation does not isolate reusable skills from those added capabilities.

UOuWG81SYj.one_liner: Canonical sampling, token-preserving history, and cache eviction mitigate prefix mismatches caused by conversation re-encoding.
UOuWG81SYj.problem: Rendering conversation history as text and re-tokenizing can change token prefixes, wasting prefill computation and stranding KV-cache branches.
UOuWG81SYj.method: The study distinguishes re-encoding drift from template-induced history rewriting and integrates three mitigations into vLLM. CG-Recheck constrains sampling to re-encoding-stable sequences, token-level history preserves earlier token IDs, and DriftEvict targets drift-related KV-cache waste.
UOuWG81SYj.key_idea: Preserve canonical token sequences and original history IDs while adapting cache eviction to branches stranded by token-prefix drift.
UOuWG81SYj.evidence: Characterization spans six open models, three conversation datasets, and four languages, with vLLM serving tests measuring cache hits, TTFT, throughput, and output quality.
UOuWG81SYj.claimed_gains: Re-encoding breaks prefixes in 4.6%–90.8% of requests at temperature 1.0, history rebuilding costs 4×–23× the prefill needed for new content, and stranded branches add 10%–122% to the live context's footprint.
UOuWG81SYj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value systematic measurement of a practical serving inefficiency and its prefill and KV-memory costs.
UOuWG81SYj.main_concern: Serving evaluations cover limited models and workload conditions, leaving deployment behavior under broader history changes and timing patterns unclear.

Zo2ENzmYae.one_liner: Adaptive contraction of RoPE phase deviations in visual-source boundary keys reduces position-dependent source preference.
Zo2ENzmYae.problem: Multi-image VLM predictions can depend on source position rather than correctly associating visual evidence with its source.
Zo2ENzmYae.method: CBPC analyzes shared and source-specific components of boundary-token keys and selectively contracts RoPE-induced phase deviations while preserving their cross-source mean. Native visual-key-centroid statistics set an input- and layer-dependent correction strength without training or strength search.
Zo2ENzmYae.key_idea: Contract source-dependent RoPE phase deviations in boundary keys using visual-key-centroid statistics while preserving the cross-source mean.
Zo2ENzmYae.evidence: Tests use Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5, and Molmo2-O models across Mantis, MuirBench, MIRB, and QBench2, including counterfactual phase reassignment and image reorderings.
Zo2ENzmYae.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the boundary-key analysis and the lightweight adaptive intervention motivated by position-dependent source preference.
Zo2ENzmYae.main_concern: The choice of visual-key-centroid variance as a bound for phase correction lacks a convincing justification.

k9CFCbiEdx.one_liner: Outcome-calibrated teachers allocate visual-state capacity across reasoning steps and distill budget-conditioned generation policies.
k9CFCbiEdx.problem: Fixed visual capacity or reconstruction-based allocation can misprice intermediate visual states whose downstream utility varies across reasoning steps.
k9CFCbiEdx.method: VisCal-Ext distills hindsight allocations into a controller while freezing the backbone. VisCal-OPD inserts capacity actions before visual generation and jointly distills capacity, visual, and text policies from a teacher using correct answers and structured cross-step outcome branches.
k9CFCbiEdx.key_idea: Allocate intermediate visual capacity by downstream answer outcomes and jointly distill budget-conditioned capacity, visual-generation, and text policies.
k9CFCbiEdx.evidence: Experiments vary capacity along fixed trajectories, use nuisance and question-image controls, and evaluate four models on eight transfer benchmarks disjoint from post-training data.
k9CFCbiEdx.claimed_gains: VisCal-OPD improves matched-budget accuracy by 5.14 percentage points over released models and matches their accuracy with an estimated 65.1% fewer visual tokens.
k9CFCbiEdx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the evidence that reconstruction fidelity differs from answer utility and the controlled evaluation of utility-based joint allocation.
k9CFCbiEdx.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate adaptive allocation from capacity-varied training or separate visual-generator improvements from text-policy updates.

HB0EaPsXbg.one_liner: Cluster-centered bilinear patch aggregation and determinantal subset selection improve cross-generator AI-generated image detection.
HB0EaPsXbg.problem: Vision foundation model detectors relying on the global CLS token overfit high-level image semantics and concentrate on a few salient patches, overlooking forensic cues across the rest of the image.
HB0EaPsXbg.method: Adaptive Evidence Selection (AES) applies Cluster-centered Bilinear Aggregation (CBA) to model within-cluster patch variations around cluster means and suppress shared semantic content. Determinantal Evidence Selection (DES) then selects a subset of cluster descriptors balancing forensic class relevance and feature diversity.
HB0EaPsXbg.key_idea: Subtract patch-cluster means via bilinear aggregation to suppress shared semantics, then select relevant and diverse cluster descriptors using determinantal selection.
HB0EaPsXbg.evidence: Generalization experiments and hyperparameter studies evaluate AES across seven public AI-generated image detection benchmarks covering diverse diffusion generators.
HB0EaPsXbg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly diagnoses semantic shortcuts and few-patch bias in foundation-model CLS tokens, pairing each issue with a targeted module tested across seven benchmarks.
HB0EaPsXbg.main_concern: Reviewers question whether subtracting cluster means genuinely separates semantics from forensic traces, note missing adapter and feature-fusion implementation details, and cite unclarified novelty over recent relevance-diversity detectors.

XNuDY8qrkJ.one_liner: Separated execution, independent analyses, and targeted data synthesis let agents iteratively revise supervised fine-tuning data recipes.
XNuDY8qrkJ.problem: Single-agent fine-tuning research can collapse into repetitive data reweighting as execution output consumes its context.
XNuDY8qrkJ.method: AutoSFT uses a meta agent to separate execution from analysis, collect independent proposals, and invoke synthesis for capabilities absent from the data pool. Comparisons hold the base model, trainer, and training budget fixed.
XNuDY8qrkJ.key_idea: Separate execution output from analytical context and combine independent data-revision proposals with synthesis for missing capabilities.
XNuDY8qrkJ.evidence: Instruction-following and coding experiments compare system components, agent traces, and concrete data interventions under controlled training settings.
XNuDY8qrkJ.claimed_gains: The executor halves context loss, analysis adds +6.5 IFEval, synthesis adds +3.4 IFEval and +2.9 IFBench, and coding analysis adds +3.7 MBPP+ over a single agent.
XNuDY8qrkJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the detailed agent traces and component studies showing how data interventions affect fine-tuning performance.
XNuDY8qrkJ.main_concern: Reviewers agree that unmatched analysis instructions and inference budgets prevent isolating the benefit of multi-agent organization.

LMosxcPHLj.one_liner: Unified comparisons and mask ablations characterize sparse fine-tuning as task-capacity allocation plus preservation of pretrained parameters.
LMosxcPHLj.problem: Different neuron-selection criteria, update locations, schedules, and ratios obscure why sparse fine-tuning can outperform full fine-tuning.
LMosxcPHLj.method: The study compares representative sparse fine-tuning methods on mathematical reasoning and code generation, using full fine-tuning as a reference. Ablations examine selection and update choices to distinguish capacity allocation from regularization.
LMosxcPHLj.key_idea: Update task-critical neurons while pinning unselected parameters to pretrained values, combining capacity allocation with regularization.
LMosxcPHLj.evidence: The abstract reports nine methods across model families, scales, and tasks, with ablations of update ratios, locations, and mask construction.
LMosxcPHLj.claimed_gains: Sparse methods improve over full fine-tuning by 2.1 points on average while retaining 96–109% of the base model's general capability.
LMosxcPHLj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unified empirical comparison and ablations on neuron selection and forgetting.
LMosxcPHLj.main_concern: Reviewers question the coverage and justification of the selected methods, including limited comparisons with other parameter-efficient approaches.

J8LcYQLXpY.one_liner: Selective removal of influential reasoning sentences aims to hinder student distillation while preserving teacher answers and readable traces.
J8LcYQLXpY.problem: Broad perturbations used for antidistillation visibly degrade reasoning traces, allowing adversaries to detect and filter them.
J8LcYQLXpY.method: TARS frames antidistillation as a detectability-constrained max-min game and removes semantically redundant thought anchors from completed traces. Sentence categories and attention scores guide selection without teacher retraining or a proxy student.
J8LcYQLXpY.key_idea: Delete semantically redundant but influential reasoning sentences selected by category and attention while retaining the teacher's final answer.
J8LcYQLXpY.evidence: MATH and GSM8K experiments examine student learning, trace-quality measures, and random-deletion controls.
J8LcYQLXpY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical appeal of post-generation editing that needs no proxy student and preserves final answers.
J8LcYQLXpY.main_concern: Reviewers find that the central claim of low detectability lacks direct detector testing and convincing trace-quality evidence at effective deletion budgets.

bJHuhRxqDt.one_liner: Target-whitened residual spectra reveal prediction directions worse than the target mean while excluding architecture-forced unit eigenvalues.
bJHuhRxqDt.problem: Average prediction error can hide directions where a representation predictor performs worse than a constant mean predictor.
bJHuhRxqDt.method: Spectral unit tests whiten residual second moments by target covariance and measure excess eigenvalues above one as regret mass. LayerNorm-aware rank bounds identify structurally forced unit-eigenvalue plateaus that the audit excludes.
bJHuhRxqDt.key_idea: Whiten residual second moments by target covariance and inspect excess eigenvalues after excluding rank-forced unit plateaus.
bJHuhRxqDt.evidence: Tests cover five public checkpoints, injected faults transferred from I-JEPA to V-JEPA and V-JEPA2, STL-10 splits, and image-set head-selection experiments.
bJHuhRxqDt.claimed_gains: The gate flags 118 of 120 faulted splits and 3 of 200 healthy splits, transferred rules type 93 of 99 faults, and the official I-JEPA head has 2.2 times the ridge head's mean regret mass.
bJHuhRxqDt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the theoretical treatment of architecture-forced spectral structure and the directional view beyond average error.
bJHuhRxqDt.main_concern: Reviewers question whether spectral diagnostics change practical decisions beyond simpler scalar or non-spectral measurements.

x85McBoKDJ.one_liner: Input statistics and output-gradient weighting direct low-rank quantization corrections toward errors that change vision-language model answers.
x85McBoKDJ.problem: A limited low-rank correction budget cannot repair every quantization error, and reconstruction quality need not preserve final answers.
x85McBoKDJ.method: OQER reconstructs quantization residuals using both input-activation statistics and the second moment of an output gradient. The output weighting prioritizes directions that move the full-precision teacher's answer.
x85McBoKDJ.key_idea: Weight low-rank residual reconstruction on both input activations and answer-sensitive output gradients.
x85McBoKDJ.evidence: Experiments use POPE and MME with LLaVA-1.5-7B, LLaVA-1.5-13B, and Qwen2.5-VL-7B, including MBQ and QIG quantizers and matched correction storage.
x85McBoKDJ.claimed_gains: At rank 64 and +0.4 bits/weight on 3-bit LLaVA-1.5-7B, OQER removes 57.5% and 33.1% of teacher disagreements on POPE and MME versus 34.3% and 16.6% for activation weighting, while rank 32 still exceeds activation-weighted rank 64.
x85McBoKDJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the decision-focused correction objective and controlled evidence for fidelity repair at equal storage.
x85McBoKDJ.main_concern: Reviewers agree that greater teacher agreement does not consistently improve downstream task performance.

OLS3NKUhWz.one_liner: Consensus residuals score expert replaceability for training-free mixture-of-experts pruning with survivor renormalization and router refill.
OLS3NKUhWz.problem: MoE storage remains large despite sparse activation, and usage or output magnitude alone does not measure deletion damage.
OLS3NKUhWz.method: RAZOR measures expert-output deviations from the original weighted mixture and derives exact single-deletion effects at fixed layer inputs. Calibration-token scores support budgeted pruning without gradients or recovery training.
OLS3NKUhWz.key_idea: Rank experts by consensus-residual deletion damage accounting for survivor renormalization and router-selected replacement.
OLS3NKUhWz.evidence: Four MoE backbones undergo nine-task evaluations at 25% and 50% expert removal, with matched REAP comparisons and output-distribution and generation analyses.
OLS3NKUhWz.claimed_gains: RAZOR has the highest evaluated nine-task macro average in all eight settings, exceeds matched REAP by 2.12–5.59 points, and wins all 36 paired task comparisons.
OLS3NKUhWz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value training-free pruning and the analyses of deletion effects, output distributions, and generation behavior.
OLS3NKUhWz.main_concern: Reviewers question whether single-expert scores capture interactions when many experts and possible replacements are removed together.

DOxBg8EuRC.one_liner: Information-equivalent input formats reverse encoder rankings by changing how architectures access positional information.
DOxBg8EuRC.problem: Matching input information does not ensure that encoder performance differences isolate architecture under a fixed learning protocol.
DOxBg8EuRC.method: The study distinguishes declared information from its architecture-specific input realization. It varies how identical occupied-cell sets populate native encoder inputs while fixing training and comparator settings.
DOxBg8EuRC.key_idea: Hold occupied-cell information fixed while changing its realization in native encoder fields, including coordinate accessibility.
DOxBg8EuRC.evidence: Camera-LiDAR correspondence experiments on RADIATE and Boreas audit all 21,435 validation frames and include five-seed comparisons and coordinate controls.
DOxBg8EuRC.claimed_gains: SparseConv3D changes from trailing the RADIATE raster comparator by 0.0787 P@1 to leading by 0.0522, with the second-dataset comparison changing from −0.0115 to +0.0618.
DOxBg8EuRC.reviewer_consensus: The substantive positive reviews agree that careful information audits and controlled experiments establish reproducible encoder-ranking reversals.
DOxBg8EuRC.main_concern: The broad architectural interpretation rests on a narrow correspondence task where coordinate access and known sparse-convolution properties may explain the reversal.

CRRTltvgfR.one_liner: Controlled scaffold changes test RL transfer, while verified Hanabi belief-state training probes reasoning gains beyond its objective.
CRRTltvgfR.problem: It remains unclear whether language-agent RL learns transferable task knowledge or depends on inference-time support.
CRRTltvgfR.method: The study varies task knowledge and reasoning scaffolds in Hanabi and K across models. FIREWORKS supplies 10K deterministically verified Hanabi belief-state transitions for additional RL transfer experiments.
CRRTltvgfR.key_idea: Hold tasks fixed while varying supplied knowledge and reasoning support, then test transfer from verified belief-state training.
CRRTltvgfR.evidence: Experiments span Hanabi and K, multiple model sizes and families, and QWEN3-4B-INSTRUCT-2507 training on FIREWORKS with non-Hanabi reasoning tests.
CRRTltvgfR.claimed_gains: Knowledge support yields +1.75 before and +2.55 after RL in Hanabi; FIREWORKS training improves supported gameplay by +4.3 points and non-Hanabi Pass@8 from 0.15 to 0.37.
CRRTltvgfR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value controlled investigation of scaffold-dependent RL transfer across multiple settings.
CRRTltvgfR.main_concern: Removing knowledge from prompts does not isolate failure to internalize knowledge from prompt shift or retrieval failure.

LBwSX8MJrz.one_liner: Simulation-trained policies use joint-state histories to find and insert unseen pegs through proprioceptively sensed contact.
LBwSX8MJrz.problem: Precise assembly must locate small openings despite unknown peg and hole poses and uncertain grasps.
LBwSX8MJrz.method: A blind RL insertion policy observes recent joint positions, velocities, and actions, training over randomized parts, grasps, and contacts. A procedural assembly generator preserves millimeter clearances for simulation at scale.
LBwSX8MJrz.key_idea: Infer contact and insertion progress from joint-motion histories learned across randomized simulated assemblies.
LBwSX8MJrz.evidence: Simulation comparisons with visual and scripted policies accompany zero-shot real-robot insertion across different shapes and sizes.
LBwSX8MJrz.claimed_gains: The policy inserts pegs of different shapes and sizes in 74% of real-robot trials.
LBwSX8MJrz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the zero-shot real-world demonstration of varied-part assembly using only joint-derived feedback.
LBwSX8MJrz.main_concern: Unequal privileged-critic information and auxiliary supervision confound the claimed generalization advantage over visual policies.

g72scTiE66.one_liner: Learnable matrix multipliers adapt effective feature scales separately from weight-decay-constrained parameter norms during language-model pretraining.
g72scTiE66.problem: Weight decay can restrain norm growth at suboptimal matrix scales despite the usefulness of separately learned normalization gains.
g72scTiE66.method: LRMs add scalar or featurewise multipliers across model matrices while retaining muP learning-rate transfer. Controlled optimizer studies and an Adam LM-head analysis connect these scales to norm regulation.
g72scTiE66.key_idea: Separate effective matrix scales from weight-decayed parameter norms by learning multipliers across and within layers.
g72scTiE66.evidence: Adam and Muon experiments include 20-paired-seed placement ablations and long pretraining across dense, hybrid, and mixture-of-experts architectures.
g72scTiE66.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the systematic multiplier-placement study and empirical benefits across architectures and optimizers.
g72scTiE66.main_concern: The simplified Adam-head theory does not establish the mechanism behind broader backbone and Muon improvements.

ew00dR8zsB.one_liner: Resolution-consistent molecular mass grids supervise coarse-to-fine generation of three-dimensional molecular fields.
ew00dR8zsB.problem: Small molecules lack a scale definition for organizing generation from coarse structure to fine detail.
ew00dR8zsB.method: ScaleMol defines molecular mass grids whose regional element content aggregates exactly across resolutions and predicts these fields hierarchically. Reference molecules can condition generation at different resolutions without additional training.
ew00dR8zsB.key_idea: Represent molecular scale by field resolution with exact aggregation, then supervise predictions from coarse element distributions to finer spatial detail.
ew00dR8zsB.evidence: QM9 and GEOM-Drugs experiments compare stability with field-based generators and ablate mass grids and coarse-to-fine prediction.
ew00dR8zsB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the interpretable scale hierarchy and empirical ablations of hierarchical molecular generation.
ew00dR8zsB.main_concern: Grid-based mass fields do not explicitly encode molecular connectivity or natural structural hierarchies, raising concerns for complex molecules.

G6HRjMzJh5.one_liner: Hidden-state probes estimate sufficient sparse-attention budgets before decoding and adjust them along reasoning trajectories.
G6HRjMzJh5.problem: Adaptive sparse-attention methods leave pre-selection budgets manual and can introduce irregular posterior-pruning computation.
G6HRjMzJh5.method: SABER trains lightweight internal probes to predict whether candidate budgets suffice and selects the smallest suitable budget. Prompt-state allocation and ongoing trajectory-aware updates share this framework.
G6HRjMzJh5.key_idea: Probe intermediate hidden states for candidate-budget sufficiency and route decoding to the smallest sufficient sparse-attention tier.
G6HRjMzJh5.evidence: Long-context and reasoning benchmarks compare against fixed-budget, top-p, and trainable sparse-attention baselines.
G6HRjMzJh5.claimed_gains: SABER reduces average selector budget by up to 67.6% while preserving accuracy relative to the reported baselines.
G6HRjMzJh5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value upstream hidden-state budget prediction and dynamic adjustment during long reasoning.
G6HRjMzJh5.main_concern: The budget-routing scheme offers limited conceptual advance over existing adaptive computation-allocation methods.

AzKzbKycKI.one_liner: Spectral recalibration of functional connectivity defines stronger phenotype predictors and similarity targets for small fMRI encoders.
AzKzbKycKI.problem: Tested brain foundation models underperform functional-connectivity KRR, whose eigenvalue weighting may also be poorly suited to phenotype prediction.
AzKzbKycKI.method: A spectral filter recalibrates each subject's connectivity eigenvalues. A small encoder then learns recording-snippet embeddings whose pairwise similarities match recalibrated connectomes.
AzKzbKycKI.key_idea: Flatten functional-connectivity eigenspectra and train snippet embeddings to reproduce the resulting pairwise similarity geometry.
AzKzbKycKI.evidence: Evaluation spans 5 datasets, 11 parcellations, and 6 targets; encoder pretraining uses about 4,000 hours from 162 datasets and comparisons with 6 published BFMs.
AzKzbKycKI.claimed_gains: The encoder matches the best of the 6 tested published BFMs with an order of magnitude fewer parameters.
AzKzbKycKI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple spectral transform and consistent phenotype-prediction gains across datasets.
AzKzbKycKI.main_concern: Incomplete baseline coverage and uncertain reproduction of some brain foundation models weaken the broader comparative conclusions.

Ju0qQRbtl1.one_liner: Variance in successor reachability scores guides when action-chunked robot policies can skip test-time search.
Ju0qQRbtl1.problem: Searching at every robot decision is expensive, and common gating signals may not consistently predict search benefit.
Ju0qQRbtl1.method: Successor-channel criticality measures variance in reachability scores across candidate successors using a resettable simulator without reward or search-benefit labels. A distilled network combines this signal with a cheap gate for deployed search decisions.
Ju0qQRbtl1.key_idea: Estimate how much future reachable-object-position spread varies across candidate actions and use low variance to skip search.
Ju0qQRbtl1.evidence: Paired per-state interventions cover fourteen datasets from three benchmark suites and an additional dataset in a second physics engine, with closed-loop gating tests.
Ju0qQRbtl1.claimed_gains: Skipping estimated-zero-criticality decisions avoids about half of searches while giving up 19.9% of net benefit, and adding distilled criticality to a cheap gate raises LIBERO success by 4.2 percentage points with 20.5% fewer search calls.
Ju0qQRbtl1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the broad paired-intervention evaluation and its evidence that common gating signals change direction across datasets.
Ju0qQRbtl1.main_concern: Dependence on resettable simulators, privileged state, and search evaluators leaves observation-only and real-hardware deployment unestablished.

EIZQHoELa4.one_liner: Base-sensitive allocation and multiplication-aligned quantization compress fine-tuning deltas while retaining scale-based task adaptation.
EIZQHoELa4.problem: Compact serving of many fine-tuned models requires delta compression that preserves accuracy, inference speed, and adaptability together.
EIZQHoELa4.method: ADE allocates compressed parameters using module-output sensitivity including base weights, and aligns quantization groups with matrix multiplication. Tunable scaling factors support adaptation on compressed deltas and fold into existing inference scales.
EIZQHoELa4.key_idea: Allocate delta capacity by base-aware sensitivity and align low-bit factor groups along the matrix contraction axis.
EIZQHoELa4.evidence: Evaluation covers six fine-tuned models, implemented and timed inference kernels, and serving configurations with up to 16 models sharing one base.
EIZQHoELa4.claimed_gains: At the same memory budget, ADE is up to 3.9% relatively more accurate than the best prior method and reduces time per output token by 13–49% relative to the fastest prior delta compression method.
EIZQHoELa4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the compatible compression, low-bit inference, and adaptation design and its implemented kernels.
EIZQHoELa4.main_concern: The latency evaluation does not cleanly establish gains for realistic mixed-model serving independently of custom-kernel advantages.

NbOb94qWwu.one_liner: Distilled answer-sensitivity scores select question-relevant visual tokens while spatial coverage and feature diversity limit redundancy.
NbOb94qWwu.problem: Common visual-token importance proxies may miss answer-relevant representations or spend scarce token budgets on redundant regions.
NbOb94qWwu.method: Ansight distills Gradient × Activation scores from a frozen VLM's generated answers into a lightweight question-conditioned selector before the language model. Selection combines predicted relevance with regional coverage and global feature diversity.
NbOb94qWwu.key_idea: Train a question-conditioned selector on answer-derived Gradient × Activation attributions, then enforce spatial coverage and feature diversity.
NbOb94qWwu.evidence: Experiments span five backbones, nine recent baselines, three retention budgets, answer preservation, paired intervals, and end-to-end timing.
NbOb94qWwu.claimed_gains: Ansight leads in 13 of 15 backbone–budget settings and reduces the strongest prior method's performance loss by 26%; on LLaVA-NeXT-7B it retains 94.9% performance with 5% of visual tokens and 8.6× less computation.
NbOb94qWwu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize broad empirical evaluation and useful performance retention with a lightweight selector.
NbOb94qWwu.main_concern: Incomplete closest-work comparisons and modified baseline implementations weaken confidence in the reported margins.

pzgLv2tlnf.one_liner: Observation-channel matrices characterize identifiable latent averages and support estimators with optimal leading finite-sample error.
pzgLv2tlnf.problem: Coarsened observations merge hidden states, obscuring which latent properties remain recoverable and their data requirements.
pzgLv2tlnf.method: The paper gives a matrix-based identifiability test for linear latent targets and constructs an estimator with an explicit risk expansion and matching lower bound. It extends analysis to finite sets of unknown channels, establishing impossibility and adaptive recovery conditions.
pzgLv2tlnf.key_idea: Use the observation-channel matrix to characterize recoverable latent functionals and construct minimum-variance estimating weights.
pzgLv2tlnf.evidence: Identifiability, minimax risk, asymptotic efficiency, and channel-uncertainty results accompany simulations and a semi-synthetic census study with randomized response.
