pzgLv2tlnf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unified theoretical treatment of recoverability and estimation efficiency under discrete observation channels.
pzgLv2tlnf.main_concern: Positioning against established inverse-problem, measurement-error, and statistical-efficiency results does not clearly establish the new contribution.

kmk4ZyJhQ5.one_liner: Differentiating deployed calibration thresholds during training optimizes early VLA failure alarms under per-condition error constraints.
kmk4ZyJhQ5.problem: Classification-trained failure scores can alarm too late when deployment thresholds must control false alarms in every operating condition.
kmk4ZyJhQ5.method: Calibration in the Loop computes condition-wise reference-success order statistics and their maximum inside the training objective. Dual ascent enforces per-condition constraints while optimizing early detection under the threshold used at deployment.
kmk4ZyJhQ5.key_idea: Backpropagate through the deployed maximum-of-condition calibration threshold while enforcing separate false-alarm constraints by dual ascent.
kmk4ZyJhQ5.evidence: Held-out LIBERO-Plus condition banks evaluate multiple VLA policies and detector architectures, with marginal and high-confidence deployment guarantees.
kmk4ZyJhQ5.claimed_gains: For π_{0.5} on LIBERO-Spatial, CIL raises early detection within tolerance from 39.3% to 59.2%.
kmk4ZyJhQ5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that matching failure-monitor training to calibrated deployment thresholds addresses a meaningful detection problem.
kmk4ZyJhQ5.main_concern: Guarantees require representative data within predefined conditions and do not cover unseen shifts or distribution changes inside a condition.

iFczOdmwjf.one_liner: Transition-token prediction skips unnecessary replanning, while confidence routing sends uncertain subtask decisions to a stronger planner.
iFczOdmwjf.problem: Hierarchical robot policies waste time on repeated expensive planning or make errors when relying entirely on lightweight planners.
iFczOdmwjf.method: SPACE first predicts a binary subtask-transition token and stops decoding when the current subtask should continue. On transitions, a local planner proposes the next subtask and a router uses token probabilities and alternative-prediction differences to decide whether to call a frontier planner.
iFczOdmwjf.key_idea: Separate the decision to update a subtask from the decision to route its prediction to a stronger planner.
iFczOdmwjf.evidence: Experiments cover RoboMME, RoboDojo, and three real-world manipulation tasks, with component ablations.
iFczOdmwjf.claimed_gains: SPACE raises success from 40.6% to 50.3% on RoboMME and from 28.6% to 38.5% on RoboDojo, while reducing high-level planning time by 60.7% and 31.6%, respectively.
iFczOdmwjf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard selective high-level planning as practically useful and recognize its success–latency benefits.
iFczOdmwjf.main_concern: The combination of established routing and early-exit mechanisms lacks sufficient analysis of the central Hold decision's reliability.

YFF6GA74hD.one_liner: A reward-trained policy allocates variable latent-token budgets to retrieved memories before injecting them into agent generation.
YFF6GA74hD.problem: Fixed textual or latent memory interfaces do not match query-dependent memory utility and can waste context on noisy evidence.
YFF6GA74hD.method: ElasticMem creates an offline memory bank with retrieval keys and content caches, retrieves from the reasoner's hidden state, and assigns each memory a learned latent budget. Selected states become soft memory tokens, with memory use trained through group-relative policy optimization on task rewards.
YFF6GA74hD.key_idea: Learn how many latent states to inject for each retrieved memory using downstream task rewards.
YFF6GA74hD.evidence: MemorySuite evaluations cover memory-intensive QA and ALFWorld control on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, with allocation-policy ablations.
YFF6GA74hD.claimed_gains: Across the two backbones, ElasticMem reports weighted-average QA accuracy improvements of 26.2% and 24.6% and ALFWorld success-rate improvements of 66.3% and 27.2%.
YFF6GA74hD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find learned memory-capacity allocation meaningful and recognize consistent gains across QA and embodied tasks.
YFF6GA74hD.main_concern: Comparisons do not isolate elastic allocation under matched total token budgets, leaving gains from allocation versus added resources unclear.

zfaWxDdB3P.one_liner: Asymmetric log-SNR boundary closures replace diffusion samplers' first and last updates while preserving the interior solver.
zfaWxDdB3P.problem: Finite-interval diffusion solvers leave endpoint truncation errors that interior discretization improvements do not address.
zfaWxDdB3P.method: Endpoint-complete sampling uses a signal-prediction closure at the low-SNR limit and a noise-prediction closure at the high-SNR limit. DPM-FS and DPM-LS replace the first and last updates, supported by endpoint analysis and connections to generalized velocity prediction.
zfaWxDdB3P.key_idea: Treat the low-SNR endpoint with signal prediction and the high-SNR endpoint with noise prediction instead of ordinary interior steps.
zfaWxDdB3P.evidence: Experiments on CIFAR-10, AFHQv2, FFHQ, and ImageNet compare pretrained models, solvers, and analytic or optimized schedules.
zfaWxDdB3P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize improvements across multiple sampling settings and the usefulness of endpoint-specific treatment with existing models.
zfaWxDdB3P.main_concern: Schedule-optimization differences make it difficult to isolate the gains from the boundary updates themselves.

oyWlFKtCpZ.one_liner: External SQL search state and periodic context rebuilding let relational feature agents discard full interaction histories.
oyWlFKtCpZ.problem: Relational feature-search agents repeatedly process growing histories of SQL candidates and results that could be selectively reused.
oyWlFKtCpZ.method: StepRel stores database knowledge, the current exact SQL program, and search evidence outside the conversation. It applies local program edits and periodically reconstructs context from retained knowledge and selected evidence.
oyWlFKtCpZ.key_idea: Preserve the executable incumbent and reusable search evidence externally, then rebuild only the context needed for local SQL revision.
oyWlFKtCpZ.evidence: Evaluation spans 18 RelBench tasks and four LLM backbones, comparing predictive performance, stability, token usage, and selected component ablations.
oyWlFKtCpZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find external search-state management a practical response to growing SQL-agent context costs and value the broad evaluation.
oyWlFKtCpZ.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the contribution of evidence selection and context reconstruction within the combined system.

ocT8JYyJ19.one_liner: Augmented Sparse Encoding Models predict language-related brain responses using hierarchical sparse autoencoder features and explicit surprisal predictors.
ocT8JYyJ19.problem: Relating dense language-model representations to brain activity gives limited interpretable explanations of the features encoded by language cortex.
ocT8JYyJ19.method: The framework replaces dense LM hidden states with hierarchically organized sparse autoencoder features and includes surprisal as a separate predictor. Encoding analyses interpret voxel populations and examine feature sharing across language-network regions.
ocT8JYyJ19.key_idea: Hierarchical sparse LM features and an explicit surprisal term serve as interpretable predictors of voxel responses.
ocT8JYyJ19.evidence: A 7T fMRI dataset includes eight participants listening to 200 linguistically diverse sentences, with nested cross-validation, stability analyses, and replication on independent datasets.
ocT8JYyJ19.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value interpretable brain-response explanations and substantial supporting analyses, including replication across fMRI datasets.
ocT8JYyJ19.main_concern: Voxel and feature-selection procedures limit confidence in generalization, particularly when source features are selected before cross-validation over stimuli.

6Gj1j15ZMk.one_liner: Envelope sampling allocates expert labels to recalibrate surrogate rewards before post-training against them.
6Gj1j15ZMk.problem: Base-model sampling can miss rare outputs that an imperfect judge overrates, enabling reward hacking after optimization.
6Gj1j15ZMk.method: The method derives an envelope distribution minimizing a worst-case coverage factor for an L2 reward class around the judge. Rejection sampling or modified-reward fine-tuning generates outputs for expert labeling and reward recalibration.
6Gj1j15ZMk.key_idea: Choose a recalibration-sampling distribution minimizing worst-case coverage for rewards in an L2 ball around the judge.
6Gj1j15ZMk.evidence: Regret and coverage analysis, a closed-form L2 envelope, and clinical-note and controlled-sycophancy experiments support the approach.
6Gj1j15ZMk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the limited-label reward-recalibration problem and theoretical connection between calibration error, coverage, and regret.
6Gj1j15ZMk.main_concern: Minimizing envelope coverage is not shown to guarantee better regret or practical performance than simpler sampling alternatives.

mkiSHfWgb4.one_liner: BURST removes target-support examples through federated unlearning while strengthening interference examples to flip selected predictions.
mkiSHfWgb4.problem: Trusting client-issued unlearning requests lets adversaries manipulate prediction integrity while preserving much of the global model utility.
mkiSHfWgb4.method: BURST constructs support and interference sets from public auxiliary data and includes them in federated training. During unlearning, it requests support removal and increases interference influence to induce target misclassification.
mkiSHfWgb4.key_idea: Withdraw examples supporting a target prediction while increasing the influence of adversarial interference during federated unlearning.
mkiSHfWgb4.evidence: Federated-unlearning attack experiments include CIFAR-10, comparisons with existing attacks, and attack-construction efficiency measurements.
mkiSHfWgb4.claimed_gains: BURST achieves an attack success rate of 91.43% on CIFAR-10 while reducing global model accuracy by 5.66%.
mkiSHfWgb4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value exposing targeted prediction-integrity risks from malicious unlearning requests and find the attack mechanism coherent.
mkiSHfWgb4.main_concern: The FedEraser implementation does not clearly establish how the stated attacker can remove support records while modifying reconstruction-time interference.

NbxYmbRMDE.one_liner: Generates and verifies simulated physics worlds automatically to train LLM discovery agents via multi-turn GRPO.
NbxYmbRMDE.problem: Scientific discovery in physics requires iterative experiment design, hypothesis revision, and law inference, which lack automated interactive training environments and verifiers.
NbxYmbRMDE.method: Discover-Many-Worlds combines LLM-driven environment construction, procedural simulation, and automated verification testing to generate physics worlds across multiple difficulty levels without human intervention. A 4B-parameter Qwen agent is trained with multi-turn GRPO inside these interactive environments to run experiments and infer physical laws.
NbxYmbRMDE.key_idea: Combine LLM-driven world construction, procedural simulation, and verification testing to generate interactive physics environments for multi-turn GRPO agent training.
NbxYmbRMDE.evidence: Evaluated by training Qwen3-4B with GRPO on generated two-particle physics worlds and testing on DiscoverPhysics alongside transfer benchmarks including NewtonBench, HeroBench, GravityBench, and LiveCodeBench.
NbxYmbRMDE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing scientific discovery around interactive experimentation in generated physics worlds is well motivated and produces clear behavioral improvements and fewer execution errors on DiscoverPhysics.
NbxYmbRMDE.main_concern: Reviewers note missing ablations isolating LLM-generated worlds from template-based worlds, potential Claude family bias in reward judging, and mixed benchmark-dependent transfer beyond DiscoverPhysics.

cjsI0gAGU0.one_liner: Extracts attention-sink, residual-alignment, and trajectory-geometry descriptors in one forward pass to predict LLM answer correctness.
cjsI0gAGU0.problem: Output-level LLM confidence signals are sensitive to prompts and decoding, while generic hidden-state probes ignore the distinct functional structure of Transformer components.
cjsI0gAGU0.method: The estimator extracts three mechanistic descriptors from a frozen Transformer in a single forward pass: Attention Sink Signature, Knowledge Response Alignment between attention and feed-forward residual updates, and Residual Trajectory Geometry. A lightweight branch-attentive probe fuses these descriptors against answer correctness labels.
cjsI0gAGU0.key_idea: Fuse single-pass attention-sink statistics, attention-to-FFN directional alignment, and residual-stream trajectory geometry through a lightweight branch-attentive probe on a frozen LLM backbone.
cjsI0gAGU0.evidence: Evaluated on AUROC, ECE, and cross-domain transfer across five question-answering benchmarks (including GSM8K) and four models from the Qwen2.5 and LLaMA-3.1 families.
cjsI0gAGU0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extracting low-dimensional component-structured descriptors from a single forward pass is computationally cheap, easy to implement, and transfers well across QA domains.
cjsI0gAGU0.main_concern: Reviewers point out that extracting features from the final prompt token before generation estimates prompt-level success probability rather than answer-conditioned confidence, alongside missing P(IK) and recalibrated baselines.

4svy1XuEAa.one_liner: Quantifies source energy in operator-unobservable directions via prior share and benchmarks hallucination across nine diffusion-prior solvers.
4svy1XuEAa.problem: In reference-free scientific imaging, small measurement residuals fail to detect diffusion-prior reconstruction hallucinations occurring in directions left unresolved by the forward operator and noise.
4svy1XuEAa.method: The authors define prior share as the fraction of source energy lying in directions left unobservable by a forward operator and noise level, computed from the operator and representative source data without a test reference. They construct the PriorShare benchmark spanning weak-lensing mass mapping, galaxy PSF deconvolution, wide-field BioSR fluorescence microscopy, multi-coil MRI, and black-hole imaging to evaluate nine diffusion-prior solvers.
4svy1XuEAa.key_idea: Measure the fraction of representative source energy lying in operator-and-noise-unobservable directions to diagnose reference-free reconstruction hallucinations in diffusion-prior inverse solvers.
4svy1XuEAa.evidence: Evaluated nine diffusion-prior inverse-problem solvers alongside classical baselines across five scientific imaging tasks: weak-lensing mass mapping, galaxy PSF deconvolution, real BioSR wide-field fluorescence observations, multi-coil MRI, and black-hole imaging.
4svy1XuEAa.claimed_gains: At a share of 72%, one solver reaches a relative residual of 0.6% while 99.95% of its squared reconstruction error lies in the discarded directions.
4svy1XuEAa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the scientific imaging benchmark tasks and classical baselines provide practical empirical coverage for separating measurement fit from recovery of weakly constrained components.
4svy1XuEAa.main_concern: Reviewers question the analytical originality of prior share beyond classical linear null-space arguments and note fragile validation protocols such as single-image hyperparameter tuning and post-hoc test-set filtering.

rRGvKxo4hB.one_liner: Post-trains an all-atom biomolecular trajectory generator with on-policy RL using protein-ligand interfacial expansion rate for screening.
rRGvKxo4hB.problem: Generative molecular dynamics models trained primarily on active protein-ligand complexes inherit biases that weaken active-versus-decoy discrimination in virtual screening.
rRGvKxo4hB.method: ABLE combines an all-atom biomolecular trajectory generator with an on-policy reinforcement learning post-training stage guided by a protein-ligand interfacial expansion rate. Computed as the instantaneous entropy growth of a local interfacial distribution from static cross-docked structures, this signal drives distinct dynamical trajectories for active ligands and decoys without requiring decoy MD simulations.
rRGvKxo4hB.key_idea: Optimize an all-atom trajectory generator via on-policy reinforcement learning rewarded by local protein-ligand interfacial entropy growth using static active and decoy structures.
rRGvKxo4hB.evidence: Evaluated on all-atom trajectory generation for proteins and protein-ligand complexes and on early active-ligand enrichment in virtual screening using static cross-docked structures.
rRGvKxo4hB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that leveraging readily available static active and decoy structures via a computable interfacial expansion signal avoids costly decoy MD simulations when adapting trajectory generators for virtual screening.
rRGvKxo4hB.main_concern: Reviewers question the physical validity of learned decoy escape trajectories and interfacial expansion rates, as well as missing supervised static-structure screening baselines trained on the same active/decoy labels.

C9AJIlyJWA.one_liner: Iteratively distills oldest agent experiences into compact test-time KV memory modules trained alongside frozen earlier cartridges.
C9AJIlyJWA.problem: In-context learning for language model agents degrades and hits finite context limits as interaction history grows, while naive iterative KV-cache compaction suffers from interference across successive compactions and incoming context.
C9AJIlyJWA.method: Accordion repeatedly consolidates an agent's oldest experiences into trained KV memory modules on a frozen base model by generating self-study examples and distilling them into a compact cache initialized with ridge-regularized Attention Matching. Each new KV cartridge is trained jointly alongside frozen earlier modules and varying amounts of subsequent raw context so successive memories compose.
C9AJIlyJWA.key_idea: Repeatedly distill self-study examples from old context into Attention-Matching-initialized KV cartridges trained behind frozen prior modules and varying amounts of subsequent raw context.
C9AJIlyJWA.evidence: Evaluated across QuALITY, Blind Spectrum Monitoring from Continual Learning Bench, and Harvey LAB over corpora of 1M-12M tokens against text-based, weight-based, and KV baselines.
C9AJIlyJWA.claimed_gains: Achieves relative improvements of approximately 13%, 60%, and 18% on QuALITY, Blind Spectrum Monitoring, and Harvey LAB over the strongest evaluated baselines while supporting repeated compaction at 19-23x compression over 1M-12M-token corpora.
C9AJIlyJWA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating survival under appended context from multi-module composability is well posed and that Accordion achieves consistent high-compression gains with stabilized Attention Matching initialization.
C9AJIlyJWA.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing budget-matched comparisons against closely related multi-module KV compaction methods such as Cartridges at Scale (CAS) and C2KV, alongside confounded capacity and compute ablations.

XSQLI6ufkJ.one_liner: Propagates and supervises parameter derivatives along Schrodinger bridge rollouts using a two-rollout mean-response loss.
XSQLI6ufkJ.problem: Fitting observed endpoint distributions with stochastic transport models does not guarantee accurate predictions of how stochastic systems respond to parameter interventions.
XSQLI6ufkJ.method: Tangent Schrodinger Bridge Matching (Tangent-SBM) propagates mechanistic parameter derivatives alongside stochastic bridge trajectories and supervises them against supplied sensitivity targets. For average-response targets, it uses two independent rollouts to match the mean response without penalizing intrinsic trajectory variability.
XSQLI6ufkJ.key_idea: Propagate mechanistic parameter derivatives along stochastic Schrodinger bridge trajectories and supervise mean-response targets with an unbiased two-rollout loss.
XSQLI6ufkJ.evidence: Supported by theoretical bounds linking sensitivity error to finite-change error and decision regret, plus experiments on Gaussian, stochastic double-well, PDEBench reaction-diffusion, and stochastic Navier-Stokes viscosity selection tasks.
XSQLI6ufkJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing distributional endpoint matching from parameter-intervention accuracy is well motivated and that the two-rollout objective cleanly eliminates the variance penalty of single-rollout squared loss.
XSQLI6ufkJ.main_concern: Reviewers note inaccurate high-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes sensitivity and finite-change predictions, incremental technical scope beyond existing derivative supervision and DSBM, and unclear presentation.

aYH3QSudNZ.one_liner: Anchors spectral self-supervised embeddings to persistent simplex frames to prevent rotational drift during continual learning.
aYH3QSudNZ.problem: Spectral geometric self-supervised learning objectives are rotationally invariant, allowing representations to rotate freely and drift into previously learned object manifolds during continual learning.
aYH3QSudNZ.method: Building on Manifold Capacity Theory and MMCR's nuclear-norm objective, GYRO anchors task embeddings to their nearest persistent simplex reference frames directly in embedding space. This constrains global rotational freedom without requiring class labels, teacher distillation networks, or rigid image-to-prototype assignments.
aYH3QSudNZ.key_idea: Constrain rotational invariance in spectral self-supervised objectives by anchoring embedding centroids to persistent simplex geometric reference frames across tasks.
aYH3QSudNZ.evidence: Supported by rotational symmetry analysis of the spectral objective and continual self-supervised learning evaluations against replay, distillation, and regularization baselines.
aYH3QSudNZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that injecting persistent simplex reference frames into MMCR's spectral objective is a simple, label-free modification that improves continual self-supervised stability over replay and regularization baselines.
aYH3QSudNZ.main_concern: Reviewers highlight that selecting hyperparameters using test-set accuracy introduces selection bias, and point out that global orthogonal rotations preserve pairwise geometry and thus do not by themselves explain forgetting.

YrqdIMBukM.one_liner: Generates adversarial-yet-recoverable cultural queries via DualCQ and trains LLMs with principle-informed teacher supervision via CAPME.
YrqdIMBukM.problem: LLMs can accurately identify explicitly stated cultural principles yet frequently violate those same principles during realistic implicit user interactions.
YrqdIMBukM.method: The authors introduce DualCQ, a query generator that jointly optimizes unassisted adherence failure and principle-informed recoverability to build the 10,661-pair CulSafe benchmark. After diagnosing bottlenecks in cultural sensitivity awareness and contextual principle matching, they propose CAPME, which uses a principle-informed teacher to supervise awareness, principle matching, and response generation.
YrqdIMBukM.key_idea: Pair dual-guided generation of unassisted-failing yet principle-recoverable queries with principle-informed teacher supervision over cultural awareness, contextual principle matching, and response generation.
YrqdIMBukM.evidence: Evaluated on the 10,661-pair CulSafe benchmark alongside failure-bottleneck diagnostics and CAPME training experiments across three LLM families (six models).
YrqdIMBukM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating explicit cultural knowledge from implicit behavioral adherence is practically important and that DualCQ's recoverability constraint yields a focused diagnostic benchmark with consistent CAPME gains.
YrqdIMBukM.main_concern: Reviewers question whether synthetic country-level queries capture nuanced real-world cultural context, note unvalidated intermediate awareness and matching failure labels, and observe that awareness-only training sometimes matches or beats joint CAPME.

YoqAhd971A.one_liner: Calibrates VLM attribute annotators on small human-labeled samples to price pseudo-labels via squared Youden index J^2.
YoqAhd971A.problem: Weakly supervised causal representation learning requires human attribute annotations, while substituting VLM pseudo-labels introduces unknown supervision loss prior to training.
YoqAhd971A.method: VLM-Gauge calibrates a vision-language model on a few hundred human-labeled images per attribute to estimate its Youden index J, pricing each VLM label at approximately J^2 human labels. This pre-training price predicts attribute-level representation quality across annotators and guides targeted allocation of human labels to near-chance attributes.
YoqAhd971A.key_idea: Estimate a VLM annotator's Youden index J on a small calibration set and value each pseudo-label as J^2 equivalent human labels.
YoqAhd971A.evidence: Supported by theoretical analysis and experiments with DEAR, CausalVAE, and SCM-VAE on four to twelve CelebA attributes and MPI3D-real across three VLM annotators from two model families.
YoqAhd971A.claimed_gains: A VLM label of Youden index J carries roughly the signal of J^2 human labels, labels from two of three annotators on 17,000 images outperform human labels on 4,000, and weighted human labels on near-chance attributes gain 5.0 points there.
YoqAhd971A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that quantifying the quality-cost trade-off of VLM pseudo-labels for causal representation learning is practically valuable and well connected to controlled fixed-architecture annotator-swap experiments.
YoqAhd971A.main_concern: Reviewers note violations of the class-conditional noise assumption across subgroups, weak mixed-label gains on near-chance attributes in practice, and heavy reliance on CelebA and Qwen annotators.

52Dx21qMeL.one_liner: Uses cell foundation model embeddings to retrieve perturbation measurements in related cells for in-context LLM prediction.
52Dx21qMeL.problem: General-purpose language models lack a direct mechanism to leverage continuous cellular representations from cell foundation models when predicting cell-context-specific perturbation effects.
52Dx21qMeL.method: CellVELA embeds query and reference cells with a cell foundation model to retrieve experimental measurements of the same genetic perturbation in related cell lines, then supplies those records to an LLM at inference time. It evaluates within-target cellular context discrimination by holding each perturbation target fixed across held-out cancer lineages and also tests target-specific reference selection.
52Dx21qMeL.key_idea: Retrieve same-perturbation experimental outcomes from neighbor cells in cell-foundation-model embedding space and condition a language model on them at inference.
52Dx21qMeL.evidence: Evaluated on within-target cancer cell-line dependency discrimination across held-out lineages (DepMap and PerturbQA) against fine-tuned LLMs, kNN similarity voting, and non-LLM readers.
52Dx21qMeL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that within-target evaluation exposes how conventional gene-ranking metrics conflate broadly essential gene priors with true cellular context specificity, and that retrieved-record controls clarify the source of gains.
52Dx21qMeL.main_concern: Reviewers point out that CellVELA adds no measurable accuracy gain over simple kNN voting or linear and tree readers on the same retrieved records, and that fine-tuning baselines face sparse supervision confounds.

Ph27mG8Pfd.one_liner: Pairs LFSR seed-based LLM weight generation with deterministic metadata-free sensitivity-aware bit allocation and bit-flip tamper sensitivity.
Ph27mG8Pfd.problem: Seed-based pseudo-random LLM weight compression allocates bits uniformly across weights, ignoring heterogeneous parameter sensitivity unless costly per-block metadata is stored.
Ph27mG8Pfd.method: SenSeed combines Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) pseudo-random weight generation with calibration-free non-uniform bit allocation that assigns larger bit budgets to sensitive weights. Its decoder deterministically reconstructs the bit-allocation schedule without depending on decoded weights, avoiding per-block metadata while propagating bit-flips across reconstructed weights to aid attack detection.
Ph27mG8Pfd.key_idea: Allocate non-uniform LFSR seed bit budgets by weight sensitivity using a deterministic, weight-independent decoding schedule that requires zero per-block metadata.
Ph27mG8Pfd.evidence: Evaluated on Llama-2-7B, Llama-2-13B, Llama-3-8B, and Mistral-7B for perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, and parameter bit-flip attack detection against SeedLM and quantization baselines.
Ph27mG8Pfd.claimed_gains: Matches 4-bit SeedLM perplexity with 3–6% fewer bits, and at 4 bits/weight reduces perplexity degradation by 23–42% and zero-shot accuracy loss by 27–55% relative to SeedLM.
Ph27mG8Pfd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight the side-information-free deterministic bit-allocation schedule as a clean, storage-saving improvement to seed-based weight compression.
Ph27mG8Pfd.main_concern: Absolute accuracy gains over SeedLM are modest (often trailing AWQ or S-Quant), models above 13B are not tested, and heightened bit-flip sensitivity may act as a fault-tolerance liability.

a0TVQ1Nrg4.one_liner: Constructs LLM activation-steering vectors from paraphrased desired-versus-contrasting natural-language guidelines paired with generic vocabulary or text tokens.
a0TVQ1Nrg4.problem: Activation-steering methods typically require collecting, labeling, and validating large behavior-specific contrastive datasets for every target behavior.
a0TVQ1Nrg4.method: SWAG (Steering With Augmented Guidelines) starts from one pair of natural-language guidelines specifying the desired and contrasting behaviors. It pairs paraphrases of each guideline with filler tokens sampled from the model vocabulary or natural text and extracts steering vectors from the resulting internal activations.
a0TVQ1Nrg4.key_idea: Extract activation-steering directions by contrasting model activations on paraphrased positive and negative behavior guidelines appended with task-independent vocabulary or text tokens.
a0TVQ1Nrg4.evidence: Evaluated across five LLM families, multiple behavioral steering tasks, and three intervention types, including the AxBench benchmark.
a0TVQ1Nrg4.claimed_gains: On the AxBench benchmark, SWAG achieves 93% of the performance of the strongest non-gradient supervised steering baseline without behavior-labeled extraction data.
a0TVQ1Nrg4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate eliminating per-behavior contrastive dataset curation with a simple drop-in steering extraction front-end evaluated across five model families.
a0TVQ1Nrg4.main_concern: Labeled examples—sometimes including evaluation questions—still select steering layers, multipliers, and substrates, undermining the data-free framing while leaving capability and safety side effects under-analyzed.

A5n8QnKTzi.one_liner: Aligns middle-layer target-language MoE routing toward successful English task-expert patterns on correctness-asymmetric parallel examples.
A5n8QnKTzi.problem: Standard multilingual fine-tuning of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs ignores router divergence in middle layers, leaving non-English queries under-routed to shared task-relevant experts.
A5n8QnKTzi.method: RA-MoE partitions parallel examples into four correctness groups (cc/ci/ic/ii) and identifies middle-layer task experts from successful English executions. On examples solved in English but missed in the target language (ci), it aligns target-language routing to match both total routing mass on task experts and relative allocation among them.
A5n8QnKTzi.key_idea: On parallel examples where English succeeds and the target language fails, align middle-layer MoE total and relative task-expert routing mass toward English patterns.
A5n8QnKTzi.evidence: Evaluated across three MoE models, three downstream tasks, and six target languages against standard SFT and routing-aware baselines, with routing-shift and ablation analyses.
A5n8QnKTzi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend leveraging middle-layer cross-lingual task-expert sharing in a well-structured pipeline supported by thorough component ablations and internal routing verification.
A5n8QnKTzi.main_concern: Constructing correctness-filtered parallel (ci) data requires costly upfront inference and yields scarce training examples on stronger languages, while post-tuning English retention and ci-only SFT baselines are omitted.

Laa8I1vVBg.one_liner: Loops gated self-attention values while keeping feedforward layers outside recurrence for efficient reasoning.
Laa8I1vVBg.problem: Recurrent-depth Transformers inflate compute by recomputing both attention and feedforward layers at every shared-parameter step.
Laa8I1vVBg.method: G-Loop repeatedly remixes input values with evolving attention state through token- and channel-wise gates, trains puzzle models by backpropagation through time, and adapts DeBERTa for language tasks.
Laa8I1vVBg.key_idea: Uses token- and channel-wise gates to blend layer-input values with evolving attention state at every recurrence, preventing token collapse.
Laa8I1vVBg.evidence: Experiments compare HRM and TRM-Att on Sudoku and Maze at 32 recurrent steps and evaluate DeBERTa-v3-base on six GLUE tasks and SQuAD 2.0.
Laa8I1vVBg.claimed_gains: At 32 recurrent steps, G-Loop cuts inference FLOPs by up to 94.7% and memory by up to 73.9% compared to HRM and TRM-Att.
Laa8I1vVBg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that attention-only recurrence is conceptually simple and computationally efficient, with competitive reasoning results and thorough gating ablations.
Laa8I1vVBg.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the language-understanding gains inconclusive because comparisons lack parameter- and compute-matched controls and use a different architecture.

5T4cPwU3Nh.one_liner: Replaces derivatives and weight transport with local perturbation measurements and learned feedback matrices.
5T4cPwU3Nh.problem: Backpropagation's exact derivatives and weight transport are biologically implausible, while alternatives struggle to scale with comparable simplicity.
5T4cPwU3Nh.method: PerProp measures layerwise neuron slopes with paired perturbed evaluations and learns feedback matrices from random probes once per update, retaining a forward–backward learning structure.
5T4cPwU3Nh.key_idea: Measures neuron slopes through paired forward perturbations and learns feedback matrices from random probes, keeping credit assignment local.
5T4cPwU3Nh.evidence: Evaluations span Transformers, Mamba, residual MLPs, ConvNeXt, spiking and stochastic units, and end-to-end BrainScaleS-2 neuromorphic experiments.
5T4cPwU3Nh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that one local rule applies across diverse architectures and is supported by theory, simulation, and physical on-chip updates.
5T4cPwU3Nh.main_concern: Reviewers most often criticize missing comparisons with closely related feedback-learning methods and insufficient ablation of probes and key modifications.

p0JqtZGmch.one_liner: Distills diffusion models with multi-resolution teacher-feature discriminators and low-noise-biased Beta sampling.
p0JqtZGmch.problem: Teacher-based adversarial distillation biases toward high noise, where fine-scale feature structure is lost, and often requires auxiliary score networks.
p0JqtZGmch.method: MuSD trains lightweight discriminator heads on frozen teacher features at multiple resolutions and samples noise from a maximum-entropy Beta distribution under a corruption budget.
p0JqtZGmch.key_idea: Reads frozen teacher features at multiple resolutions under a maximum-entropy Beta noise distribution that favors low noise within a corruption budget.
p0JqtZGmch.evidence: Experiments cover CIFAR-10, AFHQv2, FFHQ, ImageNet, U-Net and Transformer teachers, and two-step text-to-image generation with SD3.5-Medium.
p0JqtZGmch.claimed_gains: On EDM2-S and DiT-XL/2, the one-step student surpasses its 250-step teacher, with competitive or better one-step FID using fewer training images and lower GPU memory.
p0JqtZGmch.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing multi-resolution teacher features is simple and efficient, with meaningful resource reductions and broad validation.
p0JqtZGmch.main_concern: The main concern is that ablations do not fully isolate multi-resolution readouts from Beta noise sampling, leaving the source of gains unclear.

pXpcZQZEsG.one_liner: Stress-tests numerical-optimization LLMs with perturbed benchmarks, opaque identifiers, and surrogate floors to detect recall.
pXpcZQZEsG.problem: Near-exact answers on classic numerical test functions may reflect benchmark recall rather than inference from freshly sampled observations.
pXpcZQZEsG.method: The protocol combines a near-exact recall signature, smooth random perturbations of published functions, surrogate floors, multi-fidelity prediction, and integration tasks without stored answers.
pXpcZQZEsG.key_idea: Measures recall dose–response by smoothly perturbing known functions away from published forms while tracking near-exact benchmark answers.
pXpcZQZEsG.evidence: The study runs 19,140 sessions with seven LLMs and compares five surrogate fitters across optimization and multi-fidelity cells using multiple controls.
pXpcZQZEsG.claimed_gains: Across 19,140 sessions with seven LLMs, models returned near-exact answers on benchmark optimization problems in up to 88% of sessions despite fresh samples and opaque identifiers.
pXpcZQZEsG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that benchmark recall in LLM-based optimization is an important problem addressed with extensive and complementary controls.
pXpcZQZEsG.main_concern: Reviewers most often caution that near-exact benchmark answers do not by themselves identify memorization or exclude data-driven numerical inference.

tLa5gXpUyP.one_liner: Propagates Laplace parameter uncertainty through linearized ROI interventions to obtain closed-form neuroimaging influence posteriors.
tLa5gXpUyP.problem: Deterministic neuroimaging attribution maps can be unstable and rarely quantify uncertainty in regional influence.
tLa5gXpUyP.method: CFIP defines influence as output change under ROI intervention, applies a Laplace approximation to parameter uncertainty, and propagates it through a first-order linearized influence functional.
tLa5gXpUyP.key_idea: Computes analytic ROI-influence distributions by pushing a Laplace parameter posterior through a first-order linearized intervention functional.
tLa5gXpUyP.evidence: Validation spans multi-cohort structural-MRI regional features and fMRI connectivity, with retraining stability, HMC comparisons, calibration, and runtime measurements.
tLa5gXpUyP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that analytic distributions over regional effects are efficient, explicitly defined, and evaluated beyond standard attribution maps.
tLa5gXpUyP.main_concern: Reviewers most often question whether the Gaussian pushforward adds enough beyond deterministic ablation and sampling, citing inconsistent posterior calibration in harder settings.

HxRseexHsY.one_liner: Selects unlearning targets using answer-position attention, then suppresses them with contrastive logits and retention objectives.
HxRseexHsY.problem: Uniform sample-level unlearning can excessively forget non-target content and degrade general language capability.
HxRseexHsY.method: AGTTU scores tokens by attention from subsequent answer positions and unlearns the selected targets with Contrastive Logits Preference Loss. A retain-set objective limits utility loss and protects non-target content.
HxRseexHsY.key_idea: Use the model’s own answer-to-token attention to select forget targets, then apply contrastive suppression separately to target and non-target tokens.
HxRseexHsY.evidence: Experiments on TOFU and MUSE Books include Llama-3.2-1B across three TOFU forgetting ratios and comparisons with listed unlearning baselines and TPO.
HxRseexHsY.claimed_gains: On MUSE Books, AGTTU reduces forget-set verbatim memorization by 4.51% versus TPO while increasing retain-set knowledge memorization by 15.17%.
HxRseexHsY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the self-contained attention selector is efficient and intuitive, requires no auxiliary model or perturbation scoring, and is supported by a matched-budget selection ablation.
HxRseexHsY.main_concern: Reviewers most often question the limited technical novelty and whether experiments on two small models establish scalability and generalizability.

IxQ8xrYl4j.one_liner: Propagates implicit expectile values across multiple steps to strengthen learning from rare successful reinforcement-learning trajectories.
IxQ8xrYl4j.problem: In long-horizon sparse-reward tasks, behavior-policy evaluation can assign low values to states on rare successful trajectories, weakening their learning signal.
IxQ8xrYl4j.method: The paper combines expectile-based implicit value learning with recursive temporal propagation through coupled action-state and value-only estimators, IQ and IV. The formulation targets an implicit policy favoring high-valued actions while preserving unbiased reward and transition expectations.
IxQ8xrYl4j.key_idea: Recursively propagate expectile-based action and state values so optimistic implicit-policy evaluation carries value backward along successful trajectories.
IxQ8xrYl4j.evidence: The authors prove contraction and a unique fixed point for the joint action-state operator and evaluate IQ and IV against PPO with GAE on multiple sparse- and dense-reward tasks.
IxQ8xrYl4j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the estimators are simple and intuitive, the theoretical analysis is detailed, and multi-step expectile propagation offers a plausible way to exploit successful experience.
IxQ8xrYl4j.main_concern: Reviewers consistently find the baselines insufficient, especially the reliance on PPO with GAE and missing controls for critic ensembling and tuned discount factors.

IFogXt9JmC.one_liner: Synthesizes terminal-agent tasks from input-output transitions between real-world artifacts rather than fabricated environments or static inputs.
IFogXt9JmC.problem: Automated agent-task synthesis either fabricates low-fidelity environments or reduces real artifacts to shallow operations on static inputs.
IFogXt9JmC.method: WorkBorne builds artifact corpora through iterative web retrieval, discovers meaningful input-output artifact assemblies and their relations, and instantiates each transition as a grounded task. Each transition records the actor, anchoring artifacts, intended outcome, and relationship.
IFogXt9JmC.key_idea: Model an agentic task as a relation-driven transition between authentic input and output artifacts, then instantiate that transition in an executable environment.
IFogXt9JmC.evidence: The authors construct 1,061 artifact corpora, 7,882 task environments, and 15,485 trajectories, and conduct experiments with Qwen3.5-27B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B.
IFogXt9JmC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that artifact transitions are intuitive and well motivated and that controlled comparisons and empirical analyses support the central task-synthesis approach.
IFogXt9JmC.main_concern: Reviewers question generality beyond the single teacher, model family, and task setup, and note that uncontrolled synthesis comparisons confound teacher, data scale, and training recipe.

ii0KSHq8DT.one_liner: Introduces an 800-hour longitudinal single-person egocentric dataset and an open-vocabulary benchmark for anticipating personal behavior.
ii0KSHq8DT.problem: Existing egocentric datasets prioritize multi-participant diversity over long-term continuity, preventing study of months-long personal routines and action anticipation.
ii0KSHq8DT.method: NextMe-800 records 800 hours of 1 Hz images, gaze, and audio from one volunteer over 126 days, annotated at five hierarchical abstraction levels. Combined with EgoLife, it forms NextAct, a 1,500-point open-vocabulary K-step sequence prediction benchmark scored by embedding-based soft edit distance.
ii0KSHq8DT.key_idea: Collects 126 days of multi-sensory single-person egocentric video with five-level hierarchical captions to benchmark open-vocabulary K-step behavior anticipation.
ii0KSHq8DT.evidence: Evaluates multiple models on within- and cross-person anticipation across NextAct as a function of context length.
ii0KSHq8DT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the longitudinal 126-day dataset with gaze, audio, and five-level captions is a carefully documented resource for personal routine modeling.
ii0KSHq8DT.main_concern: Reviewers raise strong concerns about generalizability since NextMe-800 captures only a single individual's lifestyle and routines.

M5iSo0VMaQ.one_liner: Integrates runtime expert replication and pipelined weight/gradient communication into persistent forward and backward MoE megakernels.
M5iSo0VMaQ.problem: Fixed expert placement in MoE megakernels creates GPU stragglers under routing skew, while naive dynamic replication exposes weight-transfer and gradient-reduction latency.
M5iSo0VMaQ.method: MegaFlux uses an on-device planner to place dynamic replicas and assign tile-aligned token blocks under a per-GPU budget without changing router outputs. Persistent forward and backward megakernels start replica compute as weights arrive and overlap replica-gradient reductions with ongoing expert computation.
M5iSo0VMaQ.key_idea: Plans runtime expert replicas on-device and pipelines weight arrival and gradient reduction inside persistent forward and backward MoE megakernels.
M5iSo0VMaQ.evidence: Evaluated across 147 forward and backward configurations on eight NVIDIA B200 GPUs plus inference prefill tests.
M5iSo0VMaQ.claimed_gains: Across 147 configurations per direction on eight NVIDIA B200 GPUs, MegaFlux achieves geometric-mean speedups of 1.45x for forward and 1.28x for backward over fixed-placement megakernels, peaking at 2.14x and 2.64x.
M5iSo0VMaQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pipelining dynamic expert replication inside persistent MoE kernels addresses routing skew effectively with strong B200 speedups.
M5iSo0VMaQ.main_concern: Reviewers note missing end-to-end training convergence and step-time evaluations, unisolated individual scheduling ablations, and missing peak-memory or tolerance reports.

llteRIlmdI.one_liner: Finds new Hadamard maximal determinant records by recasting bordered bicirculant matrices as autocorrelation sequence reconstruction.
llteRIlmdI.problem: Finding n x n {+1,-1} matrices that maximize the determinant is computationally intractable for large orders n congruent to 3 mod 4.
llteRIlmdI.method: The authors restrict to bordered bicirculant block constructions, prove optimality within that family, and recast the search as reconstructing sequences from periodic autocorrelation pairs under arithmetic conditions. They apply learning-based reconstruction with local Hilbert-symbol obstruction rewards and compare against simulated annealing.
llteRIlmdI.key_idea: Recasts bordered bicirculant determinant maximization as periodic autocorrelation sequence reconstruction and guides learned search with local Hilbert-symbol obstruction rewards.
llteRIlmdI.evidence: Produces independently verifiable matrix constructions attaining new record determinants for n=51 and n congruent to 3 mod 4 between 103 and 119.
llteRIlmdI.claimed_gains: Reports new record determinants for orders n=51 and n congruent to 3 mod 4 between 103 and 119.
llteRIlmdI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that producing independently verifiable new determinant records on a longstanding mathematical problem is concrete and valuable.
llteRIlmdI.main_concern: Reviewers note that the computational advantage of learned reconstruction over simulated annealing is not established for the lift-based pipeline, and motivation for the bordered bicirculant restriction is abrupt.

vGGXAnDPzj.one_liner: Equips reward models with calibrated quantile prediction intervals via UARM to downweight uncertain rewards in GRPO.
vGGXAnDPzj.problem: Standard scalar reward models provide no evaluation confidence, causing GRPO to weight ambiguous and well-supported rewards equally.
vGGXAnDPzj.method: The authors propose Uncertainty-Aware Reward Modeling (UARM), adding a quantile-prediction MLP head and conformal-style calibration to produce a point estimate and adaptive prediction interval per sample, then reweighting GRPO advantages inversely by estimated noise variance.
vGGXAnDPzj.key_idea: Predicting calibrated interquantile intervals alongside scalar rewards enables downweighting high-uncertainty samples during GRPO advantage standardization.
vGGXAnDPzj.evidence: Experiments across 3 preference datasets, 5 backbones, 12 baselines, and 4 safety benchmarks for downstream RLHF.
vGGXAnDPzj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically relevant and appreciate the lightweight single-pass MLP head, simple GRPO integration, and broad experimental scope.
vGGXAnDPzj.main_concern: Reviewers point out that R^2@50/MSE@50 confound point accuracy with uncertainty ranking, empirical coverage/interval width are unreported, and novelty is limited over existing conformal/quantile methods like CIR and CFA.

7nBPRLTKqu.one_liner: Reconstructs identity-free character profiles from free descriptions using psychology-grounded profiling questions across eight personality dimensions.
7nBPRLTKqu.problem: Role-playing agents struggle with niche or original characters lacking gold-standard profiles, and hiding canonical names removes profile value.
7nBPRLTKqu.method: Minstrel poses three profiling questions for each of eight personality psychology dimensions to retrieve and convert free descriptions or public comments into an identity-free conditioning profile.
7nBPRLTKqu.key_idea: Queries free text through 24 personality-psychology questions across eight dimensions to assemble an identity-free character conditioning profile.
7nBPRLTKqu.evidence: Evaluated across four open-source actor models and two cross-family judges on 16 characters using win share, recognition rate, and distinctiveness.
7nBPRLTKqu.claimed_gains: Built from public comments alone, reaches win shares of 0.570 and 0.610 while limiting actor character identification to 1.6% of trials.
7nBPRLTKqu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identity-free profile reconstruction for non-canonical characters is a practical, underexplored problem connected to personality psychology.
7nBPRLTKqu.main_concern: Reviewers find the paper confusingly written with undefined terms and overly abstract notation, and note missing comparisons against simpler profile-building baselines.

PBguRifE5u.one_liner: Constructs a pure differentially private hierarchical clustering tree in near-linear time using only noisy vertex degrees.
PBguRifE5u.problem: Private graph hierarchical clustering typically requires recovering clusters or heavy computation while preserving edge-weight privacy.
PBguRifE5u.method: Noisy-Degree Hierarchy privatizes vertex degrees under weight-level l1-adjacency DP and builds a full hierarchical clustering tree in O(m + n log n) time without explicitly recovering clusters.
PBguRifE5u.key_idea: Builds a hierarchical clustering tree solely from differentially private noisy vertex degrees in O(m + n log n) time.
PBguRifE5u.evidence: Approximation bounds for Dasgupta's cost on well-clusterable graphs, a matching Omega(k) lower bound, and experiments on synthetic and real-world graphs.
PBguRifE5u.claimed_gains: Noisy-Degree Hierarchy runs in O(m + n log n) time and achieves an O(k^6 / (lambda_{k+1}^2 * epsilon)) Dasgupta-cost approximation, improving the non-private bound from O(k^22 / lambda_{k+1}^10) to O(k^6 / lambda_{k+1}^2) and O(k / epsilon) under regularity.
PBguRifE5u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the simplicity, near-linear runtime, and tightened approximation bounds using only noisy vertex degrees.
PBguRifE5u.main_concern: Reviewers note that Dasgupta's cost and degree-distinct SBM setups favor degree-based heuristics, and flag inaccurate terminology describing weight-DP as edge-DP.

PZMjP5JEse.one_liner: Restricts MoE routing to swap at most one expert per token-layer so only active experts reside in fast memory.
PZMjP5JEse.problem: Sparse MoE models require holding all experts in fast memory during serving, making them impractical for memory-constrained devices.
PZMjP5JEse.method: Temporal MoE constrains each layer to reuse all but one of the previous token's experts, keeping only active experts in RAM while overlapping the single incoming expert's flash transfer with computation.
PZMjP5JEse.key_idea: Cap expert turnover at one expert per layer per token so active experts stay resident in fast memory and flash loads overlap with computation.
PZMjP5JEse.evidence: Pretraining scaling runs (10^16 to 10^19 FLOPs), hardware benchmarks (RTX A6000, Intel laptop, Pixel 10a) on 11B-shaped models, and post-hoc distillation tests support the approach.
PZMjP5JEse.claimed_gains: Pre-trained Temporal MoE reduces serving memory by 5.1x while preserving 72-82% of standard MoE's advantage over dense models, and an 11B-scale model keeps 66-83% of standard MoE decode speed on hardware benchmarks.
PZMjP5JEse.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that capping expert swaps at one per token-layer provides a clean worst-case I/O bound enabling active-only memory residency.
PZMjP5JEse.main_concern: Reviewers highlight a disconnect between small pretrained models and randomly initialized 11B hardware benchmarks, as well as accuracy drops when applied post-hoc.

6dJKes2VwH.one_liner: Estimates graph-level error of frozen causal discovery foundation models under SCM shifts using observable diagnostics for selective deferral.
6dJKes2VwH.problem: Causal discovery foundation models can produce unreliable graphs under structural causal model (SCM) distribution shifts, where raw model confidence fails to reflect structural error.
6dJKes2VwH.method: CauRisk trains a post-hoc risk estimator on synthetic source environments using predictive uncertainty, resampling stability, and graph-data statistical compatibility while keeping the discovery model frozen. The estimated risk drives selective prediction to retain reliable graphs and defer unreliable ones.
6dJKes2VwH.key_idea: Combines predictive uncertainty, resampling stability, and data-graph compatibility into a source-trained post-hoc risk estimator to defer unreliable causal graph predictions.
6dJKes2VwH.evidence: Evaluated across two frozen discovery backbones under held-out causal mechanism and graph-topology families on failure detection, risk calibration, and risk-coverage trade-offs.
6dJKes2VwH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that assessing when to trust frozen causal discovery models under distribution shift without target ground-truth graphs is an important, practical problem.
6dJKes2VwH.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments are restricted to small synthetic datasets (10 variables, 500 observations), omit simple unsupervised falsification baselines, and fail to meet target risk budgets under topology shift.

0HRO6cvMqC.one_liner: Studies desktop software evolution to derive interface principles and synthesize agent-native programmatic interfaces from installed applications.
0HRO6cvMqC.problem: Desktop software interfaces are built for humans rather than LLM agents, forcing agents into brittle visual control or complex low-level composition.
0HRO6cvMqC.method: The authors introduce DeskIF-Bench (255 tasks across six applications and historical releases) to study how interface changes affect agent success, identifying discoverability, granularity, and observability. Guided by these principles, ANIS discovers runtime capabilities, synthesizes verified atomic and goal-level commands, and extracts reusable trajectories.
0HRO6cvMqC.key_idea: Derives interface design principles from historical software releases and synthesizes verified agent-native command interfaces via runtime capability discovery and trajectory extraction.
0HRO6cvMqC.evidence: Evaluated on DeskIF-Bench (255 tasks, 6 apps) and an expanded 368-task suite across 8 apps using DeepSeek V4 Flash and Claude Haiku 4.5 against native SDKs and CLI-Anything.
0HRO6cvMqC.claimed_gains: Atomic interfaces improve success over native SDK use by 3.8 and 3.5 percentage points with DeepSeek V4 Flash and Claude Haiku 4.5, respectively.
0HRO6cvMqC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate using historical software releases as a natural experiment to study agent interface usability and building the DeskIF-Bench benchmark.
0HRO6cvMqC.main_concern: Reviewers note that cross-version changes confound multiple factors so the three design principles are not isolated experimentally, and comparisons against CLI-Anything are confounded by missing commands.

YFNjp6KSF7.one_liner: Equips vision-language agents with drawing-tracing tools and retrieved specifications to convert P&IDs into connectivity graphs.
YFNjp6KSF7.problem: Interpreting piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs) requires tracing dense line connectivity and grounding semantic attributes in project specifications, which static visual recognition fails to do.
YFNjp6KSF7.method: PID-Agents provides a VLM agent with domain-specific drawing tools—ROI rendering, event-driven line tracing returning junction/endpoint events, and local connectivity probing—paired with retrieval-augmented specification checks to reconstruct structured pipeline and instrument listings.
YFNjp6KSF7.key_idea: Offloads pixel-level geometry to event-driven line-tracing and probing tools while using a RAG-augmented VLM agent for semantic junction and specification decisions.
YFNjp6KSF7.evidence: Evaluated on approximately 150 engineering drawings (212 annotated connections) and a cross-project setting using Gemini 3 Flash variants.
YFNjp6KSF7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that P&ID connectivity reconstruction is a practical industrial problem and that offloading geometric line tracing to discrete event tools is a sensible division of labor.
YFNjp6KSF7.main_concern: Reviewers note the lack of comparisons against traditional non-agent graph/line-tracing pipelines and insufficient ablations separating agent reasoning gains from RAG and specialized tools.

DPO6PJRlOL.one_liner: Embeds gene co-expression graphs onto 2D image grids via Gromov-Wasserstein transport for cross-species masked self-supervised single-cell pretraining.
DPO6PJRlOL.problem: Single-cell gene expression vectors lack spatial structure for vision architectures and cross-species alignment across differing gene sets.
DPO6PJRlOL.method: TransMap maps gene-gene relational distances onto a 2D pixel grid using Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) transport—and fused GW with soft ortholog correspondences across species—assigning one gene per pixel. A shared masked autoencoder is then pretrained on these 2D gene-expression images across human and mouse metacells.
DPO6PJRlOL.key_idea: Maps gene relational graphs and cross-species orthologs onto 2D pixel grids via fused Gromov-Wasserstein transport for shared masked-patch vision pretraining.
DPO6PJRlOL.evidence: Evaluated layout preservation and masked reconstruction across five datasets and two model sizes, plus zero-shot/fine-tuned evaluation after pretraining on ~732K human-mouse metacells.
DPO6PJRlOL.claimed_gains: GW layouts achieve lower mean masked patch reconstruction error than random layouts in all 10 comparisons across five datasets and two model sizes.
DPO6PJRlOL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that mapping gene networks onto 2D grids via GW transport to preserve per-gene expression values is a well-motivated input representation.
DPO6PJRlOL.main_concern: Reviewers note that fine-tuned TransMap underperforms PCA on most benchmarks, layout ablations omit the 147M model, and cross-species alignment is untested.

06Ae1Yv3a7.one_liner: Shows BatchNorm carry-versus-reset benefit rankings transfer across models, but require recalibrating a single decision threshold.
06Ae1Yv3a7.problem: Whether measurements of when carrying BatchNorm statistics helps on one model can guide carry/reset decisions on another model during domain shifts.
06Ae1Yv3a7.method: The authors run paired carry/reset evaluations on frozen networks across corruption transitions, measure cross-model rank correlation, and transfer a single learned decision threshold from other models to decide when to carry BatchNorm memory.
06Ae1Yv3a7.key_idea: Separates cross-model ranking transfer from decision-boundary transfer by learning a single recalibrated carry/reset threshold from reference models.
06Ae1Yv3a7.evidence: Evaluated across 12 CIFAR-C models and 210 ordered corruption pairs, including held-receiver, held-edge, and 120 closed-loop stream tests.
06Ae1Yv3a7.claimed_gains: A reference map ranks transitions at r=0.76, and shifting the decision threshold gains 0.83 percentage points on unseen models/transitions and 0.93 points in closed-loop streams.
06Ae1Yv3a7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight the clear, rigorous distinction between ranking transferability and decision-boundary transferability.
06Ae1Yv3a7.main_concern: Gains are modest (~0.93 points), experiments are confined to frozen CNNs on CIFAR-C with known domain boundaries, and overloaded jargon impairs readability.

mdu1KAUEXr.one_liner: Aligns heterogeneous LLMs via compact KV-cache codecs anchored to a frozen reference model's coordinates using ridge regression.
mdu1KAUEXr.problem: Existing latent communication methods require pairwise cache mappings or jointly trained adapters, preventing new heterogeneous models from joining without retraining.
mdu1KAUEXr.method: LLM-SemanticLAN anchors a shared latent space in closed form via ridge regression against a frozen reference model before training lightweight model-specific codecs (0.8%-3.6% of base parameters) that compress and reconstruct native KV caches.
mdu1KAUEXr.key_idea: Anchors a public KV-cache latent space via closed-form ridge regression to a frozen reference model so heterogeneous models align via lightweight codecs.
mdu1KAUEXr.evidence: Evaluated across scales, attention architectures, families (five Qwen models plus Llama-3.1-8B), modalities, and untrained transfer routes on public QA datasets.
mdu1KAUEXr.claimed_gains: Codecs use 0.8%-3.6% of base model parameters and produce latent representations 64x smaller on average than native BF16 KV caches.
mdu1KAUEXr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree single-partner admission and zero-shot routing across untrained model pairs address a practical multi-model communication problem.
mdu1KAUEXr.main_concern: Experiments lack comparisons to competitive KV-transfer baselines and direct text-forwarding latency/FLOPs, use mostly Qwen models, and do not isolate external anchoring from ridge initialization.

hwkiq3iaFi.one_liner: Pretrains vision models on semantic line drawings before photographs to instill shape-centered representations and improve downstream transfer.
hwkiq3iaFi.problem: Standard training on photographs biases neural networks toward texture and color cues rather than stable object shape and spatial structure.
hwkiq3iaFi.method: Inspired by infant visual development, the authors use a two-stage curriculum that trains deep networks on semantically meaningful line drawings first to form structural attractors before transitioning to natural photographs.
hwkiq3iaFi.key_idea: Uses a line-drawing-to-photograph training curriculum to bias visual representations toward boundaries and global shape.
hwkiq3iaFi.evidence: Evaluated across object recognition, segmentation, depth estimation, detection, data efficiency, shape bias, and knowledge distillation.
hwkiq3iaFi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the extensive multi-task evaluations showing strong empirical benefits from early line-drawing exposure.
hwkiq3iaFi.main_concern: The infant-development framing is criticized as unrealistic since infants do not see line drawings, and gains may stem from the semantic line-drawing prior itself rather than curriculum ordering.

wMts5wlQap.one_liner: Formalizes a learning-awareness order for multi-agent social dilemmas and proposes LARL, a model-free decentralized MARL algorithm with dynamic grouping.
wMts5wlQap.problem: Existing learning-aware MARL methods for social dilemmas rely on restrictive assumptions such as access to co-players' gradients or update rules.
wMts5wlQap.method: The authors conceptualize learning as an action to define a learning-awareness hierarchy (LA-order) and introduce LARL, a model-free decentralized MARL algorithm that uses dynamic agent grouping, GRU memory, and multi-timescale updates from each agent's own experience.
wMts5wlQap.key_idea: Orders agents by co-player learning information and trains decentralized MARL policies across orders using dynamic agent grouping and staggered update intervals.
wMts5wlQap.evidence: Evaluated across iterated matrix games and state-based social dilemmas including Coins and Coop Mining.
wMts5wlQap.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the conceptual framework unifying learning-aware methods and the strong cooperation returns of model-free decentralized LARL on Coins and Coop Mining.
wMts5wlQap.main_concern: The formal LA-order definition is underspecified and does not align with LARL's implementation (staggered update intervals and grouping), leaving the source of empirical gains unisolated.

IhQbFddkBp.one_liner: LP-BD adds a prefix-conditioned latent-plan flow to block diffusion language models to reduce within-block conditional total correlation.
IhQbFddkBp.problem: Block diffusion language models sample tokens within a block from independent per-token marginals, incurring a minimum one-step error equal to the block's conditional total correlation.
IhQbFddkBp.method: Latent-Plan Block Diffusion (LP-BD) uses a small conditional flow to sample a low-dimensional block-level latent plan from the generated prefix and conditions the masked-diffusion denoiser on it, trained end-to-end from the denoiser loss while matching BD3-LM at initialization.
IhQbFddkBp.key_idea: Samples a prefix-conditioned low-dimensional block intent via a small flow model so the parallel block denoiser shares a latent variable across tokens.
IhQbFddkBp.evidence: Proves the one-step conditional total correlation lower bound and evaluates from-scratch 28M/85M models on TinyStories and 170M BD3-LM checkpoints on OpenWebText.
IhQbFddkBp.claimed_gains: On TinyStories (16-token blocks), LP-BD lowers one-step judge NLL by 31% and matches 16-step BD3-LM quality in 8 steps; on OpenWebText (170M), it lowers generative perplexity at matched entropy by 14–55% (38–66% with guidance).
IhQbFddkBp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean theoretical characterization linking parallel decoding error to conditional total correlation and the clear, well-structured presentation.
IhQbFddkBp.main_concern: Evaluation relies only on unconditional perplexity-style proxy metrics (no downstream tasks), does not directly measure total correlation reduction, and overlaps conceptually with prior latent parallel-generation work.

ioYKmdybRj.one_liner: KSGL augments message-passing GNNs with multi-order local and global KnotState features from F2 rank–nullity statistics of induced subgraphs.
ioYKmdybRj.problem: Standard MPNNs and 3-WL-equivalent GNNs cannot distinguish non-isomorphic strongly regular graphs with identical local degree and common-neighbor counts.
ioYKmdybRj.method: Inspired by knot-theoretic interlacement graphs, the authors define KnotState using the rank–nullity structure of induced subgraph adjacency matrices over F2, and build KSGL to integrate multi-order local and global KnotState descriptors into message passing with an order-dependent discriminative hierarchy.
ioYKmdybRj.key_idea: Encodes induced-subgraph adjacency rank–nullity statistics over F2 as multi-order local and global structural descriptors fused into message-passing GNNs.
ioYKmdybRj.evidence: Theoretical separation hierarchy plus experiments on strongly regular graphs, BREC (distinguishing 300/400 pairs), and zeolite heat-of-adsorption prediction.
ioYKmdybRj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the algebraic F2 rank–nullity structural representation interesting and note strong empirical discrimination on SRG, BREC, and zeolite property prediction.
ioYKmdybRj.main_concern: Combinatorial induced-subgraph enumeration lacks runtime/memory scaling evaluation, novelty beyond the two-variable interlace polynomial is modest, and theory does not clarify when finite separation order holds.

SmnVt9xbVf.one_liner: LANTERN predicts post-stroke aphasia recovery using a hemodynamic-gain-invariant task-fMRI network reserve measure and uncertainty-aware worst-case monotone training.
SmnVt9xbVf.problem: Regional vascular scaling differences and measurement noise hinder task-fMRI prediction of language recovery after stroke.
SmnVt9xbVf.method: LANTERN defines a task-conditioned language-network reserve invariant to regional hemodynamic scaling, bounds reserve uncertainty across overlapping brain-region sets, trains a monotone predictor against worst-case error within those bounds, and calibrates prediction intervals.
SmnVt9xbVf.key_idea: Computes a gain-invariant task-diversity reserve metric, bounds its measurement uncertainty over overlapping brain regions, and trains a monotone predictor against worst-case bound error.
SmnVt9xbVf.evidence: Evaluated on current impairment in the public Aphasia Recovery Cohort and six-month WAB-AQ outcomes in a two-center longitudinal cohort of 237 participants (84 held-out center).
SmnVt9xbVf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the gain-invariant network biomarker, incorporation of measurement uncertainty into training, and clean separation of fitting, calibration, and held-out-center testing.
SmnVt9xbVf.main_concern: Exposition relies on undefined custom terminology with key math in the appendix, baselines do not isolate the reserve construction from simple row normalization, and biological/interval-MAE details are unclear.

cwBLs9vJni.one_liner: ID2P distills a future-conditioned inverse dynamics model into a flow-based robot policy via mixed velocities and hidden states.
cwBLs9vJni.problem: Robot policy learning methods rarely leverage future observations for direct action-level supervision alongside representation supervision without adding inference cost.
cwBLs9vJni.method: IDM-to-Policy Distillation (ID2P) trains an inverse dynamics model (IDM) with the same architecture conditioned on current and future observations, then supervises the flow-based policy by mixing IDM and expert action velocities and aligning action-expert hidden states, requiring no IDM at test time.
cwBLs9vJni.key_idea: Trains a future-conditioned inverse dynamics teacher and distills both mixed action velocities and hidden representations into a flow policy with zero inference overhead.
cwBLs9vJni.evidence: Variance-reduction proof under an ideal IDM plus simulation (including LIBERO-Plus) and real bimanual robot experiments on SmolVLA (0.45B) and pi0.5.
cwBLs9vJni.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the zero-inference-overhead training framework, broad evaluation across SmolVLA and pi0.5, and robustness gains over longer-trained baselines on LIBERO-Plus.
cwBLs9vJni.main_concern: Experiments lack a current-observation-only teacher control to separate future-observation value from generic teacher distillation, and most gains come from representation distillation rather than the theoretically analyzed action distillation.

RYUV5GzY8H.one_liner: TAPR grounds sequential recommendation in temporal attribute probabilistic rules composed via closed Beta-distribution conjunctions.
RYUV5GzY8H.problem: Logic-based sequential recommenders rarely ground logical operators in explicit item attributes or test whether logical structure actually drives ranking behavior.
RYUV5GzY8H.method: Temporal Attribute Probabilistic Rule (TAPR) extracts event-bound item attribute evidence from user history and composes it via probabilistic conjunction in a closed Beta representation space to directly score candidate items.
RYUV5GzY8H.key_idea: Represents event-bound item attributes as Beta distributions closed under probabilistic conjunction so composed temporal rules directly produce ranking scores.
RYUV5GzY8H.evidence: Evaluated on three real-world sequential recommendation datasets (MovieLens, H&M, Yelp) plus synthetic structural-intervention and faithfulness tests.
RYUV5GzY8H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the clean Beta-conjugate mathematical formalization and the targeted synthetic intervention and faithfulness tests beyond leaderboard metrics.
RYUV5GzY8H.main_concern: Ablations show mixed necessity of the temporal-relation module (outperformed by CNN-only on Yelp and by zeroing relational weight on MovieLens), and baselines are outdated.

gZeQjHtMCw.one_liner: SparseBalance co-optimizes distributed long-context sparse-attention training via sparsity-aware batching and runtime dynamic sparsity tuning.
gZeQjHtMCw.problem: Distributed long-context LLM training with sparse attention suffers from severe load imbalance and accuracy loss due to heterogeneous sequence lengths and sparsity sensitivities.
gZeQjHtMCw.method: SparseBalance combines Sparsity-Aware Batching (SAB) for coarse-grained load balance with Workload-Aware Dynamic Sparsity Tuning (DST), which bidirectionally adjusts micro-batch top-k attention budgets at runtime to mitigate stragglers and use idle bubbles.
gZeQjHtMCw.key_idea: Pairs sparsity-aware batching with runtime bidirectional adjustment of micro-batch top-k sparse-attention budgets guided by a latency predictor and quality guard.
gZeQjHtMCw.evidence: Evaluated across two clusters, two datasets, and three model settings (under 3B parameters) using MoBA sparse attention, measuring throughput and downstream benchmarks.
gZeQjHtMCw.claimed_gains: Achieves up to a 1.33x end-to-end speedup while maintaining downstream benchmark performance.
gZeQjHtMCw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate treating attention sparsity as a dynamic runtime lever for straggler mitigation and note consistent speedups across clusters and settings.
gZeQjHtMCw.main_concern: Missing recent load-balancing system baselines (e.g., WLB-LLM), unevaluated lookup-table latency predictor accuracy, and testing limited to one sparse-attention backend (MoBA) on sub-3B models.

nJGXlsplVB.one_liner: Analyzes pretraining Transformers with K-interval quantized softmax, showing calibration-gradient preservation and fixed-window grids prevent loss spikes.
nJGXlsplVB.problem: Quantizing attention softmax during LLM pretraining alters both forward values and backward gradients, causing training failures that inference-only studies miss.
nJGXlsplVB.method: The authors study K-interval attention approximating exp(x) on K+1 grid points, deriving exact backward rules (including row-calibration derivatives) and systematically varying per-row min–max versus fixed-window calibration, interpolation versus hard rounding, and pre- versus post-normalization straight-through surrogates.
nJGXlsplVB.key_idea: Retains per-row calibration gradients in the backward pass and uses fixed-window K-interval grids with post-normalization surrogates to stabilize quantized-softmax pretraining.
nJGXlsplVB.evidence: Matched pretraining experiments on 124M-parameter models over 2.5B tokens across multiple seeds, ablations, geometry probes, and downstream evaluations.
nJGXlsplVB.claimed_gains: At 124M parameters and 2.5B tokens, fixed-window calibration ends +0.007 nats from exact softmax with interpolation (K=4), +0.019 nats with hard rounding and post-normalization surrogate (K=4), and +0.004 nats at K=16.
nJGXlsplVB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean, controlled identification of the row-calibration gradient defect causing delayed pretraining loss spikes in an under-explored setting.
nJGXlsplVB.main_concern: Practical systems applicability is unclear because no hardware kernels or speedups are measured, normalization/reciprocal quantization is omitted, and standard formats like FP8/INT8 are not studied.

MdKVJH3Y5A.one_liner: PACE selects meta-RL training tasks by measuring episode-local adaptation dependence via paired adaptive-versus-static rollouts on frozen suffixes.
MdKVJH3Y5A.problem: Existing meta-RL curricula rank tasks by difficulty, regret, or post-adaptation return, which fail to measure how much performance actually depends on within-episode adaptation.
MdKVJH3Y5A.method: Paired Adaptation-Contrast Ecology (PACE) runs matched adaptive (update enabled) and static (update disabled) executions on a frozen task suffix to compute AdaptGain, then updates the training task distribution in a closed loop.
MdKVJH3Y5A.key_idea: Contrasts matched adaptive and static rollouts on a frozen episode suffix to score task adaptation dependence (AdaptGain) and drive closed-loop task selection.
MdKVJH3Y5A.evidence: Finite-sample analysis plus controlled matched-Post experiments and native benchmarks across 20 benchmark–learner cells spanning recurrent, in-context, gradient-based, and belief-style meta-RL agents.
MdKVJH3Y5A.claimed_gains: High-AdaptGain task groups improve Post by 0.0069 more than matched low-AdaptGain groups under equal retraining budgets, and PACE achieves the highest mean Post in 18 of 20 compatible benchmark–learner cells.
MdKVJH3Y5A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paired adaptive-versus-static intervention intuitive and well-motivated, with broad coverage across meta-RL learner families.
MdKVJH3Y5A.main_concern: Performance gains are modest relative to the extra rollout compute and numerous manually tuned hyperparameters, without matched environment-interaction budgets or statistical significance tests.

9Li4rfsUQm.one_liner: Scaffolds a frozen general-purpose VLM with mid-level action interfaces and an asynchronous monitoring-verification loop for zero-shot robot manipulation.
9Li4rfsUQm.problem: Vision-language-action models generalize poorly zero-shot and require specialized robot data, whereas general VLMs reason well about manipulation but cannot directly output continuous embodiment-specific control.
9Li4rfsUQm.method: MotorMind wraps a single frozen VLM in a manipulation harness that decomposes control into planning, mid-level action generation, memory, and an asynchronous monitoring and verification loop with continual refinement. The mid-level action interface translates VLM decisions into physical execution without task-specific policy training.
9Li4rfsUQm.key_idea: Uses a single frozen VLM inside an asynchronous closed-loop harness with mid-level action primitives, continual refinement, and execution verification for zero-shot manipulation.
9Li4rfsUQm.evidence: Evaluated zero-shot on LIBERO-PRO (base and perturbed settings) and a real xArm6 robot under direct manipulation and human perturbations, plus offline capability diagnostics and ablations.
