9Li4rfsUQm.claimed_gains: Achieves 66.7% base success and 53.8% success under perturbations on LIBERO-PRO (vs at most 13.3% and 19.2% for prior zero-shot methods), and 95% average success on a real xArm6 robot.
9Li4rfsUQm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that MotorMind achieves strong zero-shot and real-robot manipulation results without task-specific training and presents a coherent closed-loop decomposition.
9Li4rfsUQm.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient isolation of contributions relative to prior agentic harnesses (e.g., Harness VLA, CaP-X), under-specified low-level execution details, and an unclear link between low offline VLM diagnostic accuracy and high task success.

NMAQl4WMdo.one_liner: Demonstrates that KV-cache eviction budgets depend on how many distractor tokens outrank evidence rather than prompt length, and forecasts budgets via competitor counts.
NMAQl4WMdo.problem: KV-cache eviction methods set retention budgets as a fixed fraction of prompt length, which wastes memory on long low-competition prompts and fails when distractors are added at fixed length.
NMAQl4WMdo.method: The paper separates context length from distractor competition in controlled experiments and defines the required cache budget as the evidence tokens plus the tokens outranking them under a given scorer, along with rows binding evidence to the question. Pre-verification competitor counts are used to forecast per-request retention budgets and compact the cache.
NMAQl4WMdo.key_idea: Sizes KV-cache eviction budgets by counting competitor tokens that outrank evidence under the eviction scorer rather than scaling budgets proportionally to prompt length.
NMAQl4WMdo.evidence: Supported by controlled synthetic retrieval experiments up to 512K tokens (including Qwen3.5-9B at 32K) and LongBench analyses.
NMAQl4WMdo.claimed_gains: Fixed fractions keep about 100x more cache than needed on low-competition long prompts while distractors at fixed length raise required budgets more than 200-fold; frozen competitor counts forecast budgets within a factor of two up to 512K tokens and cut KV memory by up to two orders of magnitude with no accuracy loss on tested requests.
NMAQl4WMdo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating filler length from distractor count cleanly shows competition, not context length, drives required KV-cache budgets.
NMAQl4WMdo.main_concern: Reviewers note that computing competitor counts requires knowing the true evidence set (unavailable in realistic QA), that key findings rely on small synthetic retrieval sets (15-20 prompts), and that LongBench cells fall below the validity threshold.

wAeA6ZHZHp.one_liner: Trains an extractive RAG context compressor with fixed-evidence counterfactual query edits so it prunes topically relevant but constraint-violating evidence.
wAeA6ZHZHp.problem: Post-retrieval RAG context compressors rely on semantic relevance and retain text that remains topically relevant even when it violates answer-critical conditions such as temporal constraints.
wAeA6ZHZHp.method: The authors build fixed-evidence counterfactual diagnostic pairs by editing one answer-critical query condition while keeping the document and candidate evidence fixed, turning supporting evidence invalid. They train ConSieve, an extractive compressor supervised with these counterfactual pairs, to prune invalidated evidence under tight context budgets.
wAeA6ZHZHp.key_idea: Applies counterfactual query-edit supervision on fixed documents so an extractive RAG compressor learns to prune evidence invalidated by changed query constraints.
wAeA6ZHZHp.evidence: Evaluated on a predominantly temporal counterfactual diagnostic (StreamingQA/TimeQA), human-written SQuAD edits, matched counterfactual ablations, and end-to-end RAG QA under a 256-token cap.
wAeA6ZHZHp.claimed_gains: Prunes 87.2% of invalidated evidence (vs baselines retaining 55.3% to 72.1%), reduces invalid retention from 56.1% to 11.4% in a matched ablation, and reaches 0.631 QA F1 vs 0.608 for the strongest tested baseline at 256 tokens.
wAeA6ZHZHp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the fixed-evidence counterfactual diagnostic cleanly isolates constraint sensitivity and that the matched ablations and candid negative results are well executed.
wAeA6ZHZHp.main_concern: Reviewers note that gains do not generalize out of distribution (failing to improve on human-written SQuAD edits) and that in-domain fine-tuning or ordinary unanswerable-document training is not fully isolated from counterfactual supervision.

NRX54wELFM.one_liner: Co-trains an action-conditioned robot manipulation world model on real teleoperation episodes and large-scale simulated off-nominal trajectories.
NRX54wELFM.problem: Real-world robot datasets consist mostly of successful demonstrations from narrow camera viewpoints, leaving action-conditioned world models unable to predict suboptimal actions or generalize across viewpoints.
NRX54wELFM.method: MixWorld jointly trains an action-conditioned video world model (building on Ctrl-World) on roughly 95k real robot episodes and 550k simulated episodes containing off-nominal interactions such as retries, missed grasps, and diverse camera viewpoints, using LoRA, dynamics consistency loss, and asymmetric action dropout.
NRX54wELFM.key_idea: Co-trains an action-conditioned manipulation world model on ~95k real trajectories and ~550k diverse off-nominal simulated trajectories to ground realism while broadening action and viewpoint coverage.
NRX54wELFM.evidence: Evaluated on video prediction metrics, model-based evaluations, WorldArena, 510 human comparisons, and real-robot search experiments across three trajectory sets.
NRX54wELFM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that expanding world-model coverage to failures and off-nominal interactions via sim-and-real co-training is practically relevant and broadly evaluated.
NRX54wELFM.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the contribution of simulation data is confounded with additional continued training steps (lacking a compute-matched real-only continuation of Ctrl-World) and bundled hyperparameter/loss changes.

kbr6FlfOtA.one_liner: Uses generative models and manufactured solutions to synthesize verifiable PDE test problems and feedback for coding agents.
kbr6FlfOtA.problem: Evaluating PDE-solving coding agents on new problems requires expensive reference numerical solves, while fixed benchmarks restrict iterative exploration.
kbr6FlfOtA.method: The authors introduce Generator-Agent-Verifier (GAV), where a Generator learns a distribution of continuous reference solutions from simulation or experimental data and applies the method of manufactured solutions to work backward to matching PDE problems without running a solver. A Verifier scores the Agent's candidate programs on accuracy and cost and guides new problem generation toward weaknesses.
kbr6FlfOtA.key_idea: Sample continuous reference fields from a learned generative model and apply the method of manufactured solutions backward to produce exact-reference PDE tasks for coding agents.
kbr6FlfOtA.evidence: Theoretical analysis of evaluation reliability plus experiments with CodePDE, AutoNumerics, and PDE-SHARP on Navier-Stokes and Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck tasks.
kbr6FlfOtA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find combining generative modeling with the method of manufactured solutions an elegant way to supply cheap, verifiable PDE tasks that improve multiple agent frameworks.
kbr6FlfOtA.main_concern: Reviewers note that GAV-Full underperforms GAV (casting doubt on guided generation), improvements are evaluated mainly on GAV-generated tasks rather than external benchmarks, and physical consistency of manufactured forcing terms is unverified.

ENSNzYRyqX.one_liner: Fits a continuous neural implicit field over weight coordinates to synthesize parameters for expanded or modified transformer architectures.
ENSNzYRyqX.problem: Existing model-growth methods rely on discrete heuristics such as weight tiling or layer duplication, restricting expansion to rigid scaling patterns and direct copies.
ENSNzYRyqX.method: The authors propose WINR, which treats pretrained network weights as samples of a continuous function mapping structured geometric and semantic coordinates to parameter values. Fitting a neural implicit representation to one or more source checkpoints allows querying weights for target architectures with arbitrary fractional widths, depths, or layer compositions.
ENSNzYRyqX.key_idea: Fit a coordinate-based neural implicit field to pretrained checkpoints and query it at target architectural coordinates to synthesize weights for model growth.
ENSNzYRyqX.evidence: Experiments on BERT-style and decoder-only (MobileLLM) transformer model zoos covering intra-family and cross-architecture synthesis against random initialization, LEMON, and tiling-plus-noise.
ENSNzYRyqX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find formulating model growth as querying a continuous coordinate-to-weight implicit field conceptually interesting and flexible.
ENSNzYRyqX.main_concern: Reviewers flag weak cross-architecture generalization (likely due to neuron permutation symmetry), missing ablations isolating the neural field from tiling/corrections on MobileLLM, and omitted comparison to prior coordinate-to-weight work NeRN.

RHjzdouT4L.one_liner: Adds data-dependent expert-output orthogonality and shared-projection diversity regularizers to asymmetric LoRA Mixture-of-Experts.
RHjzdouT4L.problem: LoRA-based Mixture-of-Experts adapters suffer from correlated expert outputs, causing expert interference, overlapping representations, and weak specialization.
RHjzdouT4L.method: Building on an asymmetric LoRA MoE with shared low-rank projections, the authors add an explicit data-dependent orthogonality penalty on expert outputs to reduce functional redundancy and a complementary log-determinant diversity regularizer on the shared projections. They analyze both terms theoretically and evaluate across routing settings.
RHjzdouT4L.key_idea: Penalize pairwise correlation between active expert outputs on data activations while applying a diversity regularizer to the shared low-rank LoRA projection.
RHjzdouT4L.evidence: Theoretical analysis (Theorems 1-2) and fine-tuning experiments across multiple benchmarks, routing strategies, and HydraLoRA comparisons with ablations and training-cost measurements.
RHjzdouT4L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that regularizing expert outputs directly on activations is a simple, well-motivated approach to functional redundancy with consistent average gains over HydraLoRA.
RHjzdouT4L.main_concern: Reviewers point out gaps between theoretical assumptions and implementation (such as unnormalized shared projections and quadratic vs. cross-entropy objectives), modest empirical gains (0.25-0.52 points), and limited proof of true routing specialization.

Z5DVLWI7en.one_liner: Uses a meta-agent to monitor RL traces and hot-swap symbolic user-simulator, environment, reward, and hyperparameter edits during training.
Z5DVLWI7en.problem: Multi-turn user-centric agentic RL suffers from unreliable tools, flawed verifiers, and inconsistent user simulators that fixed-environment reward shaping cannot repair.
Z5DVLWI7en.method: The authors propose EAU, a meta-agent framework for environment-agent-user co-evolution over an editable symbolic representation of user and environment dynamics. During training, a meta-agent inspects trajectories, tool traces, and rewards, diagnoses failures, and hot-swaps validated modifications to the user simulator, environment, reward design, and RL settings, persisting improvements across runs.
Z5DVLWI7en.key_idea: Deploy a meta-agent over editable symbolic environment and user-simulator definitions to diagnose RL failures and hot-swap validated training-setup edits within and across runs.
Z5DVLWI7en.evidence: Evaluations across three interactive-agent benchmarks and two policy backbones comparing EAU against InfoPO, PPO, and closed-source baselines.
Z5DVLWI7en.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that repairing upstream simulator, tool, and verifier flaws during agentic RL is well motivated and practically impactful, yielding strong benchmark scores.
Z5DVLWI7en.main_concern: Reviewers question compute fairness and attribution because the meta-agent uses Claude Opus-5 with unreported overhead, allows up to five inter-run restarts, and compares against imported baseline numbers.

h7Sn9NpZgK.one_liner: Pairs an LLM peptide-redesign agent with physical evaluators and persistent rule memory to optimize bifunctional antimicrobial binders.
h7Sn9NpZgK.problem: Designing bifunctional peptides that both bind a protein target and kill bacteria involves conflicting trade-offs among binding affinity, antimicrobial potency, and hemolysis.
h7Sn9NpZgK.method: The authors present a self-evolving modular agent (JANUS-PEP) that starts from de novo binder backbones, diagnoses deficits across interface energetics, MIC prediction, and hemolysis prediction, proposes sequence edits with explicit pre-evaluation outcome predictions, and accumulates transferable design rules in persistent memory.
h7Sn9NpZgK.key_idea: Require an LLM peptide-redesign agent to commit to explicit outcome predictions before querying physical evaluators and store verified design rules in persistent memory.
h7Sn9NpZgK.evidence: Computational evaluations on author-constructed infection-scenario design benchmarks and ProtGym using in silico predictors for binding, antimicrobial activity, and hemolysis.
h7Sn9NpZgK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the multi-objective bifunctional peptide problem timely and appreciate the modular separation of planning, diagnosis, redesign, and external evaluation.
h7Sn9NpZgK.main_concern: Reviewers cite the absence of wet-lab experimental validation (relying solely on computational predictors), missing head-to-head baselines against other peptide/AMP agents, and incomplete SFT/GRPO/memory ablations.

SwZaWWmGkP.one_liner: Uses penultimate-to-final-layer token confidence changes for training-free weighted voting and online reasoning search.
SwZaWWmGkP.problem: Final-layer confidence in test-time scaling can misrank failed reasoning trajectories that remain overconfident while stuck in high-confidence reasoning stagnation.
SwZaWWmGkP.method: The authors define inter-layer confidence dynamics as the change in token confidence from the penultimate to the final transformer layer. They use this signal without additional training or verifiers to filter and weight sampled trajectories in post-hoc answer aggregation and to guide online reasoning search.
SwZaWWmGkP.key_idea: Score reasoning trajectories by the token-confidence shift between the penultimate and final layers to downweight stagnant high-confidence errors during aggregation and online search.
SwZaWWmGkP.evidence: Experiments on Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-8B, and Nemotron-3-Nano-4B across five reasoning benchmarks, coding tasks, sampling budgets, and length-filtered subsets.
SwZaWWmGkP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, clearly presented, training-free, and easy to plug into multi-sample voting setups.
SwZaWWmGkP.main_concern: Reviewers note marginal gains (about 1-2 points), limited originality relative to existing cross-layer logit/confidence methods, missing efficiency metrics and strong training-free baselines, and inability to work at N=1.

xX67RvHsV3.one_liner: Validates structural supports via feature counterfactuals and trains GNNs/HGNNs with paired restoration and class-transition losses.
xX67RvHsV3.problem: Graph and hypergraph neural networks have opaque decision processes and ambiguous local decision boundaries under class imbalance and inter-class similarity.
xX67RvHsV3.method: The authors propose a two-stage framework that first searches for structural supports driving a source state toward a restoration target and validates them via node-feature interventions to generate counterfactuals. Second, dual-target decision transition learning pairs each source with restoration and class-transition counterfactuals and jointly optimizes endpoint classification, margin, transition-magnitude, and local gradient-alignment losses.
xX67RvHsV3.key_idea: Generate validated structural-and-feature counterfactual pairs for restoration and class transitions, then use their source-target relationships as explicit margin and gradient-alignment training supervision.
xX67RvHsV3.evidence: Evaluations on two public datasets (including TEP and Paderborn) with graph and hypergraph neural networks, plus naive counterfactual augmentation comparisons and component ablations.
xX67RvHsV3.claimed_gains: On the TEP dataset, improves Macro-F1 to 91.89% and Balanced Accuracy to 90.74%.
xX67RvHsV3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate using counterfactual source-target transitions actively for decision-boundary training rather than solely for post-hoc explanation, and note strong gains on TEP.
xX67RvHsV3.main_concern: Reviewers argue that causal validation claims are overstated because cross-stage agreement is partly induced by optimization constraints, and note missing class-imbalance baselines and many unablated hyperparameters.

oHN5cGzMyT.one_liner: Applies radial band-stop image filtering to frozen VLMs and classifies paired answer transitions across five semantic labels.
oHN5cGzMyT.problem: How different spatial frequency bands in images affect answer correctness and semantic transitions in frozen vision-language models is poorly understood.
oHN5cGzMyT.method: The authors build a paired frequency-suppression analysis framework that generates eight independent radial band-stop variants per image while holding the question and frozen VLM fixed. They compare unfiltered and filtered answers using five semantic transition labels capturing preservation, degradation, and error correction, validated against human judgments.
oHN5cGzMyT.key_idea: Suppress eight radial spatial-frequency bands independently on fixed image-question pairs and categorize frozen VLM response shifts into five semantic preservation, degradation, and correction transitions.
oHN5cGzMyT.evidence: Evaluations across four visual tasks and five frozen VLMs from two families (including InternVL3 and Qwen2.5-VL), backed by human annotation checks and statistical tests.
oHN5cGzMyT.claimed_gains: Human validation yields 91.72% weighted response-level agreement between automatic semantic transition labels and human judgments.
oHN5cGzMyT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled paired experimental design and the fine-grained transition rubric that exposes simultaneous degradation and error correction hidden by aggregate accuracy.
oHN5cGzMyT.main_concern: Reviewers question equal-width radial bands given natural image 1/rho^2 power decay, note the gap between behavioral transition logging and mechanistic explanation, and flag a discrepancy between paper text and code on response counts.

VpuKV5m9ud.one_liner: Filters latent-neighborhood credit-assignment references by matching both action and observed successor transition without extra rollouts.
VpuKV5m9ud.problem: Hidden-state-based credit assignment in agentic RL pools returns across steps with similar latent states and actions even when they produce different observed transitions.
VpuKV5m9ud.method: The authors introduce CAST, which forms candidate neighborhoods via policy hidden-state similarity and selects only reference steps matching the target step in both action and observed transition, while keeping other-action records for local comparison. Step-level credit is estimated directly from these filtered records without additional environment rollouts or a learned value model.
VpuKV5m9ud.key_idea: Restrict latent-neighborhood return pooling in agentic RL to reference steps that match both the target action and its observed successor transition.
VpuKV5m9ud.evidence: Experiments with Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-9B, and Llama across four interactive environments (including ALFWorld and ScienceWorld) and 11 general capability benchmarks against GiGPO and BiPACE.
VpuKV5m9ud.claimed_gains: Outperforms GiGPO and BiPACE in all eight Qwen settings with success rate gains of up to 8.9 and 22.0 percentage points, respectively, while retaining general capability performance.
VpuKV5m9ud.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and the transition-aware filtering modification is simple, low-cost, and consistently beats GiGPO and BiPACE across tested settings.
VpuKV5m9ud.main_concern: Reviewers note weak isolation of successor-observation matching (removing it barely changes ScienceWorld and random count-matched filtering recovers most ALFWorld gains), lack of multi-seed variance, and reliance on exact string matching.

9YPSFXHfMt.one_liner: Applies training-free, cardinality-aware query scaling to counteract softmax attention-mass dilution in long-context speculative decoding.
9YPSFXHfMt.problem: Speculative decoding speedups degrade on long contexts as growing key counts dilute softmax attention mass and lower draft token acceptance.
9YPSFXHfMt.method: SharpDraft derives an exact top-k attention-mass correction under explicit assumptions and deploys a closed-form, fixed-slope cardinality-aware query scaling factor in the draft model without retraining, extra parameters, or KV-cache edits.
9YPSFXHfMt.key_idea: Scale draft-model attention queries as a closed-form function of visible key cardinality to offset long-context softmax attention-mass dilution without training.
9YPSFXHfMt.evidence: Evaluated on AIME-26, GPQA-Diamond, and LongGenBench Diary across DFlash, PARD, and EAGLE 3.1 drafters, compared against target-only decoding and online adaptation.
9YPSFXHfMt.claimed_gains: Achieves 2.59-3.19x geometric-mean end-to-end speedups over target-only autoregressive decoding across AIME-26, GPQA-Diamond, and LongGenBench Diary without increasing peak GPU memory.
9YPSFXHfMt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that SharpDraft has negligible memory and compute overhead, requires no training, and transfers across multiple speculative drafter families.
9YPSFXHfMt.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty over Scalable-Softmax and log-N scaling, modest gains over fixed scaling, and missing baselines using sliding-window attention or long-context-trained drafters.
